News.title: New £20k reward in hunt for killer of Royal Engineer, 64, found dead in woodland after his dog returned home without him
News.content:
MURDER' MANHUNT New £20k reward in hunt for killer of Royal Engineer, 64, found dead in woodland after his dog returned home without him







Next

A NEW £20k reward has been offered amid the hunt for the killer of a Royal Engineer who was found dead in woodland after his dog came home without him.

Graham Pennycook, 64, set off with his dog on a route he knew well near a polo field close to Perham Down, Wiltshire, on September 24.



Police believe Graham had been assaulted while he was out with his dog.

The pup later returned home alone before Graham’s body was found in the woods.



A murder investigation was launched, with cops carrying out extensive searches and forensic enquiries at the scene.

Investigators have previously issued an appeal for information amid the hunt for Graham’s killer.



Anyone who saw two men behaving suspiciously in the area was asked to come forward.

The force remains keen to hear from witnesses who were near the woods between 9am and 6pm on the day Graham was killed.

Cops also want to hear from anyone who saw vehicles being driven erratically or parked in unusual places.

Officers say Graham was around 45 minutes into his walk when he was attacked.



The route taken by Graham is said to be popular among dog walkers, cyclists and people exercising.

Anyone who was in the area that day has been urged to contact Wiltshire Police.

Crimestoppers is now offering a £20,000 reward for information as the investigation continues.

Beth Simpson, Crimestoppers Regional Manager Central South West, said: “Graham went out for a familiar walk and never came home.

“His family are left without him and without answers.



“If you know something about what happened but do not want to speak to the police, you can share with Crimestoppers anonymously.

“Even a detail you think is small could help.”

Detective Chief Inspector Phil Walker said: “We believe Graham had been walking with his dog on a familiar route to him, for approximately 40 to 45 minutes before he was attacked.

“We’d encourage anyone who may have seen anything or anyone suspicious in the area near to the polo ground at Perham Down on the morning of September 24 to get in touch with Crimestoppers.”

News.title: Macron has ‘secret bunker hideout’ if French rioters storm presidential HQ – as protesters continue to clash with cops
News.content:
FRENCH FORTRESS Macron has ‘secret bunker hideout’ if French rioters storm presidential HQ – as protesters continue to clash with cops







Next

EMMANUEL Macron has a secret bunker outside Paris where he will flee if violent mobs storm the Élysée Palace, a book has claimed.

The revelation comes as apocalyptic riots wreak havoc across France, with masked protesters looting shops, setting fires and clashing with armed police.



Macron’s hideout in the capital’s suburbs was revealed in La Nouvelle Armée des Ombres (The New Army of Shadows), a book by investigative journalists Pierre Gastineau, Antoine Izambard and Franck Renaud.

They say that the bunker preparations were partly sparked by the 2018 Yellow Vest uprising, when the French president was attacked during a visit to Le Puy-en-Velay.



“The government trembled” amid the unrest, one author told France Inter on Friday.

Macron’s spooks began plotting presidential evacuation plans and invoked the violent riots which brought down the government in 1934, according to extracts published in L’Express.

Officials fear that radical left-wing militants could spark a “third round” of disorder should Marine Le Pen‘s National Rally win the election next April, according to the authors.

Paris police chief Patrice Faure has held several meetings to prepare for a rebellion, various high-level sources told the authors.



Meanwhile, France’s foreign intelligence agency has simulated electoral interference, while police in the French capital have rehearsed for an entire day without smartphones in the event of a crippling cyber attack.

One senior spy warned that France was on the brink of an insurrection as early as April, pointing to rising fuel costs and simmering public fury.

However intelligence chiefs badly underestimated the chaos that would unfold on October 17, predicting only between 60,000 and 150,000 protesters, when in fact half a million took the streets.



France continues to deal with aftershocks from that uprising, with more than 600,000 people turning out nationwide on Thursday.

The Eiffel Tower was locked down as chaos erupted across the country and 80,000 protesters marched through Paris’ historic boulevards.

The iconic monument shuttered its gates as the capital braced for the pre-planned, nationwide strikes led by the Left-wing CGT and backed by fiery student groups.

Massive blazes lit up the streets of the capital as angry students carrying banners reading “inequalities seriously jeopardise our future” marched alongside striking workers and pensioners.

Major marches were also seen in in Lyon and Marseilles where special forces squads were also deployed in precaution although much of the action was peaceful.



France mobilised 70,000 cops as activists planned to bring the country to a standstill.

Police vowed an “extremely firm response” towards any “outbreaks” for the more than 250 protests which were planned for the day.

About a third a France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate on as some students set up blockades and teachers went on strike.



Earlier in the day, hooded and masked thugs set Françoise high school in Tournefeuille alight after they let off fireworks at the premise.

The school was locked down after the horrific blaze which witnesses described as an act of “guerrilla warfare”.

A teacher at the school told local media outlet La Dépêche: “They came to destroy everything.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“What unfolded this morning was in no way a blockade, nor even a student protest.

“These were not students who had come to voice their demands – they were individuals who had come to terrorize, ransack, and set fires. And they succeeded.”

News.title: Trump’s post-midterms purge begins as he ousts Susie Wiles & installs Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
News.content:
Next

PRESIDENT Donald Trump has announced his longtime adviser, Stephen Miller, will become his new White House chief of staff as his post-midterms shake-up begins.

Miller, one of the architects of Trump’s hardline immigration policies, will replace Susie Wiles, who is moving to a new role in the president’s political operation.



The surprise announcement came on Friday afternoon in a post on Trump’s Truth Social platform, just three days after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress.

“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” Trump wrote.



This comes just days after Republicans suffered a crushing election defeat, with Democrats seizing control of the House and Senate for Trump’s final two years in office.

Trump spoke to reporters outside the White House on Friday afternoon, saying he “wanted to make a change.”



“Susie’s done a great job,” he said. “We gotta make moves. Sometimes in life you gotta make moves.”

Trump said he wants Miller to “just run things well,” adding, “He’ll do a great job. Great manager.”

The president praised Wiles, who has served as his chief of staff since he returned to the White House in January 2025, in his post on Truth Social.

“Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation,” he said.



“I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff — She has done a great job!”

Wiles submitted her resignation on Thursday night, and Trump was apparently angry with her this week following the Republican wipeout, CNN’s Kaitlan Collins reported.

Wiles confirmed her departure in a statement on Friday, describing her time in the White House as the “honor of a lifetime.”

“Today is my last day as White House Chief of Staff,” she said.



“I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.”

Her departure comes over a month after Wiles announced she was cancer-free, six months after her shocking diagnosis.

It also follows the announcement that Wiles would take on a new gig as the co-chair of a new White House task force on women’s health, working alongside First Lady Melania Trump.

The shake-up marks one of the biggest personnel changes of Trump’s second term and comes as his administration reels from Tuesday’s midterm disaster.



There have been several shakeups in Trump’s cabinet in recent months, with DHS boss Kristi Noem and Attorney General Pam Bondi being shown the door, while Tulsi Gabbard resigned from her position as director of national intelligence.

With the midterms upset, speculation has risen about whether Trump would oust his top people, such as War Secretary Pete Hegseth, who experts told The U.S. Sun could be out in a matter of weeks as the White House pinned the election losses on the Iran war.

Trump, however, has shut down the speculation, telling reporters, “I think he’s doing a very good job.”

Miller, 41, has been one of Trump’s closest advisers for years and a driving force behind his sweeping immigration crackdown.



He has been the driving force behind Trump’s mass deportation agenda, helping shape the administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement operations.

But his handling of two fatal shootings involving federal immigration agents in Minnesota earlier this year sparked fierce criticism.

Renee Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, was shot dead by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Minneapolis on January 7.

Just 17 days later, Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse at a Veterans Affairs hospital, was killed by Border Patrol agents in the same city.



Following Pretti’s death, Miller branded him a “domestic terrorist” and a “would-be assassin” without providing evidence to support the accusations.

“A would-be assassin tried to murder federal law enforcement and the official Democrat account sides with the terrorists,” Miller wrote on X in January.

The remarks drew backlash after videos of the shooting contradicted key parts of the administration’s initial account.

Days later, Miller acknowledged that officials were examining whether agents had failed to follow White House instructions during the operation.

The shootings also contributed to the political turmoil surrounding Noem, who was Homeland Security secretary at the time before she was removed from her position in March.



The president had also removed Kimberly Guilfoyle, his former daughter-in-law-to-be, from her position as US ambassador to Greece in October.

Guilfoyle, who was previously engaged to Donald Trump Jr., was asked to resign following reports alleging she sought financial favors and offered access to administration officials.

The personnel changes followed the departure of former White House press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who announced in August that she was stepping down to spend more time with her young children.

Leavitt, one of Trump’s most prominent public defenders, moved into an outside political advisory role after leaving the White House and took on a gig as an on-air contributor for Fox News.

Her successor, Katie Zacharia, lasted just days on the job in October before her own abrupt exit.



Wiles herself was accused of playing a role in Zacharia’s dramatic firing last month.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Senior administration officials claimed the chief of staff had helped engineer a brutal Fox News grilling that sealed Zacharia’s fate.

“Susie gave Fox News the kill order, but Zacharia was an obviously bad choice. This was totally predictable,” one official told the Daily Mail at the time.

News.title: Brit submarine armed with two nuclear missiles on course to set world record for longest patrol at sea after 208 days
News.content:
Next

A BRITISH nuclear submarine is on course to set a new world record for the longest continuous patrol at sea after almost seven months beneath the waves.

The Royal Navy’s HMS Vengeance set sail on 12 April armed with Trident 2 nuclear missiles.



She is expected home within days after at least 208 days away.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham – who has been in office for 110 days – is expected to greet the submarine as it sails towards HMNB Clyde at Faslane.



It is the first nuclear patrol to return on his watch.

The previous known record was 205 days set by HMS Vanguard earlier this year.



During the patrols the 140-strong crew are almost totally cut off from their loved ones.

They are banned from broadcast messages home fear of revealing their location.



They receive a single text message a week, known as a family-gram, which has to be censored by the captain to avoid bad news reaching crew members which hinder them doing their jobs.

The subs were designed to sail for a maximum if 80 days due to the toll on the crew.

All the patrols for the last three years have been over six months long, due to shortage of working submarines.

Conditions are so extreme on board the 150m long vessels that NASA has studied the crews to understand how astronauts might cope on a mission to Mars.

It is the MoD’s top priority to ensure one is always at sea to provide the UK’s nuclear deterrent.



But only two of the four have been sea worthy since around 2023.

All four Vanguard class submarines were due to retire two years ago.

But their service has been extended because the Dreadnaught-class due to replace them are over a decade late.

They aren’t expected to enter service until at least the 2030s.

Former Chief of Defence Staff staff Admiral Sir Tony Radakin lashed out governments when he retired last year over their empty promises to resource the deterrent.



He said: “There is something wrong when successive governments profess the nuclear continuously at sea deterrent is our highest priority, but our sailors are having to put to sea for extraordinarily long patrols in some of the most complex machines in the planet that are beyond their original design life.”

When HMS Vanguard returned from patrol in March 2024 four of her crew had babies waiting to meet them.

Last month the senior service was able to sail three Vanguard class subs simultaneously for the first time in several years because HMS Vigiliant came out of repairs.

HMS Vengeance was on patrol, HMS Vanguard was on work-up preparing to take over, and HMS Vigilant was on sea trials of the west coast of Scotland.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The fourth boat HMS Victorious is in a years-long life extension programme at HMNB Devonport, in Plymouth.



The Navy does not comment on submarine operations.

News.title: Fury as Ed Miliband ‘has whale of a time’ snorkelling in Caribbean ‘while millions of Brits struggle to make ends meet’
News.content:
Next

ED Miliband went for a snorkel in the Caribbean surf — while Brits struggled to keep afloat in the cost of living crisis.

The Foreign Secretary and Net Zero zealot broke away from the Commonwealth summit in Antigua to go for a restaurant lunch followed by an afternoon dip with aides.



He was seen emerging from beachside changing rooms barefooted and clutching his towel and wet trunks.

Meanwhile back home, inflation-hit families were treading water as they came to terms with interest rates rising for the first time in three years and energy set to soar in January.



The ex-Labour leader and former Energy Secretary was spotted enjoying lunch at the swanky Catherine’s Cafe, which is a popular stop-off for guests arriving in superyachts.

He then strolled out onto the white sands of Pigeon Point beach.

A British tourist said: “No one at the restaurant or on the beach had any idea who Ed Miliband was.

“After lunch they walked down to the beach and were met by people carrying snorkels and masks. They all got changed into their swimming trunks to go out to snorkel.



“They were in the sea for over an hour while the security staff waited on the beach, which was mostly empty.

“Then Miliband walked back to the restaurant toilets to change. They were all talking about how clear the water was and how amazing it was.”

Tory chairman Kevin Hollinrake said: “While millions of hard-working Brits are struggling to make ends meet because of Labour’s decisions, Ed Miliband is living it up on the beach in Antigua.”

He added: “Ed Miliband may be having a whale of a time in Antigua, but British taxpayers are paying the price for his net zero zealotry — with energy bills continuing to rise. Under Labour, British families are drowning in a cost-of-living crisis.”



Before joining Andy Burnham in Antigua for the Commonwealth meeting, Mr Miliband had accompanied the King in the Bahamas and Guyana.

The PM’s trip started with a row when it emerged that his taxpayer-funded plane had diverted from London to Manchester to pick him up and his wife Marie-France van Heel.

It sparked accusations he was treating the government-owned jet like an “Uber service”.

The Labour boss was then left red-faced after falling over while playing cricket, before causing a further stir by awkwardly playing the steel drums with Mr Miliband.





And FCDO spokesperson said: “At the end of a visit to the Antigua & Barbuda Ocean’s Trust, the Foreign Secretary went swimming nearby at no cost to the taxpayer.”

News.title: Russell Brand’s dad ‘hired him prostitutes’ and ‘allowed him to watch porn as a child’ sparking star’s sick obsession
News.content:
DISTURBING PAST Russell Brand’s dad ‘hired him prostitutes’ and ‘allowed him to watch porn as a child’ sparking star’s sick obsession







Next

RUSSELL Brand’s “voracious” sexual appetites emerged after his dad introduced him to porn while he was at primary school, he wrote in his book.

The disgraced comedian, 51, revealed in his first autobiography how his father Ron gave him access to porno mags and X-rated videos as a boy.



Brand also recalled how his dad would bring women back to his flat and leave him to his own devices while he had sex.

In another account, Brand described a bizarre encounter during a family holiday at British resort Pontins when he found his dad in bed with another woman’s mum.



He said a girl had invited him into their chalet because her mother was in bed with his father.

Brand wrote in the book: “A woman leaped up naked, all knockers and skin everywhere.



“I pressed record on the old brain box.”

He also wrote about the time Ron hired three prostitutes while on holiday to Hong Kong, two for himself and one for Brand, then 17.

The comedian recalled how his dad began “unwrapping his two prostitutes” while he tried to have sex with the woman hired for him.

But he claimed the “bedlam” from his dad’s bed proved distracting, recalling cries of: “Yeah come on! Phwoaar you’re juicy!”

Writing about the encounter years later, Brand described how his sexuality had changed following the experience.



He said: “During the rest of that holiday I f****d loads more prostitutes and never wore a condom… my sexuality had morphed forever from bewildered innocence into something more complex and rapacious.”

The revelations come after Brand was found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults following a trial at Southwark Crown Court.

The 51-year-old faces a “significant” prison term after jurors deliberated for eight and a half hours before reaching their verdicts.



He was convicted of raping a 21-year-old woman at his Hampstead home in 2009 and sexually assaulting a Channel 4 worker who had been forced to give him a massage.

Brand was cleared of raping another woman he met at a cabaret show in 1999 and attempting to indecently assault an MTV worker in 2001.

Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC said he had a “childlike” expectation that his every desire should be met and only cared about his “birthright to orgasm”.



Brand was born in Grays, Essex, and his parents split when he was just six months old.

He was raised by his mum Barbara, whom he adored and became particularly close to after she suffered three bouts of cancer during his childhood.

Brand wrote how he was heavily influenced by his charismatic father Ron, whom he idolised.

In his autobiography, Brand recalled how his dad would leave him to amuse himself in his flat while he “diddled” a woman he had brought home.



He also described developing an early fascination with women’s bodies.

Even while at primary school, he claimed he would try to guess the cup sizes of women he encountered.

In another passage, he recalled attempting to watch his Auntie Josie, a friend of his mother’s, washing her “glorious breasts” in the bath.

He wrote: “That’s it, I thought. Keep washing, after all I’m only a little boy… I really was quite manipulative, even at that early age.”



The court heard that Brand’s offending against women took place between 1999 and 2009, as his public profile was taking off through television appearances and Hollywood films.

Brand's verdicts in full Count 1

Brand was charged with raping a woman in her hotel room after meeting her at cabaret show he was performing in on the fringes of the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999.

He was found not guilty of rape. Count 2

He was accused of trying to drag an MTV worker into a toilet at her London offices in 2001

He was found not guilty of attempted indecent assault. Count 3

Brand was accused of grabbing the breasts of an MTV worker he met at a friend’s party at Nordic Bar in London’s Soho in 2004 within seconds of meeting her.

He was found guilty of sexual assault. Count 4

He was accused of dragging the same MTV worker he groped at the bar into the toilets and orally raping her.

He was found not guilty of rape. Count 5

Brand was accused of kissing and groping a Choice FM radio worker in around 2004 or 2005 in front of his entourage.

He was found guilty of sexual assault. Count 6

He was charged with raping a fan at his London home after they met when he invited her backstage after one of his gigs at the Hammersmith Apollo in February 2009.

He was found guilty of rape. Count 7

He was charged with sexually assaulting a Channel 4 staffer by shoving his face in her groin when his entourage allegedly asked her to give him a massage in 2009.

He was found guilty of sexual assault.

One of the women Brand raped told the court he made her feel like a “piece of meat”.

She had met him after attending his stand-up show at the Hammersmith Apollo in 2009 before being invited backstage.

The woman went to his home a few days later, where Brand allegedly told her: “Your hair smells funny” before making her shower and wash it while he watched.

She said they initially had consensual sex, but that Brand then raped her.



Another victim, who worked at a radio station in the mid-2000s, described his alleged assault as “violent”, “sloppy” and “frenzied”.

A Channel 4 worker also told jurors she had been made to give Brand a massage after being told he was unhappy.

Brand denied the charges and claimed his promiscuous past had been twisted into allegations of criminal behaviour.

Giving evidence, he admitted being “persuasive, seductive, begging and flirting” with women but insisted consent was “non-negotiable”.

He also told the court he had been wrong to use his fame for sex but denied ever forcing himself on a woman.



His wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he shares three children, supported him throughout the trial and gave evidence on his behalf.

She described him as an “amazingly attentive husband” and a “kind and a wonderful father”.

Brand displayed little emotion as the guilty verdicts were delivered, telling his wife “I love you” before being taken into custody.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Met Police launched its investigation in September 2023 following allegations aired in a Sunday Times and Channel 4 Dispatches investigation.

He will be sentenced on Monday.

News.title: Horror moment worker engulfed by flames after touching live power line with pole sparking fireball explosion
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horrifying moment man is engulfed by flames after touching a high-voltage power line, sparking a massive blast.

Harrowing footage shows the worker being swallowed by a fireball, before flailing on the ground until bystanders rush to extinguish the blaze.



The scenes unfolded after the worker touched an overhead power line with a long pole in Kaifeng City, in China.

All seemed to be going well, until he took his eyes off the job to chat with a man next to him.



Moments later fierce flames, blue sparks and smoke suddenly exploded around the man.

As the smoke cleared, the man can be seen struggling on the ground as small flames continue around him.

Workers from a nearby car shop rushed over and doused him with a fire extinguisher to put out the flames, local reports say.

Shopkeepers nearby reportedly heard three booming explosions, likening them to the sound of fireworks.

Eyewitnesses also reported seeing smoke from their doorways as the blaze took hold of the man’s clothes.

Miraculously the man survived the horrifying ordeal and was rushed to hospital with severe burns.



The Kaifeng Power Supply Company is said to have carried out an investigation of the scene the day after the incident and found no safety hazards.

The horror blaze follows another terrifying incident, where a car exploded into a fireball and swallowed a firefighter in a wall of flames in Indiana.

The emergency worker was sent flying into the air as the blast ripped through the SUV in Avon.

Shocking footage shows the vehicle suddenly erupting into a surging ball of fire – with the firefighter stood just a few feet behind.

Fellow firefighters raced to the aid of their fallen comrade – who miraculously survived the terrifying incident on November 2.



In a similar freak instance just weeks before, two cops were engulfed in flames after another car erupted on a busy motorway in California.

Dramatic footage captured the moment the roaring inferno swallowed the unsuspecting officers, who were hospitalised with burns following the explosion.

Thick plumes of smoke billowed into the air after the blast, which erupted just as highway patrol officers were tending to a broken-down car on California’s Interstate 215.

Police suspect the driver of the Toyota Camry was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pair of cops were speaking with the suspected drunk driver near the unoccupied vehicle when it suddenly burst into flames.



Both driver and his passenger escaped unscathed and the burned cops were rushed to hospital and were expected to fully recover.

News.title: Harrowing emergency call reveals chilling screams after mum, 58, mauled by alligator in front of horrified family
News.content:
Next

A HARROWING emergency call filled with horrifying screams has revealed the moments after a mum mauled by an alligator.

Dina Spann, 58, suffered severe injuries to her right arm and left hand during a family boating trip in Florida’s Marion County on August 8.



The savage “full speed” attack left her arm “dangling off” in front of her horrified family.

A woman can be heard yelling: “Somebody got bit by an alligator, I think her got bit – it’s dangling off,” in one of two distressing 911 calls obtained by the New York Post.



“She lost half an arm,” the woman can be heard saying.

During the harrowing ordeal, other bystanders try to get Dina back onto the boat.



The operator then asks if the arm was amputated, to which the call replies: “I think so.”

In the second call, a man tells the operator that they are on the Silver River while a woman can be heard crying in the background.



He then adds: “Her arm is gone.”

Dina’s son Zach Guerrina, 38, previously told the Post how his mum’s arm was left “hanging by a thread”.

He said his mother bravely fought back with her bare hands and lost part of her left ring finger before the alligator clamped down on her right arm.

He said: “She wasn’t just letting it happen.

“She was trying to hold its mouth shut, swimming to the top to get a breath of fresh air and keep it from biting her legs.



“It had her but she said she was trying to make sure it didn’t get to her legs.”

A 9ft 8in alligator was removed from the river by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) the day after the attack.

Zach, a dad-of-five who works as a carpenter, had left his mum floating in the river with two teenage relatives and his brother’s girlfriend moments before the attack.

John Gamache was eating lunch with his father on their boat near the scene when they heard the events unfold.

Gamache told Fox affiliate WOFL that he spotted the alligator approaching the group in the clear spring water.



“I looked just upriver from us a couple hundred feet and saw an alligator head way above the water and going full speed towards the swimmers,” he recalled.

By the time Gamache was able to reach Dina, the alligator had let go of her, and the sound of his boat had the reptile fleeing.

Gamache found the woman clinging to a paddleboard as several nearby swimmers appeared in distress.

“I noticed just a cloud of blood, and four or five swimmers panic,” he said.

“It did pull her under for awhile, and looking at the extent of her injury, there was a lot of action going on underwater.”



He rushed to help her after seeing the state of her injuries and used a rope to make a tourniquet on her bleeding and mangled arm.

“It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere,” he said.

“Obviously, the minutes mattered.”

Gamache and his father helped bring the other swimmers and children onto their boat before speeding off to a nearby boat launch.

First responders then rushed the woman to the hospital, and on Sunday, her family confirmed to WOFL that she was discharged.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dina revealed the extent of her injuries in a video posted to Facebook in September, showing her right arm amputated below the elbow and left ring finger missing.

She wrote: “The gator got a piece of me. It didn’t get the best of me.”

News.title: Brand's barrister refers himself to regulator after report he confronted journalist
News.content:
Russell Brand's defence barrister has referred himself to the regulator after reports that he confronted a Sunday Times journalist who was involved in a media investigation into Brand in 2023.

In a Times and Sunday Times podcast on Thursday, Rosamund Urwin said she introduced herself to Ian Winter KC outside court after verdicts were delivered.

She claimed he responded with a "snarl" and said "I hope you're pleased with yourself".

"Apparently I said, but I can't actually remember this but I've read it in reporting, 'I am pleased that justice has been done'", Urwin said.

She said that Winter replied "it wasn't" and suggested she was to blame using a profanity.

In a statement, Winter said the "ways matters have been characterised" in the media meant they should be "subject to proper scrutiny".

On Friday, Winter said he considered his professional duty required him to self-report the allegations to the Bar Standards Board.

The Bar Standards Board regulates barristers in England and Wales in the public interest.

In a statement, Winter said: "Having seen the ways matters have been characterised in today's press I consider my professional duty requires me to self-report those allegations to the Bar Standards Board, so the matter can be subject to proper scrutiny. I have made such a report."

Four women variously accused Brand of rape, sexual assaults and emotional abuse in a joint investigation by Channel 4 Dispatches and the Times and Sunday Times in September 2023.

The actor and comedian denied the allegations.

News.title: How 2000s lad culture helped Russell Brand to hide in plain sight
News.content:
Warning: This article contains graphic descriptions of sexual acts

No British celebrity navigated the cultural changes of the early 21st Century better than Russell Brand.

His life has been one long personal rebrand.

He morphed from provocative stand-up comic to TV star and Hollywood actor. He became a YouTuber and political activist, taking up left-wing causes around issues of inequality in the 2010s, then Covid conspiracies and in 2024 supporting Donald Trump for president. That same year he was baptised as a Christian in London's River Thames.

Now he has a new persona to try on: convicted rapist.

On Thursday, the disgraced comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court, following a three-week trial.

As he faces jail, it's clear that the behaviour that formed the backdrop to Brand's prosecution is the same behaviour that helped elevate him in the first place.

News.title: Trump replaces White House chief of staff days after Republicans suffer midterm defeats
News.content:
One of Trump's closest aides, Miller stuck by the president following his 2020 election defeat and followed Trump back into power last year.

Wiles gave her resignation to Trump on Thursday night, a US official told CBS News, the BBC's media partner. Three sources told CBS she quit because of the election losses.

Trump said in a statement that Wiles would be moved to the "Trump Political Operation". He told reporters that Miller "gets it, very good politically".

Wiles said being on Trump's team was "the honor of a lifetime".

"I'm so proud to have been a part of what we've accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First," she said. "While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will."

It was unclear if her deputies would remain at the White House.

Wiles, 69, is seen as among the most powerful figures in the Trump administration and someone particularly close to the US president.

Asked last month whether Wiles could be replaced soon, Trump said there was "zero chance".

"Susie is here and she's gonna be here for a long time," he said.

Wiles recently battled cancer, announcing in September, six months after her diagnosis, that she was in remission.

News.title: Harry and five others seek to challenge Mail publisher privacy ruling
News.content:
The Duke of Sussex and five other high-profile figures who lost a privacy case against the publisher of the Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday are seeking to challenge the High Court ruling.

Prince Harry, singer Sir Elton John and actress Elizabeth Hurley were among the group facing paying joint legal costs of up to Â£34.5m after the court ruled in July they had failed to prove the allegations of unlawful information gathering.

Associated Newspapers Limited strongly denied the claims, which were heard at an 11-week trial in London that ended with judge Mr Justice Nicklin dismissing all the allegations.

At the time, a spokesperson for the publisher described the judgement as an "overwhelming victory for the Daily Mail and its journalists".

The prince testified in person during the civil hearing and claimed the details that appeared in 14 articles about him "plainly" proved journalists were listening in to phone calls - but a High Court judge said he had failed to prove that.

On Friday, a spokesperson for Prince Harry, Hurley, Sir Elton, his husband David Furnish, actress Sadie Frost and political campaigner Baroness Lawrence said the claimants had filed applications with the Court of Appeal applying for permission to challenge the judgements.

The statement said the planned appeal was both on Mr Justice Nicklin's dismissal of their claims and a subsequent indemnity costs order.

The spokesperson said: "The claimants respectfully disagree with those unprecedented decisions, which they consider to be legally and factually flawed."

In August, a month on from his judgement, Mr Justice Nicklin ruled that the case was a rare one in which the claimants should have to pay far in excess of the costs that had been agreed before the trial.

He also ordered at that time the claimants should make an initial payment of Â£9.54m while the final total was calculated.

The statement from the group's joint spokesperson did not make any reference to Liberal Democrat politician Sir Simon Hughes who was part of the action. The BBC has contacted Sir Simon to establish whether he is joining the appeal.

After the costs ruling, he told the BBC he was "disappointed" and would take "the time necessary to consider both the substantive and the costs judgment and whether to pursue appeals against decisions in either judgment or both".

The trial saw many current and former Mail and Mail on Sunday journalists and executives giving evidence denying accusations of illegal activity that was put to them by lawyers representing the prince and his fellow claimants.

Lawyers for the publisher said in court that the journalists had provided a "compelling account of a pattern of legitimate sourcing of articles", including using information provided by friends and "leaky" social circles surrounding those they had written about.

In a civil case such as this, the legal convention is that the losing party must reimburse "reasonable" legal fees incurred by the other side. They also have to settle their own legal costs.

News.title: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
News.content:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk has said production of the firm's Cybertruck is "winding down" in Texas, to focus on its self-driving Cybercab cars.

The model is only produced at Tesla's Austin base, and he did not clarify if manufacturing would be moved elsewhere or simply cease.

The Cybertruck has received a mixed response since its launch in 2023, with some praising its individuality and others simply labelling it ugly.

It has also suffered from disappointing sales, quality problems and recalls.

BBC technology reporter Shiona McCallum has this report.

More on this story.

News.title: Manhunt after boy injured by sword, sparking Gloucester school lockdowns
News.content:
Police described both suspects as white males. One is aged in his late teens to early 20s, of a medium to large build, and about 6ft tall. He was wearing white sliders at the time of the incident.

The other suspect is described as being about 5ft 5ins tall, of slim build and wearing black clothing.

St Peter's High School pupil Jimmy said the situation was "really scary" and he was still in shock.

After getting into the Tuffley school for the day, he said his friends came in and told him something had happened near his home.

He said the school's alarm then went off and the computer he was on displayed a message saying "This is a lockdown".

"The computers are not accessible at all and we've all had to turn the lights off, lock the doors, turn all the blinds down, and we've had to get on the ground," he said.

"At the time I was scared. My heart was racing," he added.

Jimmy said pupils were locked in their classrooms for two to three hours.

"[When police cars arrived] I thought this is getting serious, I'm getting worried, I don't know what's going on," he said.

The 15-year-old said he was able to message his mother when the school let students use their phones after about an hour.

"When I was able to eventually get out, she was giving me a bunch of hugs," he said.

"What I am is shocked. I'm surprised that this happened," he added.

Jimmy said the school had previously run lockdown drills but a real event had never happened before.

News.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
News.content:
European Union prosecutors have begun investigating the possible misuse of EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people last week.

Prosecutors backed by a special unit of Spain's Guardia Civil security force said they were conducting the inquiry at the offices of Adif rail infrastructure authority and rail safety agency AESF.

The 28 October accident on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line was one of the worst railway disasters in Europe this century.

It is the second EU fraud inquiry opened into Spain's railways this year, after 46 people were killed on the same line at Adamuz in January.

Last week, a train operated by state-owned operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo outside the village of Urda, around 130km (80 miles) south of Madrid.

The LZB communication system that monitors the position of trains had gone down, and the Renfe train had been given the all clear to start running at normal speed, even though the Iryo train ahead of it had been unable to restart.

The two accidents nine months apart on the same line have claimed 115 lives and dozens more injuries.

News.title: Huntingdon train attack victim thought 'this is what it feels like to die', court told
News.content:
A passenger stabbed multiple times by a knifeman accused of trying to kill 10 people on a train has told jurors he thought "this is what it feels like to die".

Scott Bletcher was on the York to London King's Cross LNER service on 1 November last year when the attacks happened, leading to an unscheduled stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire.

On Friday, Cambridge Crown Court also heard from staff member Samir Zitouni, who said he fought back using a frying pan, stating he did not want to "give up until the train stopped".

Anthony Williams, 33, of Langford Road, Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder.

He is also charged with four other alleged attempted murders following earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

Bletcher said he was travelling alone after doing Christmas shopping in Newark-on-Trent, in Nottinghamshire, and was "quite looking forward to the tapas I'd bought actually".

After Peterborough he noticed people running down the aisle, but he remained seated because he was "still not concerned", presuming there had been a disagreement.

He then saw a knife being held in front of him at eye level and said he felt "trappedâ¦ there is no way of escape", followed by a "scratch" to the head from the knife.

Bletcher said he moved his arm to shield his face and added: "There was nothing said to me and I didn't respond because there was nothing to respond to."

The court heard the victim - who is the first to give live evidence at the trial - was stabbed five more times.

News.title: Met Police boss 'wouldn't be surprised' if more allegations made about Brand
News.content:
During a pre-trial hearing in October, Brand tried unsuccessfully to have his criminal case thrown out.

His lawyers argued that the actor and entertainer could not receive a fair trial because of the publicity following the Dispatches programme.

During the trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009, when he rose to fame as one of Britain's most high-profile entertainers.

The women came to court to reveal how Brand used his immense fame to force them into sexual activity.

The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, told Brand to expect "a significant custodial term" after the verdicts were delivered.

A man who was accused of laughing while Russell Brand sexually assaulted a woman in 2009, has been asked "to step back" from his employer while they consider the verdicts.

Jack Bayles was part of his entourage in 2009 and was said to be present when one of the sexual assaults took place.

Brand had been working on a Channel 4 project when he laid his head into the groin area of a woman who was helping him at the time.

During the trial, the victim told the court Bayles and another member of Brand's staff had asked her to give the comedian a massage, and said he wouldn't continue unless she did.

Shortly after, he sexually assaulted her.

She had complained to her manager, who told the court through a statement at the trial that the victim had described how the men had laughed while the attack took place.

In recent years, Bayles has been working for the TV production company, Various Artists Ltd, as their head of comedy.

In a statement, they told the BBC: "We have asked Jack Bayles to step back from the company whilst we consider the verdict and events surrounding the trial. Our thoughts, though, are primarily with every one of Brand's victims at this time."

According to his biography on the Various Artists Ltd website, Bayles commissioned shows for Channel 4 including two series Derry Girls and Aisling Bea's This Way Up, plus Back, Year Of The Rabbit, Frank Of Ireland and Hullraisers.

In a statement, Bayles said he was sorry but doesn't remember the sexual assault.

"I am appalled and sickened by Brand's actions and have co-operated fully and voluntarily with the investigation and endeavoured to assist as best I can," he said.

"However, I do not remember the incident that took place 17 years ago in 2009. But I acknowledge that I clearly missed something at the time and did not see nor recognise that it caused distress. For that I am sincerely sorry."

Bayles said at the time of the offence he was in the early stages of his career, calling it "a frantic, pressured and toxic working environment".

He described Brand as someone who was "chaotic, dismissive and manipulated the people around him".

Bayles said this was why he decided to stop working with Brand in 2010 and had not had any contact with him since. He added that during his time with Brand, no complaints were made about the entertainer's behaviour.

"I am unaware if any were raised to anyone else more senior to me," he said.

"I would never willingly or proactively wish to make anyone feel uncomfortable, unsafe or unsupported at work. If I was ever present when Brand acted inappropriately and I failed to spot it and step in, then I sincerely apologise".

News.title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments
News.content:
Several universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.

Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".

She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too.

The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary.

Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.

Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs. They repay 9% of anything they earn over Â£25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off.

The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.

It also found that 12 universities only gave students worked examples of repayments based on earnings that are less than the UK average, which is Â£39,039.

News.title: Tube drivers to stage strikes in Christmas run-up
News.content:
A series of strikes in the spring over the same issue caused significant disruption across the network, with some lines being entirely closed.

Despite further talks being held since, RMT has not accepted TfL's proposals.

General secretary Eddie Dempsey said: "London Underground is attempting to dress up a wholesale attack on drivers' working conditions as a voluntary four-day week.

"Our members are being asked to spend more time driving trains, accept longer and more unpredictable shifts and surrender agreements that have been negotiated and defended over many years."

The union also said it believed the changes would "pave the way for hundreds of job cuts".

TfL said that drivers choosing to remain on a five-day week would be given a guarantee of remaining at the same depot.

Nick Dent, director of customer operations for London Underground, said: "This will give our colleagues a real, meaningful choice on their working pattern without having to change where they work.

"This will also mean less time at work for Tube drivers, while delivering a more efficient, reliable Tube service for our customers."

BBC London's transport correspondent Tom Edwards said the issue of a four-day working week had turned into a "long-running, festering dispute".

"The RMT union regards it as an intensification of the job; TfL sees the changes as being minor and part of a good deal.

"The RMT has been here before and strikes have been called off before. But this is a knotty issue and patience is wearing thin."

News.title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM
News.content:
Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.

The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible".

It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination. However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable.

It comes a week after the UK's equality watchdog said employees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues are earning.

Burnham said the current system felt "weighted against the applicant" and the changes were aimed at "tilting the scales back".

"It can be quite soul destroying for young people these days, applying for jobs when the salary is not listed but sometimes they're not getting a reply," he told the BBC.

The prime minister added that publishing salaries in adverts was also important for closing the gender pay gap.

He was also challenged over whether MPs should be disclosing salaries when advertising for staff in their offices.

A number of politicians are currently advertising for roles without giving an expected salary., external

Burnham said: "It would apply completely to them too and the call I'm making today is, before the law changes do it voluntarily because it's the right thing to do."

News.title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules
News.content:
The naming of smoky bacon-flavoured crisps has become the latest political headache to emerge from the government's bid for closer ties with the EU.

The government is negotiating a deal on food standards in a bid to cut costs for British companies trading with Europe.

Labour ministers have been keen to talk up the potential economic benefits of the agreement, which could be announced at a summit later this month.

But the deal's requirement for Britain to adopt EU food rules in a wide range of areas has threatened to reignite sovereignty debates from the Brexit era.

Labour ministers have been keen to sidestep talking about the impact of alignment in particular sectors, instead stressing the overall economic boost it expects the food deal to bring.

On Thursday, Environment Secretary Angela Eagle told a radio presenter he should "get a life" when he asked about the potential impact of the new rules on snacks, such as smoky bacon crisps.

But it highlights the political dangers for the government of realigning with regulations that British politicians have not been able to shape, with the Conservatives and Reform UK keen to pounce on cases showing Britain to be a "rule taker" from Brussels.

It is not the first regulatory skirmish over smoky bacon crisps - following previous headlines over how the well-loved British flavour could be affected by an EU decision in 2024 to phase out a number of artificial smoke flavourings.

Now, the flavour name itself has been called into question by a separate EU attempt to restrict how descriptions of meat are used to market food.

Under rules adopted this summer, the EU plans to restrict the use of 31 terms, including bacon, drumstick and steak, to products that contain meat, claiming consumers could be confused by plant-based alternatives using the same names.

The European snack industry is seeking clarity on how the rules, which will also cover terms such as pork, chicken and beef, would apply to meat-flavoured crisps, including those flavoured without the use of any meat extracts.

The UK government has said it expects the new regulations to be in scope of its proposed food standards deal.

This means they would also apply to companies marketing their products in Britain, which is among the biggest consumers of crisps in Europe, according to analysts Euromonitor., external

News.title: MTV Dirty Sanchez star Michael 'Pancho' Locke dies aged 47
News.content:
In a video Pritchard, from Cardiff, said he was currently climbing Mount Everest in the Himalayas and would dedicate his journey to its base camp to Locke.

"I'm still a little bit in shock," he said.

"My little friend of more than 35 years has left the building.

"We've had some amazing laughs together over the years. I've known him since he was about 14 years old.

"Of course the Sanchez years, travelled all over the world with him, been in some classic messes with him in the past partying. Now he's gone but I'll never forget him."

Fellow Dirty Sanchez star Lee Dainton, writing on social media, said: "When you grow up skating with your friends you're in your own little world.

"You never think about losing anyone from it. In your head those days and the people you shared them with live forever.

"Since hearing the news all those memories have been flooding back.

"I can see Panch, hear the laughter and remember all the best times like it was yesterday. Then it hits me that he's gone and I still can't believe it."

News.title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?
News.content:
High above the Arctic, powerful winds usually circle the North Pole each winter, helping trap some of the coldest air on Earth.

But this circulation, known as the polar vortex, has weakened and shifted position in recent days.

While such disruptions can occur during winter, scientists say an event this early in November is unprecedented in modern observations.

Similar disruptions in past years have sometimes been followed by colder weather affecting parts of Europe and North America.

However, as this is happening so early in the season, there are few historical examples to compare with and it could throw current winter forecasts into even more uncertainty.

News.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK crowns winner as BBC axes the series
News.content:
Warning: This article includes spoilers for the finale of RuPaul's Drag Race UK.

After 10 weeks of toe-to-toe lip-syncs, fierce runways and shady remarks, the time has come for one queen to be named the UK's next Drag Race superstar.

For the final time on the BBC, 12 contestants were whittled down to just one after the broadcaster announced it was axing RuPaul's Drag Race UK due to budget cuts.

On Thursday night, RuPaul crowned Flesh as the series eight winner.

The London queen snatched the title from Mocha, Naya Thorn and Alik, who also made it to the final episode.

The 26-year-old was crowned by last year's winner, Bones, who is also her best friend and drag sister, with the duo performing together as Heavenly Bodies.

Speaking to BBC Newsbeat after celebrating overnight, the Soho queen says the win still feels "surreal" and she spent the whole evening "smiling, crying, and laughing".

She will be the last queen crowned on the BBC before the UK edition moves to Wow Presents Plus, a streaming platform owned by the production company behind the show.

While some fans have welcomed the prospect of a new chapter for the series which might include bigger cash prizes, like in other spin-offs, others fear leaving the BBC will mean less representation for LGBTQ+ culture.

Flesh says the move to Wow could widen the range of performers and subcultures featured on the show, but worries the shift to subscription could reduce the audience for drag.

"This is where it feels slightly sadder that we're leaving the BBC because for all of the parameters that it created that limited what we could do, there was more exposure than drag has ever been given," she says.

She admits she is "concerned" about the "knock-on effect" this could have on the future of the UK drag industry, such as creating fewer opportunities for contestants.

"Without that exposure, there will be less demand and with less demand and less exposure, events won't be able to be created," she says.

News.title: Trump axes chief of staff Susie Wiles for Stephen Miller after resounding midterms defeat
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Stephen Miller, the architect of Donald Trump’s hardline anti-immigrant policies, will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff in the wake of midterm elections that saw Republicans lose control of the House and Senate as well as dozens of governorships and state legislatures.

Trump announced the personnel shakeup on Truth Social on Friday, writing that he was “pleased to announce” that Miller would take over Wiles’ role on November 9 and calling him “one of [his] trusted advisers.”

He explained the decision to reporters as he departed the White House for a weekend in Florida, telling them he had “wanted to make a change.”

“I think Susie's done a very good job, great job ... sometimes in life, you have to make moves,” he said.

He also called Miller a “great manager” and suggested he would be tasked with managing day-to-day policy work.

open image in gallery Miller has worked for Trump since his first campaign for the presidency in 2015 ( Reuters )

In a post on X, Wiles said Friday was her last day on the job and called her White House tenure “the honor of a lifetime.”

“I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” she added.

Miller, 41, is a longtime aide to the president who has spent much of the last two years implementing the administration's mass deportation campaign and pushing for harsh policies meant to make it more difficult for anyone from non-white-majority countries to immigrant to the United States.

He has also advocated for initiatives meant to use the entire weight of the federal government to punish jurisdictions where voters have elected Democrats, including by cutting off or denying them federal funds.

The California native has been singularly obsessed with stopping and reversing non-white immigration to the United States since his high school days when he was a regular caller into conservative radio shows.

Since Trump returned to office in 2025, he has also pushed for a maximalist view of presidential power that makes little to no allowances for the role of Congress — especially a Congress that will be controlled by Democrats starting Jan. 3.

And he advanced some of Trump’s more controversial foreign policy moves, including the president’s ill-fated push to acquire Greenland.

open image in gallery In a post on X, Wiles said Friday was her last day on the job and called her White House tenure “the honor of a lifetime.” She is pictured with the president in October ( AFP/Getty )

In January, he claimed the U.S. could seize the island, which is part of Denmark, by force and suggested that no country would oppose such a move because “we live in a world ... that is governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power.”

Miller’s influence has drawn criticism from even some Republicans such as outgoing North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis, who has called him “a big problem” who “should go.”

Tillis has also slammed Miller as the "architect of most of the dumbest proposals from the Trump White House" who has an "irrational way about going about things" and is “out of his depth.”

Trump’s decision to elevate Miller to the chief of staff position indicates a desire on the part of the president to escalate conflicts with an incoming Democratic Congress which is gearing up to resume oversight and investigations into the Trump administration’s conduct.

Wiles, who submitted her resignation to the president on Thursday, was the first woman to serve as White House chief of staff. She had been a co-architect of Trump’s 2024 election victory and had a reputation as one of the few people in Trump’s orbit who could talk him down from ill-considered decisions.

open image in gallery Miller, 41, pictured with Wiles, is a longtime aide to the president who has spent much of the last two years implementing the administration's hrdline mass deportations ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Miller was all smiles as he departed with Trump’s executive assistant, Natalie Harp, for Marine One shortly after the White House drama unfolded Friday afternoon ( AFP/Getty )

As recently as last month, Trump was denying reports that Wiles was on the outs and claimed she would be in her job as long as she wanted to be.

But a source familiar with the matter told The Independent that Trump had been souring on Wiles for some time as his popularity has waned and opposition to his administration’s policies has grown, with some in his circle suggesting that her family members were taking advantage of her position for their own financial gain.

The ascension of Miller as Wiles’ replacement is a clear signal that Trump’s policy agenda will not moderate in his lame duck period and could grow increasingly hard-line if Miller carries out what sources in the administration describe as a long-held desire to use the government’s full powers to target political opposition.

He has spent much of Trump’s second term leading efforts to turn the machinery of government against Democratic-leaning organizations and NGOs, a push that kicked into high gear after last year’s killing of MAGA activist Kirk.

Days after the September 2025 assassination, Miller told Vice President JD Vance — who was guest-hosting Kirk’s eponymous podcast — he wanted the administration “to use every resource we have at the Department of Justice, Homeland Security and throughout this government to identify, disrupt, dismantle and destroy” a “network” he blamed for Kirk’s death.

News.title: Yorkshire Tea causes upset after raising price and cutting number of teabags
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Yorkshire Tea has angered some of its customers after it raised prices and slashed the number of teabags in one of its blends.

Its Decaf Bedtime Brew with Vanilla & Nutmeg has been reduced from 40 to 20 tea bags, but is being sold at a higher price at UK supermarkets.

At Sainsbury’s, the 50g box with 20 tea bags is retailed at £3, up from £2.50 for the 100g box.

Ocado is selling the tea bag blend for £3, up from £2, while Tesco is selling it for £2.99, up from £2.50.

The move has caused upset amongst some shoppers who now have to pay more for a box that is half the size.

Yorkshire Tea said it understood that the price rise “may not be welcome news”.

A spokesperson told The Sun: “We’re always looking for ways to keep our tea offering in step with changing consumer needs, tastes and trends.

“We’ve recently introduced two new ranges, bringing fresh choice to our customers while making some changes to our existing products.

“We know Bedtime Brew is much loved, and its move to our new fruit and herbal selection means we can keep offering this favourite.”

open image in gallery Kenyan farmers who grow tea sold in UK supermarkets have warned that climate impacts are hitting yields and their already 'scarce' incomes ( PA )

It added: “We appreciate that a price increase may not be welcome news, but it reflects the blend’s new place in the range.”

The decaffeinated black tea is made of lemon balm, lemongrass, nutmeg and vanilla.

Tea prices in the UK have risen in recent years, with farmers issuing warnings of short supplies as climate change hits their yields.

In August, tea prices were up 2.5 per cent, compared to 0.5 per cent in July.

Kenyan growers, who provide half of all black tea consumed across Britain, say unpredictable weather patterns and lower crop yields have driven up global tea costs.

Fintea, a union of tea farming cooperatives based in Kericho, said production across five of its cooperatives fell by 30 per cent in May and June this year.

Nelson Ngeno, the manager of Fintea, said farmers are “really scared” as their livelihoods are “cut short” by the changing conditions.

“Climate is really affecting our farmers,” Mr Ngeno said. “There has been a complete change as far as the weather is concerned.”

News.title: Oscar-winning Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio dies at 52
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Oscar-winning Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio, whose acclaimed drama “A Fantastic Woman” broke ground with its portrayal of a transgender woman, has died in Santiago, Chile, at 52.

His family announced his death Friday in an Instagram post, citing health reasons but not specifying the cause.

“His memory will remain forever among us,” the family said. “He was a beautiful person who contributed to Chilean culture in great moments of its history.”

Lelio won the 2018 Academy Award for best international film (formerly known as foreign language film) for “A Fantastic Woman," starring trans actress Daniela Vega as a waitress and nightclub singer whose life is torn by the death of her boyfriend.

It was Chile's second Academy Award, following the animated short “Bear Story” in 2016.

Lelio’s other films include "Gloria," "The Wave," "The Wonder," “Disobedience,” and “The Year of the Tiger.” Throughout his career, he collaborated with Julianne Moore, Rachel Weisz and Florence Pugh.

Lelio had begun filming “Poeta Chileno” (Chilean Poet) based on the book by Alejandro Zambra in September.

He was born in the Argentine city of Mendoza and moved to Chile at the age of 2. He studied journalism for a year before enrolling at the Chilean Film School.

News.title: Thomas Markle allegations: What we know after Meghan’s father charged with child abuse images offences
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Duchess of Sussex’s estranged father Thomas Markle Snr is accused of possessing child sex abuse images.

Meghan Markle’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jnr, alleged that he found images belonging to her father at his former home in the Philippines, The Sun reported.

It has since emerged that the duchess sent a final letter to her father in 2025 while he was recovering from a leg amputation, to say she knows he is an abuser and that he will never see his grandchildren Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five.

In an interview with the Daily Mail, Mr Markle Snr denied possessing child sex images, calling the accusations “sick lies”.

He has admitted to paying for sex in the south-east Asian country but denies ever possessing a hoard of such material.

With an investigation ongoing, Philippine interior minister Joniv Remulla told the The Guardian that it appeared Mr Markle Snr was a “possible sex offender of the grossest kind”.

The Sun reports that Mr Markle Jnr told police he discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of the images at his father’s home in Cebu, and reported him to local police and the FBI.

open image in gallery Meghan and her father have not spoken since 2018 ( Instagram )

According to the newspaper, Mr Markle Snr is alleged to have left the images in storage boxes when he moved out of the property earlier this year.

Mr Markle Jnr said he submitted a statement to police in the Philippines and told The Sun: “When I found this material I was horrified and I had no option but to report my dad.

“I have supported, cared for him and helped him for years – but that stops now. I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him.”

The newspaper reports that Mr Markle Jnr was searching for a phone for his girlfriend’s father in boxes of his own father’s belongings, which led him to discover the images and videos.

In July, he reported them to the FBI Hotline, the United States’ National Centre for Exploited and Missing Children and state police in Pennsylvania, where his father was living.

Mr Markle Jnr also retrieved the four large cardboard boxes from storage and an IT expert helped him access three computer hard drives, revealing further images, The Sun reports.

Court papers filed in Cebu have begun police inquiry, the newspaper says.

open image in gallery Mr Markle has denied the allegations ( Instagram )

The Metropolitan Police confirmed that in 2019 it had passed a letter “containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom” to Meghan and Prince Harry, but did not share details with other law enforcement agencies.

The BBC and other media including the Telegraph, which said it had seen a copy, reported the note was written by Mr Markle Sr’s ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, who has since died.

She is the mother of Mr Markle Jr and Meghan’s other half-sibling, Samantha Markle, who has defended their father, telling the Mail on Sunday: “I believe this is a set-up.”

Meghan is “upset and really frustrated” by the Met’s handling of the investigation, the Telegraph reported.

She said that she was shown a letter sent to Scotland Yard making “troubling” allegations against Mr Markle Sr and was assured that these were being investigated.

The Met is now “reviewing the handling of this matter”, including whether it needs to be referred to the police watchdog.

In 2025, Mr Markle Snr moved to the Philippines for a new life after suffering a series of strokes.

Then, in December of that year he had his leg amputated during life-saving surgery.

open image in gallery She has been estranged from her father since the weeks leading up to her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018 ( AFP/Getty )

The Sun on Sunday reported that Meghan had written a final letter to her father during this period, telling him she knows he is an abuser and that he will never meet his grandchildren.

He is reportedly now living in a rehab centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk again.

In an interview with the Mail on Sunday, Mr Markle Sr said he has “never had sex with anyone under the age of 18”.

He told the paper that when he was single he travelled to the Philippines at least twice and “slept with prostitutes”.

“I like Asian women but that is not a crime,” he said. “I am not well enough to go to the Philippines but I will speak to anyone who wants to talk to me. I have nothing to hide.”

The Duchess has been estranged from her former TV lighting director father since the weeks before her wedding in 2018, after he staged and sold photographs to the paparazzi.

Meghan said in a statement: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.

open image in gallery Thomas Markle Sr has said the allegations are a ‘bunch of lies’ ( ITV/GMB )

“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me.

“It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.

“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.

“I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.

“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”

In response to the accusations, Mr Markle Snr said: “I'm shocked, I'm hurt and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.

“This is bulls****. It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies.”

News.title: Macklemore claims nine arenas blocked him from bringing ‘Free Palestine’ tour to US
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Macklemore has claimed that nine arenas have prevented him from being able to perform his “Free Palestine” tour in the United States.

The 43-year-old rapper, real name Benjamin Haggerty, announced initial concerts in London, Paris and Dublin in September after he was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour over comments he made about Gaza.

His exit from the tour came after billionaire and Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft gathered other venue owners to join him in blocking Macklemore from performing at their arenas.

Macklemore said in a statement Friday that “from the beginning, our plan was to bring this tour home to the U.S.”

However, he said there are no planned dates at this time, adding: “After weeks of reaching out, nine major American arenas have turned us down.”

open image in gallery Macklemore has claimed that arenas have prevented him from bringing his ‘Free Palestine’ tour to the US ( Getty )

“Madison Square Garden. Prudential Center. Barclays Center. UBS Arena. Intuit Dome. Kia Forum. Crypto.com Arena. Chase Center. Climate Pledge Arena,” Macklemore said, calling out each arena.

“By mid-September, we received available dates at these arenas through the end of the year,” the “Thrift Shop” rapper continued. “But once they found out these were my benefit shows for Palestine, those dates were suddenly off the table. The doors were closed. The conversations were all different, but the result was the same. The shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues.”

He continued: “In over twenty years of touring, I’ve never experienced anything like this. Looking back over the last three years, the only real regret I have is not speaking publicly when Zionists were kicking me under the table.

“At the time, I didn’t believe that centering what was happening to me was worth taking any attention away from the genocide in Palestine. But the intimidation, manipulation and suppression I experienced are part of how those in power keep entertainers quiet.”

Macklemore went on to say that he would “rather lose every opportunity in this industry than spend another day protecting people who value their business relationships with Israel more than they value Palestinian human life.”

open image in gallery ‘The intimidation, manipulation and suppression I experienced are part of how those in power keep entertainers quiet,’ Macklemore wrote on social media ( Getty )

He captioned his post: “Trying to silence us will only make the message louder.”

Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran’s tour in September due to his onstage display of support for Palestine amid the ongoing conflict with Israel. The rapper then doubled down, announcing his “Free Palestine” tour. He said shortly after that the gigs “sold out immediately” after ticket sales began.

All the proceeds from the concerts went toward a number of organizations working in support of Palestinian people with medical care, humanitarian assistance, education, community support and advocacy.

The Independent has contacted the nine arenas for comment. A spokesperson for Madison Square Garden said: “We have some of the busiest venues in the world with extremely limited availability and he’s not an arena level act.”

News.title: A quarter of Americans falsely link child vaccines and acetaminophen to autism, survey shows
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Many Americans still hold unproven and false beliefs about risk factors for autism, a large new survey reveals.

A quarter of more than 30,000 adults in a recent study said childhood vaccination and taking acetaminophen – also known as Tylenol – during pregnancy were tied to the brain development condition — despite extensive evidence showing the opposite.

More men and Republicans were likely to endorse these beliefs, as well as adults aged 35-44 and people who were Black or Hispanic. Republican leaders such as Robert Kennedy Jr. and President Donald Trump have pushed the ideas about vaccination and autism.

The findings may reflect diminished trust in traditional sources of public health, the researchers from Massachusetts, New York and New Jersey suggest. Greater trust in scientific and medical institutions was associated with lower rates of endorsement.

“Our results add to abundant evidence of the growing politicization of beliefs about science and medicine,” they wrote. “This politicization of science preceded the Covid-19 pandemic, but variability in responses to the pandemic by state and federal leadership likely accelerated this trend.”

open image in gallery A surprising number of American adults still hold unproven beliefs about autism risk factors, a new survey finds ( Getty Images )

That might not be surprising. The pandemic and rollout of the Covid vaccines have been tied to a surge in vaccine hesitancy and misinformation.

What may be surprising is that social media use – a known source of misinformation and disinformation – was not linked to these beliefs.

Instead, more frequent social media use showed a lower likelihood for them.

“One possibility is that social media use parallels information seeking more generally — i.e., those with lower levels of use are also those with less access to sources of reliable health information,” the researchers said in a news release.

The data was recorded online from 30,288 adults in all 50 states and Washington, D.C.

What is known about autism

Autism affects how people learn and communicate, but living with autism is a unique experience for each individual.
