World.title: Fani-Kayode rejects senior counsel of Nigeria title
World.content:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, on Friday, disassociated himself from the designation of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN), known as Blue Silk, that the Nigerian Law Society (NLS) conferred on him.

According to a press statement signed by his special assistant on media, Lizzy Okoji, Mr Fani-Kayode said he “did not personally authorise or approve the acceptance of the said designation and hereby formally disassociates himself from the purported conferment.”

He explained that he sent a representative to the NLS event for official engagements in honour of the society’s invitation.

Mr Fani-Kayode, a lawyer, described his representative’s acceptance of the designation as an “unfortunate administrative misjudgement” and did not reflect his endorsement or convictions.

The NLS, which gained attention in recent years with its posturing as a rival to the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) and introduction of the controversial Blue Silk title in 2025, reportedly conferred the title on Mr Fani-Kayode and four other lawyers.

The other recipients were Seyi Tinubu, Olufunmilayo Osifuye, Ihudiebube Chukwumdi and Alabi Adigun. The conferment reportedly took place on Thursday at the society’s 2026 Annual General Conference held in Utako, Abuja.

Mr Fani-Kayode, a former aviation minister, cast doubts on the legal status of the NLS.

He said, with his 41 years of professional experience as a legal practitioner, he would not “undermine the integrity of the legal profession, or bring the profession into disrepute.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“It is particularly pertinent to note that the purported conferment raises serious questions regarding its legal and professional implications, particularly in view of the statutory framework regulating the legal profession in Nigeria and relevant judicial pronouncements concerning the conferment of professional ranks outside the established legal framework.”

He urged the public to disregard any misrepresentation and reaffirmed his commitment to “the rule of law, professional ethics, and the dignity of the legal profession.”

The conferment of the designation of blue silk has been the subject of controversy in Nigeria.

In November 2025, the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) addressed concerns over the actions of Tonye Jaja, who was promoting the creation of the “privileged rank” or “Blue Silk” for legal practitioners.

According to the NBA, his action was inconsistent with the legal profession’s regulatory framework, misleading and misrepresented institutional structures.

On 12 February, the Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee (LPPC), a body saddled with the conferment of the rank of the Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), warned lawyers against using the designation ‘Blue Silk’ and stressed that the title is not recognised in the Nigerian legal profession.

In May, the Federal High Court in Abuja dismissed a suit seeking to introduce the rank of ‘Blue Silk’ for legal practitioners in Nigeria as an alternative to the rank of SAN.

World.title: Friday Sermon: Stop mocking President Tinubu’s Umrah Ibadah in the name of politics!, By Murtadha Gusau
World.content:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

All praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of all worlds, Who sees the hidden secrets of the chest and records every word uttered by the tongue. We send peace and blessings upon the Master of Prophets, Muhammad (Peace be upon him), who warned his Ummah against the destructive nature of the tongue and the violation of sacred symbols.

Dear brothers and sisters! President Bola Ahmed Tinubu performed the Ibadah of Umrah, the lesser Hajj in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, in late October 2026.

During the Umrah trip, President Tinubu and members of his delegation had the rare honour of entering inside the Noble Ka’abah to pray, following a privilege extended by King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

The Nigerian delegation included selected Muslim governors, led by Nigeria Governors’ Forum Chairman AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara State, National Security Advisor Nuhu Ribadu, industrialist Abdul Samad Rabiu, as well as various ministers and government officials.

During the spiritual exercise, President Tinubu prayed for lasting peace, national unity, security, economic progress, and stability in Nigeria. He also urged Nigerians to embrace national diversity as a source of strength.

President Tinubu subsequently departed Saudi Arabia after concluding the visit.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Dear servants of Allah! Know that this world is a fleeting shadow, and politics is but a shifting game played within its temporary borders. Leaders rise and fall, nations shift, and political allegiances evolve. Yet, there remain certain constants that a Muslim believer must never compromise: the sanctity of acts of worship, the reverence due to the rituals of Allah, and the absolute danger of letting political animosity corrupt the spiritual heart.

A dangerous trend has crept into our discourses—where the sacred is weaponised for worldly rivalries, and the spiritual journeys of individuals are subjected to the mockery of the public square. Specifically, we observe the tongues of many targeting the Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage of our leaders, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. This sermon is a clarion call, a solemn warning, and a heart-softening admonition to those who let political fervor blind them to spiritual boundaries: To Be careful!

The first and most critical reality to understand is that the Ibadah of Umrah is not a political rally; it is a sacred response to a divine invitation. When a human being—regardless of their political office, their shortcomings, or your personal opinion of their governance—puts on the white sheets of Ihram, cries out “Labbaikallahummah Labbaik”, Here I am, O Allah, at Your service, and circumambulates the Ka’abah, they are engaging in a foundational ritual of Islam.

Allah Almighty states clearly in the Noble Qur’an:

“That is so. And whoever honours the symbols of Allah – indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.” [Qur’an, 22:32]

Conversely, treating these symbols with flippancy or using them as punchlines for political memes borders on a spiritual catastrophe. When you mock a Muslim believer’s presence at the Ka’abah, are you mocking the man, or are you trivialising the place? Are you criticising his policies, or are you scoffing at the act of a servant standing before his Master, Allah?

The tongue is a small organ, but its harvest can drag a person face-down into the fire. Regulate your political speech so that it does not spill over into cosmic arrogance.

Human nature often tempts us to judge the intentions of others, especially those we dislike. In politics, it is easy to dismiss a leader’s pilgrimage as “PR,” “photo-ops,” or “hypocrisy.”

Let us recall the profound ascetic teaching from the life of the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) and his companions. During a battle, Usamah Bin Zaid (may Allah be pleased with him) faced an enemy soldier who had killed many Muslim believers. Just as Usamah raised his sword to strike him, the man cried out, “La ilaha illallah”, There is no god but Allah. Usamah, believing the man only said it to save his life, struck him down anyway.

When news of this reached the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him), his face changed with grief and anger. He turned to Usamah and repeatedly asked:

“Did you split open his heart to see whether he said it sincerely or not?” [Sahih Muslim]

If the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) rebuked a beloved companion for questioning the shahadah and testimony of an active enemy on the battlefield, what gives any commentator, any blogger, any politician, or any citizen the right to peer into the heart of a pilgrim in Makkah and declare his worship invalid? Remember, you do not own the keys to acceptance; Allah Almighty does.

Political dissatisfaction is a right, and holding leaders accountable is a civic and Islamic duty. Islam encourages speaking truth to power and demanding justice. However, when political frustration mutates into blind hatred, it darkens the intellect and ruins spiritual discernment.

Allah the Most High warns the Muslim believers. He says:

“O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.” [Qur’an, 5:8]

Psychologically, when you mock someone’s prayers or pilgrimage, you are training your mind to view them as sub-human or entirely devoid of good. This is a deception of Iblis, the Satan. A person can be a flawed leader, make economic policies that cause hardship, or govern in a way you deeply disagree with—yet still have a spark of faith that drives them to tears in front of the Ka’abah.

Do not let your political stance rob you of your spiritual objectivity. If a leader goes to seek guidance, forgiveness, or strength at the House of Allah, the mature response of a Muslim believer is to pray that they find it—because a guided, righteous leader benefits the entire nation, while a broken leader leaves everyone vulnerable.

Consider this a final, moving narrative for the soul. The classical scholars of Islam—the ascetics and the righteous—used to fear talking about the sins or spiritual states of others because of a terrifying spiritual law: What you mock in your brother, Allah may test you with before you die.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim wrote that criticising others for their spiritual vulnerabilities or mocking their relationship with Allah is a sign of self-righteousness. When you look at a leader’s Umrah and sneer, you are implicitly saying, “My worship is pure, but his is fake.” This arrogance destroys your own good deeds.

Imagine standing on the Day of Judgment. You expect to see your prayers, your charity, and your fasts. Instead, you find your scale empty because your good deeds were transferred to the politician you mocked. You handed over your eternal capital in exchange for a few likes, posts, retweets, or laughs in a political WhatsApp group. What a miserable bankruptcy!

Respected brothers and sisters! Let us draw a firm, unbreakable line between political critique and spiritual transgression.

● Critique policies? Yes.

● Demand accountability? Yes.

● Express frustration over governance? Yes.

● Mock the sacred acts of worship, judge intentions, or ridicule a human being standing at the House of Allah? Never.

Turn your tongues away from the sacred boundaries of worship. Protect your own scales of justice. If you see a leader at the Ka’abah, let your heart-softening reminder be:

“Ya Allah, if he is seeking Your face, guide him to justice for the sake of the millions he leads. And if he is lacking, reform his heart, for the reform of the leader is the reform of the Ummah.”

Fellow Nigerians! In recent times, a deeply troubling affliction has manifested within our public discourse—an ailment born of political rivalry that has breached the boundaries of faith. We have witnessed individuals, driven by political differences, resorting to mockery, sarcasm, and ridicule regarding the acts of worship performed by others. Specifically, the spectacle of turning the sacred journey of Umrah—undertaken by leaders, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu—into a jest for political scoring is a dangerous transgression that requires an immediate, heart-softening warning.

Politics is a worldly endeavour, a sphere of governance, debate, policy, and critique. Critique policies as you wish. Demand accountability as you must. But when you cross the threshold of secular criticism to mock a Muslim believer standing before their Lord in the Haram of Makkah, wallahi you are no longer playing politics. You are playing with your hereafter, your Akhirah!

Allah, the Exalted, issues a severe warning in the Glorious Qur’an regarding those who turn signs of faith or devotion into objects of ridicule. He says:

“If you ask them, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and playing.’ Say, ‘Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?’ Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.” [Qur’an, 9:65-66]

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) taught us that a person’s heart is a sanctuary known only to the Creator. When a Muslim believer puts on the Ihram, declares “Labbaikallahummah Labbaik,” and circumambulates the Ka’abah, they are answering the call of Prophet Ibrahim (AS). They are standing as a beggar at the door of the Almighty Allah. To reduce that profound spiritual submission into a meme, a punchline, or a weapon of political warfare is to display a terrifying lack of Taqwa and Allah-consciousness.

Remember the words of the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him):

“A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He does not wrong him, he does not fail him, and he does not humiliate him. Piety is here”—and he pointed to his chest three times—”It is enough evil for a man to humiliate his Muslim brother.” [Sahih Muslim]

Consider the spiritual psychological cost of your actions. When you mock an act of worship, you cultivate a disease of arrogance within your own chest. You convince yourself that your political alignment makes you spiritually superior, or that your disdain for an earthly leader gives you the right to judge their standing before Allah. This is the very arrogance that led Iblis to destruction.

Let the history of our righteous predecessors serve as a moving narrative and an ascetic teaching. They would tremble at the thought of speaking ill of another person’s secret worship. They understood that a leader’s account is with Allah, and a servant’s devotion is private. If you believe a leader is falling short, the Prophetic remedy is sincere supplication and Du’a for their guidance and rectification, not public ridicule of their prayers.

Dear Muslim believers! This is a clarion call par-excellence to purify your hearts. The digital age and the political coliseum have desensitised us. We post, tweet, and share without weighing the weight of our words on the Day of Judgment.

Imagine standing on the Day of Resurrection, a day when every hidden deed is brought to light, and discovering that your good deeds have been transferred to the account of the very politician you despised—all because your tongue and your fingers could not refrain from mocking their pilgrimage. Is a transient political victory worth your eternal ruin?

Turn back to Allah in sincere repentance. Remove the poison of political malice from your spiritual practice. Let us critique with civility, hold to account with justice, but guard the sacred boundaries of Islam with absolute reverence.

Dear brothers and sisters! The Ka’abah is the absolute anchor of the human spirit, a terrestrial mirror of the celestial realm, and the immutable center around which the Muslim believer’s life must revolve. It is not merely a structure of granite and silk; it is the physical manifestation of divine oneness (Tauhid) and the ultimate focal point of human devotion.

When you stand before the Ka’abah, you do not merely look at a building; you stand at the intersection of heaven and earth. Islamic scholars of the heart remind us that the Ka’abah is positioned directly beneath the Baitul-Ma’mur, the most Frequented House in the seventh heaven, where seventy thousand angels circumambulate daily, never to return. When you perform Tawaf, your steps synchronise with the cosmic worship of the angelic host. You become part of a celestial symphony of praise that has echoed since the dawn of creation.

Five times a day, over two billion human beings turn their faces toward this single point on Earth. This is not an empty ritual; it is a psychological anchor. No matter how fractured, chaotic, or confusing your day has been, the moment you turn toward the Qiblah, you are choosing order over chaos. You are uniting your heart with millions of Muslim believers across time and space. The Ka’abah is our ultimate anchor of unity—a reminder that despite our different languages, cultures, and flaws, we share one heartbeat, one direction, and one Destination.

While the Ka’abah holds an unparalleled, sacred status, the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) looked at it and delivered a profound truth that should shake every soul. He said:

“How great you are and how great is your sanctity! Yet, the sanctity of a Muslim believer is even greater in the sight of Allah than you.” [Sunan Ibn Majah]

This is the ultimate Islamic insight: The Ka’abah was built to direct the human heart to Allah, but the human heart itself is the vessel that holds Iman (faith). To disrespect, oppress, or break the heart of a fellow Muslim believer is a greater violation than tearing down the stones of the Ka’abah. We must honour the House of Allah, but we must also honour the servants of Allah.

Stop living a life without a center. If your life feels scattered, it is because you have placed your desires, your anxieties, or your worldly career at the core of your existence.

Reset your spiritual compass. Let your daily prayers be your personal Tawaf around the commands of Allah. Turn your face, your heart, and your ambitions toward the King of Kings, Allah. Just as the Ka’abah stands firm, unmoving amidst the millions who rush around it, let your faith remain unshakable amidst the turbulent storms of this life.

Dear servants of Allah! Know that the minor pilgrimage, the Umrah, is not a vacation. It is not a tourism of sight, but a migration of the soul. It is a divine invitation issued by the King of kings, Allah, to those He chooses to forgive.

When you intend Umrah, you enter the state of Ihram. You strip away the garments of status, wealth, and ego. You shroud yourself in two simple pieces of white cloth, stepping out of the world and into the rehearsal of your own resurrection. You stand equal to millions, declaring with your body and your breath that you own nothing, and that Allah Almighty owns everything.

The position of Umrah in Islam is the position of an absolute spiritual erasure. The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) declared that:

“Alternate between Hajj and Umrah, for they remove poverty and sins just as the bellows remove impurities from iron, gold, and silver.”

And he said:

“An Umrah to another Umrah is an expiation for whatever sins occur between them.”

Umrah is the ultimate weapon of the Muslim believer against despair. When the weight of the world crushes your chest, when your sins feel like mountains, and when your heart feels hardened by the illusions of this temporary life, Umrah is the divine reset button. It is the place where tears do not represent weakness, but the washing away of a heavy past.

Think of the Tawaf. You circumambulate the Ka’abah—the visual center of your entire earthly existence. Seven times you orbit the house of Allah, aligning the beating of your heart with the axis of Islamic monotheism. Every step is a heartbeat. Every circle is a declaration that Allah is the center of your universe, your thoughts, your family, and your destiny.

Think of the Sa’yi. You run between Safa and Marwa, retracing the desperate, unyielding trust of Hajar. It is the ultimate psychological and physical manifestation of Tawakkul, the reliance on Allah Almighty. You run in the valley of your struggles, crying out to the Heavens, knowing that when the means of this world fail you, the Lord of the heavens will cause Zamzam to gush forth from beneath your feet.

You arrive burdened. You leave unburdened. You arrive captive to your desires. You leave emancipated. When you shave or trim your hair at the completion of your rites, you are shedding the final remnants of your old self. You step out of the Haram as a newborn soul, clothed in mercy, enveloped in peace, and armed with an unbreakable connection to your Creator, Allah.

Do not delay the call. If your wealth allows and your body is able, answer the invitation of your Lord. Let your tears flow upon the sacred gravel. Let your voice rise with the Talbiyah: “Labbaikallahummah Labbaik—Here I am, O Allah, here I am!”

And finally, know that, mocking the religion of Allah is not a casual slip of the tongue; it is a profound spiritual catastrophe that instantly nullifies faith. In an era where sacred symbols such as Umrah are reduced to punchlines and divine decrees are bartered for social validation, the Muslim believer must confront a sobering reality: treating Islam as a jest is a definitive exit from its fold.

The Creator of the cosmos has established boundaries that are absolute. The verses of Allah, His names, the character of His Messenger (Peace be upon him), and the pillars of His law are the bedrock of human existence. When these are mocked, it signals a deeper, terrifying pathology—the death of Taqwa and Allah-consciousness, and the total absence of reverence in the heart.

The gravity of this sin is perfectly illustrated in an incident during the Campaign of Tabuk. A group of individuals, sitting in a gathering, casually remarked about the reciters of the Noble Qur’an. They said:

“We have not seen anyone like these reciters of ours—they have the biggest appetites, the most untruthful tongues, and are the most cowardly in the face of the enemy.”

A companion, recognising the poison in these words, immediately called them out as hypocrites and reported the matter. The men rushed to the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) as he was mounting his camel, clutching at his stirrups, pleading:

“O Messenger of Allah, we were only talking idly and jesting to pass the time on the journey!”

The divine response was immediate, terrifying, and eternal. Allah the Most High says:

“And if you ask them, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and playing.’ Say, ‘Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?’ Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.” [Qur’an, 9:65–66]

Notice the psychological reality: they did not intend to wage war against Islam; they intended to make a joke. Yet Allah did not accept their excuse of “casual humour.” Idolising entertainment over the Almighty strips away the garment of Iman.

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) warned us of this exact psychological desensitisation. He said:

“A servant may speak a word entirely half-heartedly, not realising its gravity, and because of it, he plummets into the Fire of Hell further than the distance between the East and the West.” [Al-Bukhari]

To protect your soul from this spiritual erosion, you must actively implement three boundaries:

1.⁠ ⁠Guard Your Tongue and Screen

Treat the Sunnah, the Umrah, the Ka’abah, the Hijab, the Beard, the Prayer, and the Islamic scholars with absolute sanctity. If a joke compromises these, it is toxic.

2.⁠ ⁠The Power of Departure

If you sit in a gathering—online or offline—where Islam is ridiculed, walk away. Remaining silent is complicity. Allah Almighty says:

“…do not sit with them until they enter into another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them.” [Qur’an, 4:140]

3.⁠ ⁠Renew Your Awe

Constantly study the Majesty of Allah. The more you know Him, the more impossible it becomes to ever laugh at a joke made at His expense.

● The Bottom Line

Do not trade the eternal honour of being a servant of Allah for a cheap laugh. Protect your reverence, safeguard your tongue, and hold fast to the sacred.

May Allah open the doors to His Sacred House for every longing heart, cleanse us of our shortcomings, and accept from us our worship.

Ya Allah! Rectify our leaders and rectify our followers. Purify our hearts from hypocrisy, arrogance, and malice. Guide our tongues to speak only what is true and pleasing to You. Protect us from mocking Your signs and Your worship.

May Allah purify our hearts from rancour, safeguard our tongues from arrogance, and grant us the wisdom to balance our worldly concerns with our eternal obligations. Ameen.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace, blessings and salutations of Allah be upon our noble Messenger, Muhammad, and upon his family, his Companions and his true followers.

Murtadha Muhammad Gusau is the Chief Imam of Nagazi-Uvete Jumu’ah and the late Alhaji Abdur-Rahman Okene’s Mosques, Okene, Kogi State, Nigeria. He can be reached via: [email protected] or +2348038289761 or +2348024192217.

World.title: Nigeria, eight other African countries record 67 yellow fever cases, 18 deaths — WHO
World.content:
Nigeria and eight other African countries recorded 67 confirmed yellow fever cases, including 18 deaths, between January and October 2026, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO).

The affected countries are Burkina Faso, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria and Togo.

In a Disease Outbreak News report published on 6 November 2026, the WHO said yellow fever transmission continues across its African Region, with recent outbreak activity concentrated in parts of West Africa, including communities close to international borders.

Nigeria recorded four confirmed cases, including one death, during the reporting period, while Cameroon reported nine cases and one death.

Côte d’Ivoire recorded the highest number of confirmed cases, with 30 infections and 10 deaths, followed by Burkina Faso, which reported 15 cases and three deaths.

Ghana recorded four cases and three deaths, while Liberia reported one laboratory-confirmed case. The Central African Republic recorded two cases, while Guinea and Togo reported one case each. No deaths were recorded among confirmed cases in the latter three countries.

The WHO noted that the figures reflect the latest information available as of 12 October 2026. It said the detection of cases in the nine countries indicates increased transmission across parts of West Africa.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Factors driving transmission

The WHO identified frequent cross-border movement, uneven vaccination coverage and environmental conditions that favour the spread of infected mosquitoes as factors increasing the risk of further transmission.

“Occupational and environmental exposures, including work in or near forested areas, mining activities, and other outdoor occupations, are important risk factors for yellow fever infection,” it noted.

“Frequent cross-border population movement, the presence of competent mosquito vectors, and uneven vaccination coverage increase the risk of further transmission and geographic spread.”

According to the WHO, cross-border movement for trade, farming, livestock, and mining could contribute to the spread of the virus between affected and neighbouring countries.

The WHO said affected countries, with support from the organisation and other partners, are strengthening disease surveillance, investigating cases, conducting laboratory tests and intensifying efforts to identify infections.

Other measures include community engagement, risk communication and vaccination activities in affected and high-risk areas.

Regional risk

The WHO said it assessed the overall public health risk associated with the yellow fever situation as moderate across the African Region on 27 October, while the global risk remains low.

It considered continued transmission and additional cases in the region likely, citing existing immunity gaps, challenges with surveillance and laboratory testing, insecurity, limited resources and difficulties accessing some affected communities.

The organisation warned that introducing the virus into densely populated urban and peri-urban areas with low vaccination coverage could trigger larger outbreaks and put additional pressure on public health response systems.

“Unvaccinated populations are at highest risk, particularly rural and forest-edge communities, mobile and cross-border populations and people who work in forested areas, agriculture or mining,” it added.

Vaccination remains key

Yellow fever is an acute viral disease transmitted through the bite of infected mosquitoes. It can cause fever, headache, body aches, nausea, vomiting and weakness.

According to the WHO, about 15 per cent of infected people develop severe illness, which may involve recurrent high fever, jaundice, bleeding, shock and organ failure.

“Approximately half of patients who enter this severe phase die within seven to 10 days,” it noted.

The WHO said no specific antiviral treatment is routinely recommended, and clinical management is largely supportive.

It identified vaccination as the most effective preventive measure, noting that a single dose provides lifelong protection.

The WHO urged at-risk countries to maintain high vaccination coverage through routine immunisation and preventive or outbreak-response campaigns, particularly in communities with identified immunity gaps.

It also called for stronger surveillance, timely laboratory testing, mosquito control and public awareness of symptoms and prevention measures.

The organisation advised international travellers aged nine months and above visiting areas at risk of yellow fever transmission to receive vaccination.

World.title: Flamingos captain Harmony Chidi targets historic U-17 World Cup title for Nigeria
World.content:
Nigeria captain Harmony Chidi says winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup would create an unforgettable moment for the country as the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco.

Chidi said lifting the trophy would be a source of pride for the players, their coaches and the country, which is seeking to become the first African nation to win the competition.

“I think it would be a great thing, a joy, and would never be forgotten in life,” she told FIFA.

“Reaching the final is a very big thing, it’s a great thing, and it’s something that we have dreamed of. [Winning] would be something myself, my country, my teammates, our coaches, and everybody would be proud of.”

Nigeria have already made history by becoming the first African team to reach the final of the competition. A victory over Japan would take that achievement further by securing the continent’s first title.

The Flamingos’ journey to the final has been marked by a remarkable recovery after they lost 2-1 to Poland in their opening Group B match.

Under coach Akeem Busari, Nigeria responded with five consecutive victories over Puerto Rico, defending champions DPR Korea, Mexico, Venezuela and Brazil to reach the final.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Their 3-1 victory over DPR Korea was one of the campaign’s defining moments, while the semi-final win over Brazil secured their place in the title match.

Busari had declared before the tournament that Nigeria wanted to become champions, and his team now have an opportunity to fulfil that ambition against Japan.

For Chidi, however, reaching the final is only part of the dream. The captain is hoping to lead her teammates to a victory that would give Nigeria and the players a lasting place in the competition’s history.

The final gives the Flamingos a chance to turn their historic campaign into an unprecedented triumph for African women’s football.

World.title: ‘I don’t fight for supremacy, but historically, I’m number one’ — Alaafin
World.content:
The Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Owoade, has said he does not engage in supremacy contests with other traditional rulers.

Mr Owoade made the statement during an interview with Edmund Obilo on State Affairs, where he maintained that the Alaafin’s throne occupies the foremost position in Yorubaland.

The video was posted on Mr Obilo’s YouTube page on Friday.

His remarks follow a reported disagreement with the Ooni of Ife, Enitan Ogunwusi, over the Okanlomo of Yorubaland title, which Mr Ogunwusi bestowed on businessman Dotun Sanusi.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Alaafin challenged the Ooni’s decision, describing it as an abuse of authority, an affront to his institution and a breach of traditional customs and the law.

Asked if his relationship with the Ooni of Ife involved a contest for traditional dominance, Mr Owoade said: “Alaafin is the supreme king in Yoruba land. Historically, yes I am. Alaafin is number one. Well, that’s a very good question anyway.

“I don’t fight for supremacy or whatever, you know, with anybody. But all I know is that historically, if you want to go by history and then the contribution of Yoruba civilisation, then I would say that Alaafin is number one.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Oyo State Council of Obas

Furthermore, the Alaafin declined to comment on Governor Seyi Makinde’s appointment of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, as chairman of the reconstituted Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs.

This newspaper earlier reported that the Oyo State House of Assembly stripped the Alaafin stool of its permanent chairmanship of the council through the amended Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs Law, 2025.

At the inauguration of Oba Ladoja as chairman, held at the House of Chiefs Hall, State Secretariat, the Alaafin was conspicuously absent, marking the formal commencement of the new law.

When asked whether he was unhappy with Oba Ladoja’s appointment, Mr Owoade declined to respond.

“Well, that’s a question I would, I’m sorry, I wouldn’t want to answer anyway”, he added.

The Alaafin also announced plans for the maiden edition of Oyo Empire Day, scheduled for 17 to 19 December in Oyo City, Oyo State.

He said the three-day event would attract up to 40,000 attendees.

“The Oyo Empire Day is a three-day event. We are expecting a large crowd. We’re expecting up to 40,000 people.”

World.title: AFCON Qualifiers: Fresh injury setback for Osimhen as Galatasaray confirm knee surgery
World.content:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is set to undergo another surgery after Galatasaray confirmed that he will have an arthroscopic procedure on his left knee, raising doubts about his availability for Nigeria’s forthcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Tanzania.

The Turkish champions announced on Friday that the Nigerian forward sustained a strain in his left knee during their UEFA Champions League encounter against VfB Stuttgart.

An MRI examination subsequently detected a loose body in the affected knee, prompting the club to schedule surgery for Saturday at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital.

In a statement, Galatasaray said the procedure would be performed by the club’s doctor, Yener İnce.

The club also confirmed that Osimhen had been withdrawn from the squad for Saturday’s domestic fixture against Amed Sportif Faaliyetler.

The development is a major setback for Nigeria as they prepare for a double-header against Tanzania in the 2027 AFCON qualifiers.

The Super Eagles will host the Taifa Stars in Uyo on 13 November before travelling to Tanzania for the return fixture on 17 November.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Osimhen’s expected absence would be another major blow to head coach Éric Chelle, who has previously had to manage the team’s attack without the Galatasaray forward.

The 27-year-old missed Nigeria’s opening two qualifying matches against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau in September after struggling to recover from a muscle injury sustained during Galatasaray’s 3-2 victory over Istanbul Basaksehir on 4 September.

He was initially named in Chelle’s squad for those matches but was subsequently withdrawn after his recovery took longer than anticipated.

Galatasaray disclosed that medical examinations revealed a moderate-to-advanced strain with bleeding in his right adductor muscle group.

His latest injury, involving the left knee, presents a fresh fitness challenge for the striker, although Galatasaray are yet to provide a recovery timeline following the planned operation.

Nigeria are in Group L alongside Tanzania, Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau. Tanzania, as one of the tournament’s co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda, have already secured automatic qualification for the 2027 finals, leaving the other three countries to contest the remaining qualifying place.

World.title: 2027: Malami condemns alleged attacks on ADC campaign
World.content:
Former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, has condemned alleged attacks and acts of intimidation against members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State.

Malami, the ADC governorship candidate in Kebbi State, also expressed appreciation to residents for what he described as the massive turnout and support for former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the party’s leadership at the campaign event held on Thursday, November 5.

In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Assistant on Media, Mohammed Bello Doka, Malami said the turnout demonstrated the people’s determination to pursue a better future for the state and the country.

He commended Atiku for his leadership and commitment to national renewal, while acknowledging the contributions of the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, other party leaders, campaign coordinators, supporters and volunteers.

Malami said the party was committed to building a Nigeria that was affordable and secure, identifying rising fuel costs, insecurity and unemployment as issues requiring urgent attention.

He also outlined his priorities for Kebbi to include agricultural transformation, quality education, accessible healthcare, youth empowerment, security, local government autonomy and accountable governance.

However, he expressed concern over reports of attacks on members of the campaign convoy, destruction of media equipment and the alleged use of tear gas around areas occupied by members of the visiting delegation.

He said any involvement of government institutions or security agencies in such incidents would be unacceptable and called for an investigation.

Malami also condemned the demolition of the Malami Pressure Group (MPG) headquarters along Sani Abacha Bypass, Birnin Kebbi, describing the circumstances surrounding the incident as troubling.

He said the Kebbi State Government’s denial of involvement and its attribution of the demolition to a private ownership dispute did not remove the need for transparency and accountability.

According to him, political disagreements should not be used to justify intimidation, destruction of property or the suppression of lawful opposition.

Malami said the constitutional rights to freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly must be respected by all levels of government.

On the challenges facing Kebbi, he listed banditry, displacement, poverty, food insecurity and disruption of agricultural activities, citing the National Emergency Management Agency’s humanitarian intervention in March 2026 for victims of banditry in Shanga, Yauri and Bunza.

He urged the state government to prioritise the protection of farmers, access to education, food affordability and employment opportunities for young people rather than engage in actions capable of intimidating political opponents.

The ADC governorship candidate also called on the state government, security agencies and political actors to respect democratic principles and guarantee citizens the freedom to participate in the political process.

He urged party supporters to remain peaceful, disciplined and law-abiding, saying democratic change should be pursued through responsible political engagement and respect for the rule of law.

World.title: Pope says in ‘fairly good shape’ after lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV delivers his speech during the weekly general audience at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican on October 7, 2026. (Photo by Andreas SOLARO / AFP)







Pope Leo XIV said Friday he was in “fairly good shape” after lung cancer surgery last month as he began a 12-day tour of South America with a visit to Uruguay.

“I know some people were doubtful about this trip taking place,” Leo told reporters on board the papal plane.

“I had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward. And I am very happy to say praise the Lord and thanks to wonderful medical assistance, I’m here today, I think in fairly good shape,” he said.

Leo, 71, had a cancerous tumor and part of his right lung removed in an operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital on October 13.

He was discharged on October 17 and doctors quoted by the Vatican have said he is fit to travel and does not require any further therapy.

Asked by reporters if he had advice for people facing a cancer diagnosis, he said: “Not to be afraid.

“Early detection is obviously the best way to go and so regular check-ups are a blessing. And take care of yourselves,” he said.

Leo was also asked if he had resumed playing tennis — a favorite sport. “Not yet, but I will,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Malami’s aide condemns demolition of ADC support group’s office
World.content:
A media aide to former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, SAN, has condemned the demolition of the headquarters of the Malami Pressure Group (MPG) in Birnin Kebbi, describing the action as an assault on democratic freedoms and political association.

Mohammed Bello Doka, Special Assistant on Media to Malami, alleged that a suspected agency of the Kebbi State Government carried out the demolition on October 30, 2026, a day before the scheduled inauguration of the facility.

In a statement dated November 1, Doka said the property belonged to Malami, who had donated it to the MPG, an ADC-affiliated youth support organisation, to serve as its headquarters ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He said the facility was demolished without prior communication, formal notice or warning, before it could officially commence operations.

Doka described the incident as unacceptable in a constitutional democracy, arguing that it raised concerns about citizens’ rights to own property, associate freely, express political opinions and participate in the democratic process.

He questioned the authority behind the demolition, demanding to know which government agency carried out the operation, whether a formal notice was served on the property owner and whether a court order or established administrative procedure authorised the action.

He urged the Kebbi State Government to provide a clear explanation of the circumstances surrounding the demolition.

Citing the 1999 Constitution, Doka said Sections 39 and 40 guarantee freedom of expression and association, while Sections 43 and 44 provide for property ownership and protection against compulsory acquisition except in accordance with the law.

He acknowledged that governments had the authority to enforce planning regulations and building standards but insisted that such powers must be exercised transparently and in accordance with due process.

According to him, the timing of the demolition, with the 2027 general elections approaching, raised concerns about the political environment in which opposition parties and their supporters were expected to operate.

He argued that democracy required political competition, freedom of association and protection of dissent, adding that citizens should be able to establish political offices and organise meetings without fear of arbitrary interference.

Doka also questioned the state’s governance priorities, drawing attention to poverty, malnutrition, food insecurity and insecurity confronting residents of Kebbi.

Citing the National Bureau of Statistics’ 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index, he said Kebbi recorded a poverty incidence of 82.2 per cent, compared with the national average of 63 per cent.

He further cited the report’s estimate that more than 95 per cent of children under five in the state were multidimensionally poor, representing approximately 820,000 children.

On malnutrition, Doka referenced a Premium Times investigation published on January 23, 2026, which, according to him, reported that 608 severely malnourished children died between January and September 2025 across 21 treatment centres in five local government areas.

He said the figures underscored the need for urgent government attention to nutrition programmes and access to healthcare.

Doka also cited the October 2026 Cadre Harmonisé food-security assessment, which projected that 969,245 people in Kebbi would face crisis-level food insecurity between October and December 2026, with the figure expected to rise to 1,196,830 during the June-August 2027 lean season.

On insecurity, he referenced a January 2026 assessment by the European Union Agency for Asylum, drawing on data from the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, which documented 70 security incidents and 156 associated fatalities in Kebbi between January 2024 and August 2025.

He also referred to attacks and reprisals in Besse and Shanga local government areas in October 2026, saying conflicting media reports put the combined death toll at between 10 and 12.

Doka, however, clarified that he was not suggesting that the demolition caused the state’s socioeconomic challenges but said the incident raised broader questions about governance priorities, institutional accountability and the protection of citizens’ rights.

He also invoked the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, saying it recognised freedom of expression, association and property rights as essential components of democratic governance.

The media aide called on the Kebbi State Government to identify the agency responsible for the demolition, disclose the legal authority for the operation and make relevant notices, enforcement documents or court orders available for public scrutiny.

He further urged the Nigeria Police Force, the National Human Rights Commission and other relevant authorities to examine any formal complaints and ensure that the rights of those affected were protected.

Doka said the matter went beyond Malami, the ADC or the MPG, insisting that it concerned the constitutional rights of all Nigerians, irrespective of their political affiliations.

He maintained that peaceful political mobilisation should not be treated as a threat to government authority and called for accountability over the demolition.

World.title: 2027: Atiku’s aide tackles Keyamo over exclusion from ballot
World.content:
Festus Keyamo

An aide to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has criticised the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, over his remarks that the heavens would not fall if Atiku was excluded from the 2027 presidential ballot.

Ibe, who described Keyamo’s position as an attempt to undermine Nigerians’ democratic rights, said excluding a major political challenger would erode public confidence in the electoral process.

He stated this in a Facebook post while reacting to Keyamo’s comments on the possibility of Atiku not participating in the 2027 presidential election.

Ibe argued that the exclusion of a major challenger should not be treated as inconsequential, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to decide their preferred presidential candidate through the ballot.

“When a ruling party treats the exclusion of a major challenger as inconsequential, it is asking Nigerians to accept that their choice is inconsequential too. That is how you erode public faith in democracy,” he said.

Challenging Keyamo, Ibe asked why the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would welcome the prospect of an election without Atiku if it was confident in President Bola Tinubu’s performance.

He insisted that Tinubu should be allowed to defend his record before Nigerians, while Atiku should also be given the opportunity to present his case to the electorate.

Ibe expressed confidence that Atiku would secure widespread support in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, saying the former vice president’s supporters were prepared to translate their support into votes.

“On 16 January 2027, we intend to turn the support Nigerians have shown Atiku into votes and those votes into a mandate. If Nigerians send Tinubu packing at the ballot box, it will be political hell for an APC that has grown accustomed to taking them for granted,” he said.

The former vice president’s aide also invoked an Igbo proverb to caution Keyamo and the APC against disregarding the wishes of voters.

He quoted the saying, “A gwa ntị okwu, ntị anụghị, e gburu isi, e gburu ya na ntị,” which he translated to mean that when the ear refuses to heed counsel, it shares the fate of the head when it is lost.

According to him, a political party that refuses to listen to voters should be prepared for their response on election day.

Ibe further vowed that Atiku’s supporters would defend their right to choose their preferred candidate through all lawful means and exercise that right at the polls.

He, however, ended his post with a sharp personal attack on Keyamo, saying the minister and his supporters belonged in hell.

World.title: Grid ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​​​‍‍‍⁠‌​instability not responsible for IE Band A outage — TCN
World.content:
The management of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) on Friday said grid instability was not responsible for the Ikeja Electric (IE) Band A outage reported by the company on Nov. 3 and Nov. 4.

Ms. Ndidi Mba, the General Manager of the Corporate Communication Unit of TCN, disclosed this in a statement in Lagos.

According to her, TCN described the attribution as inaccurate and misleading, saying that the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid was not the responsibility of a Distribution Company (DisCo).

“By virtue of Section 67 of the Electricity Act 2023, the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid falls exclusively within the defined functions of the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO).

“IE, like every other market participant, has no authority to make such determinations, and NISO has made no such attribution of the outages in IE’s notice to TCN,” she said.

Mba said that NISO had already explained the situation, attributing the current decline in power generation to gas supply constraints to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower reservoir inflows.

She said that the reduced generation had affected the energy allocated to DisCos, resulting in fewer hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks.

“The impact on each DisCo varies with available generation and its allocation,” she said.

Mba said that the shortfall in electricity supply to IE’s customers was a consequence of reduced generation and the resulting allocation, not any failure of TCN’s transmission network.

“TCN can only transmit the energy made available to it and cannot transmit energy that is not generated.

“The records for all feeders supplying IE confirm the national picture NISO described.

“Of the interruptions recorded on Nov. 1 and 2, 68 percent were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation.

“A further 26 percent were due to IE’s non-compliance with load allocation by the National Control Centre (NCC) of NISO or to faults and works on IKEDC’s own network.

“The remaining six percent were TCN planned maintenance, switching, or a line limitation. None of the recorded interruptions was a TCN equipment fault or trip,” she said.

According to her, the feeders listed in IE’s notice also did not support the company’s claim.

“Of the 46 interruptions recorded on the 33kV feeders named in the notice, 29 were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation, while 14 were recorded against IKEDC.

“Nine were for non-compliance with load allocation, and five for faults or trips on its own network. The other three were scheduled TCN maintenance on the Ogba-Alimosho line on Nov. 1.”

Mba said that on Nov. 2, the Rack Centre feeder was interrupted by a cable fault on IE’s network, which its crew repaired.

“IE’s notice itself assigns several of these feeders, including MTN, Iju Water Works, and Rack Centre, to IE for 33 kV faults,” she said.

She said that IE’s position was therefore inconsistent with the actual situation in the Nigerian electricity supply industry.

Mba said that attributing shortfalls caused by generation constraints to TCN could misinform customers, undermine public confidence, and obscure the challenges requiring collective efforts by stakeholders.

TCN urged IE and other DisCos to desist from making unfounded claims about the causes of electricity supply shortfalls to their customers.

“DisCos should communicate based on verified information from NISO, the body responsible for the operation of the grid,” she said.

She urged electricity customers to refer to NISO’s official platforms for accurate information on the state of the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry.

MBA said that TCN sympathized with customers affected by the reduced hours of electricity supply.

“It remains committed to transmitting all available energy safely, reliably, and efficiently within the prevailing operational constraints, and to working with NISO, generation companies, and DisCos to improve the situation,” she said. (NAN)

World.title: APGA ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌⁠⁠⁠⁠‍⁠‍‌​adopts Tinubu as presidential candidate, targets 50% votes in Anambra
World.content:
The All Progressive Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu, the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), as its presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections.

The governor of Anambra, Prof. Charles Soludo, and the national leader, APGA, made this known on Friday in Awka during the inauguration of APGA’s national campaign for the 2027 general elections.

“APGA has no presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections and will, therefore, adopt President Tinubu as its preferred candidate.

“Today, we adopt the APC Presidential candidate, Bola Tinubu, as our candidate,” he said.

Soludo said that Tinubu had demonstrated love and concern for the Igbo people, particularly the people of Anambra.

He also recalled that Tinubu had appointed several Anambra indigenes to strategic positions in Lagos state during his tenure as governor.

‘’APGA had adopted the presidential candidate of the ruling party in previous elections; therefore, the party’s decision to support Tinubu in the 2027 general elections is a continuation of that political arrangement,” he said.

The governor insisted that Tinubu was the only presidential candidate of the party come 2027 general elections.

“We don’t have a presidential candidate; Tinubu is our candidate,” he said.

He further recalled that the state recorded about 5,000 votes for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election.

‘’Yet, the president has continued to address some of the challenges confronting the state and the Southeast region.

“We gave him only about 5,000 votes, and yet he is doing wonderful works in the state,” he said.

Soludo urged people of the state to support Tinubu in the 2027 election.

According to him, doing so will give the state and the Southeast a stronger opportunity to engage with the Federal Government and negotiate for their development.

The governor declared his intention to deliver 50 percent of the state’s votes to Tinubu, the presidential candidate of the APC, in the 2027 general elections.

“We need to vote for him in order to sit with the government at the center and negotiate for the development of the Southeast and Anambra.

“We are targeting 50 percent for the president,” he said. (NAN)

World.title: Military force alone cannot defeat terrorism – Buratai
World.content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai (retd.), has said that military force alone cannot defeat terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need to address poverty, unemployment, poor governance and other socio-economic factors fuelling insecurity.

Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions.

The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons.



“Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. It can create the conditions for peace, but it cannot by itself build peace.

“It can degrade a terrorist group; it cannot alone remove the grievances of poverty, ignorance and manipulation from which such groups recruit,” he said.

Buratai emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and community participation in counter-insurgency operations, describing local communities as indispensable partners in the fight against terrorism.

According to him, security agencies cannot achieve meaningful results without the confidence and cooperation of the communities they are deployed to protect.

“No amount of firepower can compensate for poor intelligence. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated.

He also warned that human rights violations during military operations could alienate local communities and provide terrorist organisations with propaganda materials to attract new recruits.

Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms.

He called for stronger counter-terrorism capacity within the Nigeria Police Force, arguing that the military should not continue to shoulder responsibilities traditionally assigned to civilian security institutions.

“The military is not the police; it is not the social welfare agency; it is not the school system. When the military is deployed to perform tasks that belong to civil authorities, it becomes overstretched, and the roots of the conflict remain untouched,” he said.

On the rehabilitation and reintegration of former terrorists, the retired general supported credible deradicalisation programmes but insisted that such initiatives must not undermine justice for victims of terrorism.

He said rehabilitation efforts must be transparent, properly monitored and community-based, adding that affected communities needed assurances that justice had been served.

Drawing from his experience as commander of the Multinational Joint Task Force headquartered in N’Djamena, Chad, Buratai advocated stronger regional security cooperation, noting that terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram and its affiliates, operated across national boundaries.

He urged Nigeria to strengthen collaboration with neighbouring countries and regional institutions, including the Economic Community of West African States, African Union and countries within the Lake Chad Basin.

The former army chief also supported the recommendation for a state of emergency on poverty in Northern Nigeria, saying the initiative should prioritise out-of-school children, the Almajiri system, youth unemployment, vocational training and social protection.

He, however, cautioned that poverty alleviation programmes must be transparent and protected against elite capture.

“Poverty is not an excuse for terrorism, but it is a fertile ground for recruitment and manipulation. We must treat it with the seriousness it deserves,” he said.

Citing findings from the book, Buratai said field surveys conducted across Adamawa, Borno, Yobe, Kano, Kebbi, Kogi, Niger and the Federal Capital Territory showed that 86 per cent of respondents believed negotiation could be helpful in addressing terrorism, while 92 per cent agreed that community members could contribute significantly to intelligence gathering.

He added that 84 per cent of respondents linked terrorist recruitment to poor economic conditions and the Almajiri situation.

Earlier, the author, Dr. Joan Ugo Mbagwu, a Professor of Peace, Criminology and Security Studies at Chrisland University, Abeokuta, Ogun State, said the book was conceived to broaden national understanding of counter-terrorism beyond the conventional reliance on military force.

Mbagwu, who disclosed that she had conducted research for the Ford Foundation and the Institute for Development Studies, also served as a Process Evaluator for the United Nations Peacebuilding Fund in Africa.

The book was formally unveiled by retired Major General R.O. Yusuf, while the Chairman of the occasion, Olubunmi Ajala, commended Buratai for his commitment to security-related issues.

An award of appreciation was also presented to the former army chief in recognition of his contributions to combating terrorism during his tenure.

World.title: 2027: ADC appeals Lifu’s judgment, asks INEC to suspend action
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has appealed the Federal High Court judgment in favour of Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe and asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to suspend action on the ruling pending the determination of the appeal.

The party made the request in a letter dated November 6, 2026, addressed to the INEC Chairman and marked for the attention of the Director of Legal Services.

The letter, which was signed by the ADC’s counsel, Shaibu Enejoh Aruwa, SAN, of S. E. Aruwa, SAN & Co., was received at the Office of the INEC Chairman on November 6.

Titled, “Notice of Pendency of Notice of Appeal and Application for Stay of Execution of the Judgment of Federal High Court, Abuja Division, Delivered on the 5th November, 2026,” the letter informed the Commission that the party had filed a notice of appeal against the judgment delivered on November 5.

According to Aruwa, the ADC was dissatisfied with the decision of the court and had consequently approached the Court of Appeal to challenge it.

A copy of the notice of appeal, dated November 6, was attached to the letter as Annexure A.

The party also disclosed that it had filed a Motion on Notice at the Federal High Court, seeking a stay of execution of the judgment pending the hearing and determination of its appeal.

A copy of the motion, also dated November 6, was attached as Annexure B.

The suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1619/2025, is titled Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe v. African Democratic Congress (ADC) and four others, with the ADC listed as the first defendant.

The party further informed INEC that Bala Gombe was aware of both the appeal and the application for a stay of execution.

“We therefore, write to bring to your attention that the Plaintiff (Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe) is aware of the appeal filed

World.title: Gas Eruption: CSOs Demand National Emergency in Rivers Community
World.content:
. Raise alarm over alleged 11 deaths

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

A coalition of civil society organisations under the platform of The People’s Assembly has called on President Bola Tinubu to declare a national environmental and public health emergency in Bille Kingdom, Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State, following persistent gas eruptions in the area.

The coalition alleged that the eruption which is still on as at the time of this report has allegedly claimed 11 lives and exposed residents to serious health risks.

The coalition also demanded the immediate relocation of residents to safer locations, emergency medical intervention and the release of funds to identify and contain the source of the gas leak, which has continued to bubble from creeks, boreholes, hand-dug wells, school grounds and residential compounds.

Speaking at a press conference organised by The People’s Assembly in Port Harcourt on Thursday, the Executive Director of Kebetkache Women Development and Resource Centre and co-convener of the Assembly, Dr Emem Okon, described the situation as a looming humanitarian disaster requiring urgent federal intervention.

Okon warned that continued government inaction could result in further loss of lives, stressing that the people of Bille should not be abandoned to face a potentially catastrophic environmental crisis.

She said, “This is a national emergency that cannot wait. Gas has been bubbling from the ground and water in Bille for about a year, contaminating the air and threatening the lives of residents. Families can no longer safely cook, drink their water or depend on fishing for their livelihoods.”

According to the coalition, the gas eruption, which reportedly began around October 2025, has resulted in repeated fires and explosions, with 11 deaths associated with the crisis and several residents reportedly suffering from vomiting, breathing difficulties and other illnesses.

The group said independent monitoring had detected unsafe levels of methane, hydrogen sulphide and carbon dioxide in the community, raising concerns about the potential consequences of prolonged exposure.

It noted that the crisis had disrupted economic and social activities, particularly fishing, while the contamination of water sources and the rising cost of living had worsened poverty among residents.

The coalition’s concerns were contained in an open letter addressed to President Tinubu, the President of the Senate, the Ministers of Health and Environment, and the Director-General of the National Emergency Management Agency, among other federal authorities.

The letter, issued by The People’s Assembly and Bille Working Group, a coalition convened by Social Action and its partners, called for the establishment of a presidential task force to investigate and resolve the crisis.

The group expressed concern that despite joint investigation visits by the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency and the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the source of the gas eruption remained unidentified.

It also alleged that NOSDRA lacked adequate funding to undertake further investigations, mitigation and remediation.

The coalition disclosed that during a meeting with NOSDRA Director-General, Chief Chukwuemeka Woke, on October 17, 2026, the agency acknowledged the financial constraints affecting its response.

It further demanded the immediate publication of preliminary soil and water test results conducted by the regulatory agencies, insisting that residents had a right to know the substances contaminating their environment.

Dr Prince Edegbuo of Social Action, said the Federal Government must move beyond investigations and take decisive steps to protect the people.

He demanded the temporary relocation of residents, provision of safe shelters, clean drinking water, food and healthcare, pending independent confirmation that the community was safe for habitation.

The coalition also called for emergency funding for NOSDRA, activation of the regional Spill Command Centre and access to the Upstream Remediation Fund to address the crisis.

It urged the government to deploy fingerprinting technology to identify the source of the gas, audit active, idle and abandoned oil wells, pipelines and facilities within Oil Mining Leases 18 and 24, and temporarily suspend oil and gas operations in the affected areas until the source was identified and contained.

Meanwhile, Kentebe Ebiaridor of Oilwatch International called for stronger accountability in the oil and gas sector, warning against the growing practice of international oil companies selling their onshore assets without adequately addressing outstanding environmental liabilities.

The coalition also demanded that current and former operators of OMLs 18 and 24 be held jointly and severally liable pending the identification of the source of the gas eruption, with affected residents adequately compensated.

As part of its wider environmental justice campaign, The People’s Assembly announced the launch of its ‘No Clean-Up, No Vote’ campaign across the Niger Delta.

Edegbuo said the campaign would mobilise residents to demand clear, funded and time-bound environmental remediation plans from political parties and candidates ahead of future elections.

He said, “The Niger Delta has fed this country for over seven decades and has lost so much in return. Its people have waited long enough for promises to become action.

“Our message to every political party and candidate is simple: the people of the Niger Delta will support those who present clear and credible plans to clean up polluted communities, protect public health and hold oil companies accountable. Where there is no clean-up, there will be no vote.”

The coalition warned that the Bille crisis could become a national security emergency if left unresolved, urging the Federal Government to treat it as a priority rather than another environmental investigation.

It said resolving the crisis would also provide a framework for addressing similar environmental emergencies in communities such as Uzere, Alakiri, Rumuekpe and Aleto across the Niger Delta.

World.title: Nigeria’s MFM Girls Remain Unbeaten at FIBA Africa Women’s Basketball League Zone 3 Qualifiers in Abidjan
World.content:
Mountain of Fire and Miracles Ministries (MFM) Women Basketball Club put on a basketball clinic in Monrovia on Thursday night at the Samuel Doe Stadium, dismantling the hosts team, Flames Female Basketball Club by 77–46 points in a commanding performance at the ongoing 2026 FIBA Africa Women Basketball League Zone 3 Qualifiers.

The Nigerian champions dominated from the opening tip, sweeping all four quarters to secure an emphatic 31-point svictory and signal their clear intent on the road to the WBLA main tournament.

Folashade Olukoya Queens as they’re fondly called set the tone early in the opening quarter, executing their half-court offense with precision to jump out to a 20–11 points lead. The Queens turned up the defensive intensity in the middle quarters, completely stifling Flames Female’s backcourt. The 3 times league champions restricted Flames to just 8 points in the second quarter and 7 in the third, effectively putting the game out of reach before the final period even began. The Liberian team found some offensive rhythm late in the fourth quarter with 20 points, but MFM’s offense answered right back with 25 of their own to close out the 77–46 wire-to-wire victory.

The church girls who won the Nigerian league without a defeat, was powered by a relentless effort from captain Ukamaka Okoh who bagged a team high 13points, 2 rebounds and 1 assists, veteran forward Regina Iornumbe added 10 points and a team high 6 steals while Marvis Hembam contributed 9 points with 9 assists with Dalphne Olugbagho and Yakhira Buzugbe both contributing 7points each.

The win makes it 2 wins in 2 matches after their 59-36 points win over Nigerian rivals First Bank basketball club in their opening game of the FIBA Zone 3 Qualifiers and a push for a place in the FIBA Africa Women’s Basketball League final tournament in Cairo from 11- 20 December, 2026.

World.title: NDLEA Arraigns Two Mexicans, Four Nigerians over Oyo Methamphetamine Laboratory
World.content:
*Court remands suspects in correctional centre, fixes trial for January

Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arraigned two Mexican nationals and four Nigerians over their alleged involvement in the establishment and operation of a clandestine methamphetamine laboratory in a forest in Tapa village, Ibarapa North Local Government Area of Oyo State.

The six defendants were arraigned before Justice Nkeonye Evelyn Maha of the Federal High Court, Ibadan, on a four-count charge bordering on conspiracy, establishment of an illicit drug laboratory and the unlawful handling of chemicals for the production of methamphetamine.

The defendants are Mexican nationals Jose Villa Ochoa, 56, and Carrera Loaiza Arturo, 40, alongside four Nigerians identified as Maxwell Uche Nevoh, 30; Olatunji Yusuf, 37; Bankole Akeem Owolabi, 45; and Ganiu Monsiu, 43.

According to a statement by NDLEA’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Mr Femi Babafemi, on Friday, Villa Ochoa and the four Nigerians were arrested on June 17, 2026, by operatives of the agency in a forested area of Tapa village.

Arturo was subsequently tracked and arrested on August 19 while allegedly attempting to flee the country through the Lagos airport.

The charge alleged that the defendants conspired to operate a drug trafficking organisation and established a clandestine laboratory for the production of methamphetamine between December 2025 and June 2026 at different locations in Lagos and Oyo States.

They were also accused of unlawfully transporting and distributing chemical substances intended for the manufacture of the psychotropic drug, contrary to Section 20(1)(f) and punishable under Section 20(2)(a) of the NDLEA Act.

All six defendants pleaded not guilty after the charges were read to them in a language they understood.

Following their pleas, Justice Maha ordered their remand at the Correctional Centre in Ibadan and adjourned the case until January 26, 27, 28 and 29, 2027, for trial.

The Oyo operation is coming months after NDLEA operatives arrested three other Mexican nationals and seven Nigerian collaborators over the alleged establishment of a similar methamphetamine laboratory in a forest hideout in Ogun State.

The 10 defendants in the Ogun case were also arraigned before a Federal High Court in Lagos, where their bail application was rejected and the court ordered an accelerated hearing.

The agency said the two operations involved foreign nationals and Nigerian collaborators allegedly linked to clandestine methamphetamine production facilities in forest locations in the South-West.

World.title: EFCC Recovers N1.233 Trillion, Secures 10,872 Convictions in 34 Months
World.content:
*As Commission Tracks Down Foreign Nationals Operating Illegal Refinery in South-West

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has recovered over N1.233 trillion, alongside an unspecified amount of foreign currency, the Commission’s spokesperson, Dele Oyewale, has said.

He added that the Commission had also secured 10,872 convictions within the same period.

Speaking at a joint press conference by spokespersons of the Armed Forces of Nigeria and other security agencies in Abuja, Oyewale said the landmark recoveries covered a 34-month period, from October 1, 2023, to July 31, 2026, under the leadership of Executive Chairman Ola Olukoyede.

He also confirmed the discovery of an illegal refinery in the South-West and the arrest of foreign nationals in connection with illegal lithium processing plants.

He said: “I can confirm that we uncovered the facility. You will recall that on October 23, we arrested 14 Chinese nationals and a Nigerian along the same axis for allegedly operating illegal lithium processing plants.

“The earlier arrests and subsequent investigations made it difficult to immediately apprehend the operators of the illegal refinery, as the activities were taking place within the same operational area.

“We subsequently returned to the location as part of our expanded investigation to establish whether the illegal activities were still ongoing. However, when we arrived, nobody was present at the facility.

“We discovered the refinery and its equipment, but no arrests were made during that operation. Our investigations are still ongoing.”

World.title: NAF Recovers Cockpit Voice Recorder from Crashed ATR-42 Aircraft
World.content:
*As recovery, investigation continue in Igbokoda

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has recorded further progress in the recovery and investigation of the ATR-42 aircraft accident in Igbokoda, Ondo State, with the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), which technical teams from the NAF and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) have confirmed to be intact.

Part of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), commonly referred to as the black box, was also recovered, while efforts to locate and retrieve the remaining portion are ongoing.

According to a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, additional aircraft wreckage, engine components and human remains have also been recovered.

“Operations are ongoing in the challenging swamp terrain, with teams working to retrieve outstanding components and facilitate the necessary technical examinations. The investigation is being conducted with due diligence to ensure comprehensive, evidence-based findings.

“The recovery process also involves careful attention to the proper handling of human remains, with the Directorate of Identification and Classification (DIC) undertaking the necessary procedures for their proper identification,” the statement said.

Ejodame said the NAF had maintained engagement with the families of the victims, recognising their need for information and support.

“Engagement with relevant authorities on environmental concerns raised by the host community also remains an important part of the broader response,” he said.

While acknowledging the public’s concern and interest, the NAF appealed for continued patience and understanding, noting that these critical processes require time, careful coordination and professional attention.

He said the ultimate objective was not only to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident but also to draw the necessary lessons to strengthen flight safety, enhance ongoing air power operations and further safeguard the lives of personnel and citizens.

World.title: Miva Wins International Award for Technology-Driven Education
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

Miva Open University, a subsidiary of uLesson Group, has won an international award recognising its use of technology to expand access to higher education.

The university received the Excellence in Accessible Higher Education 2026 award from Global Brands Magazine, following an assessment of organisations across different industries and countries.

The recognition, announced on November 4, 2026, was part of the 14th edition of the Global Brands Magazine Awards, which honours organisations for their performance, innovation, service delivery and leadership.

According to the awarding organisation, nominees in the education category were assessed on criteria including innovation, quality, branding, customer service and overall performance, with Miva emerging as the winner.

The award highlights the role of flexible, technology-enabled learning in widening access to university education, particularly for people seeking alternatives to conventional classroom-based programmes.

Through its open and distance learning model, Miva offers undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications, combining digital learning with academic support to provide students with a structured but flexible route to higher education.

Commenting on the recognition, Chief Executive Officer of uLesson Group, Iheanyi Akwiwu, said the award reflected the institution’s efforts to make quality higher education more accessible through innovative learning experiences.
