“We are pleased to be recognised by Global Brands Magazine for our contribution to expanding access to quality higher education. This recognition reflects our commitment to delivering innovative learning experiences that respond to the needs of today’s learners,” he said.

He added that the university would continue to strengthen its education model and create more opportunities for people to pursue their academic and professional ambitions.

The Global Brands Magazine Awards is an annual programme that recognises organisations for their performance across different sectors globally. Miva’s 2026 award places it among the organisations recognised for their contributions to Nigeria’s education sector.

World.title: BCA Targets Africa’s Media Infrastructure Gap with Mauritius Hub
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

Africa’s growing film, music and television industries are generating increasing demand for professional production and broadcasting services, but a shortage of technical infrastructure is forcing media companies to outsource critical operations to Europe and the Middle East, limiting the continent’s ability to retain the economic value of its creative output.

Broadcasting Center Africa is seeking to address the gap through a media infrastructure hub in Mauritius, bringing together television studios, post-production facilities, broadcasting operations, engineering services and a secure data centre to serve African and international media organisations.

The proposed facility, expected to open in 2029, will form the technical core of MediaCity Mauritius, a wider development designed to accommodate production companies, broadcasters, technology firms, academic institutions, training centres, start-ups and international investors.

Chief Executive Officer of BCA and MediaCity Mauritius, Najib Gouiaa, disclosed this in an interview at the 2026 Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, organised by the African Export-Import Bank in Lagos from November 5 to 8.

BCA shared a stand at the event with its European partner, Broadcasting Center Europe, and MediaCity Mauritius to present the project to producers, broadcasters, streaming platforms, telecommunications operators, investors and other participants in Africa’s creative industries.

Gouiaa said the continent had the creative talent, audiences and international demand to support a thriving media industry, but lacked the technical infrastructure required to turn creative productions into sustainable businesses.

He argued that the problem was not a shortage of creative capacity but the absence of an integrated production and distribution ecosystem, leaving companies to depend on foreign facilities for several stages of their operations.

“The talent is there, and so are the audiences and the demand. What’s missing is the technical chain that turns creative work into a lasting business. African creative projects do not fail because of a lack of talent but because the support around them doesn’t exist. People work in isolation, skills are scattered, and at every stage some of the value leaves the continent,” he said.

According to him, the economic value lost goes beyond the cost of outsourcing production services, extending to employment, technical expertise, professional development and commercial opportunities associated with the media value chain.

He explained that a production shot in Africa could still depend on facilities in Europe for editing and post-production, while the television channel transmitting it might be operated from Dubai. Its archives could be stored in Europe, with the supporting data hosted outside the continent.

“Those are the stages where the margins, the jobs and the careers are, and they’re being exported just as demand for African capacity is taking off,” Gouiaa said.

He added that international media groups with Africa-focused operations also tended to locate their departments in Dubai, London or Paris rather than on the continent because of concerns about infrastructure reliability, operational risks and the availability of personnel trained to international standards.

He said the appetite for establishing more operations in Africa existed, but companies needed assurances that they could access reliable facilities, manage risks and recruit appropriately trained teams.

According to him, bringing those operations closer to the African markets they serve would be in the commercial interest of international media groups, provided the necessary infrastructure and operational guarantees were available.

Gouiaa said BCA’s approach was informed by media infrastructure models in international markets, particularly Dubai Media City, MediaCityUK and RTL City in Luxembourg, where production companies, broadcasters, technical operators and training institutions operate within integrated developments.

He said the model allowed businesses to share infrastructure, access specialised services and work more closely with other players in the industry rather than operating independently.

“The places that succeed are the ones that put everything on one site. A studio with no post-production, a broadcast centre with no producers nearby, a media school with no equipment to train on: each of these struggles on its own. Put them together and they feed each other,” he said.

Under the proposed arrangement, BCA will provide the technical services supporting media production, broadcasting, content management and distribution, while MediaCity Mauritius will provide the wider business and institutional environment.

The BCA facility will house television studios and their control rooms, facilities for live and recorded production, post-production suites, a master control room, satellite and internet links, engineering laboratories and an auditorium.

It will also have a secure data centre certified to the international ISO 27001 standard, allowing content to be hosted, stored and archived in Africa.

The building is being purpose-built by MediaCity Mauritius to specifications developed with BCE and is scheduled to open in 2029.

Gouiaa described BCA as a one-stop technical service centre for African and international media and creative companies, handling operations from production to final delivery.

He said the company would operate to the standards of major European media groups, providing clients with access to technical capacity without requiring them to acquire and maintain all the necessary equipment themselves.

Explaining the company’s business model, he said media organisations would purchase operational capacity under service agreements with guaranteed service levels rather than invest heavily in infrastructure, equipment and technical personnel.

“Because our clients don’t buy equipment. They buy capacity, under a contract with guaranteed service levels, backed by teams working around the clock and equipment we maintain and replace. That turns a heavy upfront investment into a predictable running cost,” he said.

He said the arrangement would enable clients to launch television channels within six months instead of 18 months, maintain broadcasting operations through managed backup systems and expand into new markets, languages and platforms without building new infrastructure from scratch.

Gouiaa said the model reflected the approach adopted by major European media service providers, which had increasingly moved complex technical operations to specialist service centres.

He identified six categories of potential customers for BCA, including international television channels, African public and private broadcasters, telecommunications and mobile operators, sports rights holders, content producers and advertising agencies, as well as international media groups seeking an operational base in Africa.

For international channels seeking to establish an Africa-ready feed without recruiting a local operations team, BCA plans to provide a 180-day channel launch kit.

African broadcasters needing to keep their channels on air while modernising their operations will have access to managed disaster recovery services.

Telecommunications and mobile operators expanding into video services will be able to use a video operations laboratory, while sports rights holders will have access to a live operations package for converting sporting events into live and near-live content across different platforms.

Producers and advertising agencies will be offered a supply-chain sprint designed to move productions from the production stage to distribution.

International media groups seeking to establish an Africa-facing base will also have access to a market-entry package combining managed services and access to the company’s data centre.

Gouiaa said the increasing complexity of the media industry had made it difficult for individual broadcasters, telecommunications operators and content owners to manage every aspect of their operations internally.

He listed traditional broadcasting, streaming applications, free ad-supported channels, video-on-demand services, targeted advertising, multilingual content versions, rights management, live events and distribution across multiple platforms as activities requiring specialised technical capabilities.

He said organisations also needed to maintain round-the-clock operations while managing the cost of equipment, personnel and infrastructure.

On the growth of Africa’s digital content market, Gouiaa said more than 560 streaming services now operated across the continent, while Afrobeats and Amapiano had helped make African music one of the fastest-growing creative sectors globally.

However, he said 97 per cent of streaming content consumed in Africa was imported, illustrating the disparity between the continent’s growing appetite for digital content and its capacity to produce, finish and distribute it.

He argued that establishing more streaming platforms alone would not address the underlying problem, as the industry needed the technical infrastructure and specialist services required to support content across different distribution channels.

Gouiaa also identified music as one of the most dynamic but least equipped segments of Africa’s creative industry.

He said African artists and record labels had gained international recognition through global streaming platforms but remained constrained by inadequate facilities for recording, filming, editing and managing the rights to their work at broadcast quality.

According to him, concerts, live sessions and festivals require specialised infrastructure to capture performances, mix the recordings, archive the content and convert them into commercial products.

He said BCA intended to support this segment alongside the production companies, event spaces and training campus planned for MediaCity Mauritius.

BCE partnership and skills development

A central part of the project is its partnership with Broadcasting Center Europe, the technical operator of RTL Group, which will provide the technology, operational expertise and training required to establish BCA’s operations.

Gouiaa said BCE had spent 25 years managing critical broadcasting operations, had teams in seven countries and served more than 400 clients, including RTL, Radio France, Arte and France Télévisions.

The European company also has experience in Africa and the Indian Ocean, having moved Ethiopia’s public broadcaster, Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation, into new facilities incorporating studios, a data centre and broadcasting systems. It also carried out the complete modernisation of Antenne Réunion.

He said the partnership would allow BCA to adopt established European broadcasting systems and operational procedures while developing the capacity to serve African markets.

BCA will initially operate from BCE’s facilities at RTL City in Luxembourg for three years before transferring its operations to Mauritius.

Gouiaa said the arrangement was designed to allow the company to establish its business, serve its first customers, train personnel and test its infrastructure on actual productions before the Mauritius hub opens.

Under the plan, the equipment will be transferred to Mauritius, certified teams will follow, and the company expects to have its first clients already on board.

He said the strategy was intended to reduce the delivery risks associated with major infrastructure projects by testing the operational model before the permanent facility was completed.

BCE will provide three main components for the project: technology, operational expertise and professional training.

The technology component will cover the facility’s design, broadcasting and internet protocol systems, as well as equipment selection and procurement based on the standards of a major European operator.

The operational component will involve transferring the expertise required to manage round-the-clock broadcasting, maintain service continuity, respond to technical incidents, control quality and secure content.

Gouiaa said the training component would ensure that BCA’s personnel could operate the systems to BCE’s standards from the beginning.

He said the company planned to train 160 young Africans at BCE’s facilities in Luxembourg, where they would learn using the same equipment expected to be installed in Mauritius.

The engineers, technicians and operators recruited by BCA would gain practical experience working on actual productions and obtain professional certification rather than rely solely on classroom instruction.

Gouiaa said the objective was to have the personnel acquire three years of experience before the Mauritius facility opens, creating a pool of African specialists with international exposure.

He described professionalisation as a cornerstone of the project, arguing that the development of technical skills was essential to building a sustainable media industry on the continent.

BCE will remain involved after the transfer as BCA’s supervisory and support partner under a formal services and strategic partnership agreement.

The agreement includes contractual milestones covering systems integration, staff certification, ISO 27001 certification and the facility’s official opening.

Gouiaa said BCE’s expertise would also remain available on demand for clients requiring specialised design work, specific installations or day-to-day operational support.

MediaCity Mauritius and regional ambitions

Beyond the technical facilities, Gouiaa said the wider MediaCity Mauritius development would bring together content creators, media companies, technology businesses, academic institutions, training centres, start-ups and international investors.

He said locating BCA within the development would provide access to potential customers, shared infrastructure and a workforce trained in the technologies and standards used by the company.

He cited RTL City in Luxembourg as an example of how bringing broadcasting channels, content teams and technical operators together could improve collaboration and reduce the need for intermediaries.

According to him, having studios, control rooms, broadcast centres and newsrooms within the same development would allow businesses to work directly with one another.

He said companies operating within MediaCity Mauritius would become potential customers for BCA, while sharing infrastructure and specialist services would improve efficiency without compromising broadcasting standards.

The development’s academic partners would also help train personnel in the technologies and professional standards required by BCA.

Gouiaa added that events hosted at MediaCity would provide opportunities for the company to demonstrate its capabilities and attract new customers.

He said the development would become more valuable as additional tenants, partners and institutions joined it, strengthening the services available to businesses operating within the ecosystem.

On its customer acquisition strategy, Gouiaa said BCA was already in discussions with potential clients across the streaming, telecommunications, television broadcasting and content production industries.

The company has identified 30 organisations with pressing operational needs, budgets to address those needs and decision-makers it can reach.

He said the plan was to convert the discussions into paid assessments of the organisations’ operations and identify areas where BCA could improve their processes.

Those assessments would then lead to pilot projects, including channel launches, which the company could use as references to attract additional customers.

Gouiaa said BCA was targeting both African and international media organisations.

For African customers, the company would provide access to infrastructure they might not have the financial resources or technical capacity to build and operate independently.

For international companies seeking to produce content in Africa or work with local partners, BCA would offer an entry point into the market without requiring them to assume the full operational risks of establishing their own facilities.

He said the presence of offices, event spaces, business partners and skilled personnel within MediaCity Mauritius would provide additional benefits beyond the technical services available at the broadcasting centre.

Gouiaa said the company was also seeking to attract international media groups that currently managed their Africa-focused operations from outside the continent.

Why Mauritius?

Explaining the choice of Mauritius over other African media and business centres such as Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg, Gouiaa said the island offered a combination of political and business stability, international connectivity and multilingual capabilities.

He said Mauritius could serve French-, English- and Portuguese-speaking markets while providing a business environment familiar to international media organisations.

He cited guarantees for foreign ownership, exemptions from duties on technical equipment, production incentives and data protection legislation aligned with the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation as factors supporting the choice.

Gouiaa also pointed to Mauritius Telecom’s 2026–2029 strategy, which positions the country as a digital gateway between Africa and Asia through sovereign cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence and innovation corridors.

He said the MediaCity development would also help build a local pool of operators, editors, metadata specialists and broadcast support personnel.

According to him, the location would enable BCA to serve major business centres including Johannesburg, Nairobi, Paris, Dubai and Mumbai.

He said the project was aligned with the African Continental Free Trade Area’s Protocol on Digital Trade because shared production and distribution infrastructure could make it easier for African content businesses to operate across the continent’s 54 markets.

Gouiaa said Mauritius had signed the agreement and offered strong intellectual property protection, making it a suitable base for a business seeking to support cross-border content production and distribution.

He described BCA as the type of creative infrastructure investment that CANEX was established to support, arguing that such projects could attract financing while generating measurable returns through exports, industrial development and skills acquisition.

He said Afreximbank had identified infrastructure and skills shortages as major constraints facing Africa’s creative industries, adding that BCA was intended to contribute to addressing those challenges.

Looking beyond Mauritius, Gouiaa said the company’s long-term plan was to establish a model that could be replicated in other African countries from 2030.

He said the expansion would follow the successful establishment of the Mauritius operation, the acquisition of reference clients, the certification of personnel and the testing of operational procedures.

The next phase would involve regional growth and additional services led jointly by BCE and BCA.

However, he said the immediate priority remained establishing the Mauritius hub and demonstrating the viability of the business model.

Gouiaa said the message to African producers, broadcasters and record labels visiting the company’s stand at CANEX was that production and technical services they currently outsourced abroad would soon be available on the continent to the same standards.

He said the services would be delivered by African teams trained at BCE in Luxembourg and operating the same systems that would be installed in Mauritius.

He added that the project would provide a setting where media companies could produce content, train personnel, meet partners and conduct business.

For international media groups, he said BCA was offering the infrastructure, operational guarantees and technical partnership needed to move their Africa-facing operations closer to the markets they serve.

Najib Gouiaa is the initiator and Chief Executive Officer of Broadcasting Center Africa and MediaCity Mauritius. He has three decades of experience in international news and production, including 20 years in international news and a further 10 years working on media projects in the Middle East and Africa. He previously worked as a reporter and producer for international agencies and channels across Africa, the Middle East and Eastern Europe, served as head of news at an Africa-focused channel and consulted on media and creative projects in the Gulf.

World.title: NiDCOM Targets $100bn Annual Diaspora Investment, Announces November Summit
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM) has said Nigeria could attract up to $100 billion annually in diaspora investment if the financial, entrepreneurial and intellectual resources of Nigerians living abroad are effectively harnessed.

The Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NiDCOM, Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, stated this in Abuja while announcing the 9th Nigeria Diaspora Investment Summit (NDIS) 2026, scheduled for November 10 and 11.

Dabiri-Erewa, who was represented by the Acting Secretary of the commission, Hon. Abdurrahman Terab, said diaspora investment represented a major economic resource capable of accelerating Nigeria’s development and supporting the Federal Government’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy.

She said the diaspora community should be viewed not merely as a social group but as a strategic economic asset whose financial and professional capacities could transform critical sectors of the economy.

The summit, organised by NiDCOM in partnership with the Nigeria Diaspora Summit Initiative (NDSI), will be held under the theme, ‘Bridging the Trust Gap: Connecting Diaspora Capital with Credible Home-based Opportunities.’

According to her, the 2026 edition will adopt a hybrid format, combining virtual participation through Zoom with limited physical attendance at the Shehu Musa Yar’Adua Centre, Abuja.

She explained that the focus on trust and credible investment opportunities was informed by the need to address concerns that often discourage Nigerians abroad from investing in their home country.

Dabiri-Erewa said unlocking diaspora capital required more than showcasing investment opportunities, stressing the importance of transparency, investor protection, credible institutions, reliable information and effective regulatory frameworks.

She said the summit would provide prospective investors with direct access to government institutions, regulators, project sponsors and investment agencies to obtain practical guidance on investment procedures, compliance requirements and safeguards.

The two-day summit will feature discussions on capital market opportunities, infrastructure investment, regulatory frameworks and investor protection.

Dabiri-Erewa said the first day, November 10, would focus on Nigeria’s capital market, including available financial instruments, investment entry procedures, transparency measures, risk management and safeguards for diaspora investors.

Participating institutions are expected to include the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), alongside capital market operators and advisers.

She said the second day would focus on infrastructure opportunities and regulatory frameworks, including bankable projects, public-private partnerships and investment protection mechanisms.

Institutions expected to participate include the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Nigerian Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA), Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council (PEBEC) and Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC).

According to her, discussions would also address business registration, due diligence, anti-fraud measures and administrative reforms aimed at creating a more reliable investment environment.

The NiDCOM boss said the summit was designed to move beyond general advocacy by providing interactive question-and-answer sessions through which participants could engage directly with regulators, mortgage providers, project sponsors and verified service providers.

She explained that the physical component had been scaled down because of the forthcoming national election campaign season, but assured Nigerians abroad that the commission remained committed to promoting credible and protected investment opportunities.

Dabiri-Erewa described the 2026 summit as preparatory groundwork for the 10th anniversary edition in 2027.

She invited Nigerians in the diaspora, diaspora business groups, professionals, institutional investors, project developers and entrepreneurs to participate in the summit.

She also expressed appreciation to First Bank of Nigeria Plc and other partners for their continued support in connecting Nigerians abroad with investment opportunities at home.

She said the ultimate objective was to build secure, transparent and profitable investment pathways through which diaspora capital could contribute meaningfully to Nigeria’s sustainable economic development.

World.title: Johannesburg’s first family? Meet Helen Zille’s husband and kids
World.content:
Helen Zille is leading the Johannesburg mayoral race, as the Democratic Alliance (DA) has emerged as a frontrunner after this week’s local government elections.

The 75-year-old has previously helmed control of Cape Town, winning the 2008 World Mayor Award, which honoured her leadership and efforts to improve service delivery in the city.

IS HELEN ZILLE JOHANNESBURG’S NEXT MAYOR?

As it stands with the voter count, the DA is in a strong position to take control of Johannesburg. However, Helen Zille is not guaranteed the mayoralty.



After the IEC finalises the election results, the newly elected councillors will then vote for the mayor. For Helen to get the keys to the city, the DA will likely need to rally support from other parties, such as Action SA, to secure a majority in the council.

She will then need the majority of councillors’ votes to become Johannesburg’s next mayor.

MEET HER HUSBAND AND KIDS…

Helen Zille has spoken of receiving the support from her family, including husband, and two sons, in her bid to become Johannesburg mayor.



Helen is married to retired professor Johann Maree, who has a PhD in sociology from the University of Cape Town. The couple married in 1982.

ThrowbackThursday — my husband and I on honeymoon in 1982 pic.twitter.com/vLJ4JOJSRy — Helen Zille (@helenzille) October 9, 2025

They have two sons together: Paul and Thomas.



Paul, who married Gretl Visser in 2014, is a mathematics teacher and founder of Paper Video, an organisation that distributes educational resources to students around the country.

He’s also a member of Beams, a music band that has played at several of Cape Town’s hot spots. Paul gave his mother the nickname “GodZille” over her strict parenting style.

Thomas is a digital marketing manager and has worked for Showmax and CNBC Africa. He bears a striking resemblance to his mother.

Helen Zille is also a grandmother to Mila and Francois, the daughter and son of Paul and Gretl.

She is also a foster grandmother to children she took in from her domestic worker.

World.title: Thai national who tried to smuggle parrot eggs through OR Tambo gets hefty sentence
World.content:
Preliminary investigations indicated the eggs belonged to a parrot species protected under CITES. Image: PASA

In August, a 50-year-old man from Thailand was arrested at OR Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg for attempting to smuggle 50 protected parrot eggs out of South Africa.

The man was convicted and sentenced in the Kempton Park Regional Court this week. It followed a joint operation by the Green Scorpions and police.

Under a plea agreement, he was sentenced to a R500 000 fine or five years’ imprisonment.



The sentence was suspended for five years. This is subject to R300 000 being paid to the South African National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI).

The money will contribute towards the care of animals seized during law enforcement operations.

Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), David Maynier, welcomed the conviction.



“This case is an example of what can be achieved with cooperation and coordination across law enforcement agencies,” he said.

Parrot eggs rescued after smuggling attempt

The suspect was arrested at OR Tambo airport in August this year after attempting to smuggle 50 endangered parrot eggs out of the country.

Customs officials discovered the eggs concealed inside a homemade incubator bag carried as hand luggage.



The arrest followed an intelligence-driven operation involving the DFFE, SAPS Crime Intelligence and Border Police.

SANBI staff subsequently stepped in to care for the seized eggs. Despite the conditions in which they were transported, many successfully hatched. The chicks received intensive veterinary and husbandry care to maximise their chances of survival.

Preliminary investigations indicated that the eggs may belong to parrot species protected under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).



Maynier said the institute’s expertise had also been vital in securing the conviction.

“The Court’s ruling that funds must be paid to SANBI is welcomed, and the DFFE will be pursuing similar requests in other cases where wildlife is confiscated,” he added.

Arrest warrant issued in separate case

The case came just weeks after another Thai national was arrested at the same airport in connection with an even larger suspected parrot egg smuggling operation.



In July, a 23-year-old Thai national was detained at OR Tambo after authorities discovered 418 parrot eggs in his possession.

The two incidents have heightened concerns about South Africa’s role in international wildlife trafficking.

“These arrests highlight the growing sophistication of transnational wildlife trafficking networks,” the environment ministry said.



According to the DFFE, the Green Scorpions will continue the investigation into the wider trafficking network with the support of other countries and international organisations.

World.title: NASA looks to NSRI for future astronaut rescue operations
World.content:
The NSRI could one day play a vital role in rescuing astronauts off the Cape coast. Image via Facebook @SeaRescue

For the first time in the National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI)’s 59-year existence, the organisation could potentially play a vital role in rescuing NASA astronauts.

According to the NSRI, NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) is developing contingency plans for emergency situations – such as a launch abort – when astronauts return from future Artemis missions to the Moon.

As such, the famed space agency is assessing several potential recovery areas worldwide – including Cape Town.



NSRI MEETS NASA REPS

NASA representatives recently paid a “surprise” visit to Cape Town, whereby they made contact with the NSRI at very short notice, explained Charlz Maritz, NSRI Head of Operations.

“Our understanding is that the NASA team had heard about the NSRI as a potential maritime rescue resource while in South Africa and wanted to learn more about our capabilities,” he said. “It is encouraging to know that the NSRI remains highly regarded when it comes to maritime rescue and safety around our coast.

“At the heart of it, it is still about saving lives in difficult conditions and coordinating an effective response.”



The reps also took the opportunity to meet with local trauma facilities. In doing so, they assessed their emergency medical capabilities on their visit to the Mother City.

WHAT NSRI RESCUE WOULD ENTAIL

The meeting between the NSRI and NASA’s representatives saw the parties discussing the former’s “potential role in locating, reaching and recovering astronauts and specialist rescue personnel at sea.”

In several emergency scenarios, if an Orion spacecraft were to abort eight minutes from launching from the state of Florida, it could splash down off the Cape coast.



A launch abort could see a spacecraft splashing down on the Cape coast, one of many potential recovery areas worldwide. Image: Pexels

Should astronauts get injured and cannot await a response from NASA or the US Department of Defence recovery teams, the NSRI – so long as the location is within operational capabilities – could initiate an immediate rescue. Moreover, they could assist in transporting astronauts and specialist rescuers back to shore to receive medical attention.

However, said Maritz, logistical issues – specifically, the distance between the splashdown and the coast – could severely limit the NSRI’s range and time at sea.

Additionally, astronaut recovery involves specialised medical, technical, safety and security procedures. As such, the NSRI’s primary role would be carrying out maritime rescue, while NASA’s specialist teams would oversee spacecraft-specific requirements.



OTHER FACTORS TO CONSIDER

NASA representatives also briefed the NSRI about other factors, including:

How the Orion spacecraft would behave in the event of an emergency abort.

Astronaut injuries that could occur following a harder-than-normal splashdown.

Providing responders with technical guidance regarding potential hazards and safe access to the capsule, along with relevant medical information for hospitals.

What’s more, they assessed the medical and rescue support available in the highly unlikely event of spacecraft ditching occurring shortly after launch.

This assessment entails visiting Cape Town and several other countries situated along the West African seaboard.



A NEW FRONTIER IN MARITIME RESCUE

All in all, it sounds like the visit was productive. This could give South African organisations like the NSRI a chance to contribute to space-related matters in the future. Plus, as Maritz noted, it also shows how highly they’re valued by the likes of NASA for their maritime rescue operations.

In other news, over 17 000 rooibos plant seeds are being primed for an upcoming space mission to the International Space Station.

World.title: Gayton open to DA coalition: ‘We are vying for power’
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has expressed interest in forming a coalition with the DA. Images via Facebook

Patriotic Alliance president Gayton McKenzie has expressed interest in working with the Democratic Alliance in a coalition government, despite claiming that he “despises” the political party.

The PA has gained significant ground in the Western Cape and Northern Cape and has emerged as the largest party in Prince Albert, securing 5 out of 10 council seats.

The outspoken leader has also called on his party members to “accept defeat graciously”, after losing two wards in Eldorado Park, Johannesburg



GAYTON MCKENZIE OPEN TO DA COALITION

Speaking at a media briefing at the IEC national results centre, Gayton McKenzie revealed that the PA’s next agenda was to discuss the way forward on coalition talks, particularly in Prince Albert in the Western Cape, where the party won 5 out of 10 council seats.

The PA’s mayoral candidate for Prince Albert Municipality is Arnold MacKay.

Results revealed that the DA won 4 seats, while the ANC secured just one.

He said: “We don’t like the DA, let me be frank. I despise them. But we will work with them because it’s not about me; it’s about the leadership of the PA

“What the leadership decides on Monday, we will work with anyone. If the AWB still existed, we would have worked with them. It’s about our people”.

Gayton responded to claims that both he and PA Deputy-President were after political power, even at the expense of their personal feelings.



He continued: “We are vying for power. Don’t let people lie to you; politicians love power. People say McKenzie loves power, yes, of course. I’m a retired businessman; I’ve made my money. If I didnt love and want power, why would I put myself in politics”

Apart from Prince Albert, the PA emerged as the second-largest party in George, behind the DA, and third in Kannaland, behind the DA and ICOSA.

WATCH: PA leader Gayton McKenzie says he is willing to consider working with the DA in coalition arrangements for the benefit of society, despite admitting that he hates the party.



McKenzie says he is prepared to ensure a smooth working relationship in metros where the two… pic.twitter.com/C8KlrdtaUo — Kaya News (@KayaNews) November 6, 2026

‘ACCEPT DEFEAT GRACIOUSLY’

Meanwhile, Gayton McKenzie has called on PA members to “accept defeat graciously”, after losing wards 17 and 18 in Eldorado Park.

The 51-year-old claimed that he had been “inundated with conspiracy theories and allegations” about the party’s “shocking loss of both wards”.

He shared in a Facebook post: “I hereby wanna make it public that we accept defeat in both Wards and wanna congratulate the DA. We should not be sore losers.

“The people made their choice, and instead of blaming the people, we should go and do some introspection. The numbers we had were totally wrong.”

World.title: City bemoans cable theft near ‘unlawfully-occupied’ land in trendy Cape Town suburb
World.content:
The vandalism and theft has also impacted MyCiTi bus operations in the area. Image: CoCT

The City of Cape Town says repeated cable theft and vandalism has cost taxpayers around R8 million in Lower Woodstock.

The damage has targeted electrical infrastructure in and around the Tide Street Substation. Some of the equipment was brand new.

The City says the incidents are linked to criminal activity near the “unlawful occupation” of Transnet-owned land, on the fringes of Lower Woodstock.



The neighbourhood has undergone significant gentrification in recent years. It is now home to coffee shops, bars, restaurants, supermarkets, art galleries and the popular Old Biscuit Mill market.

The City warns that the damage poses a threat to electricity supplies for residential and commercial customers in the area. The latest incident was reported on 2 November 2026.

Some damaged medium-voltage cables also remain unfixed. This is because shacks have been built over them, making repairs difficult.

“This situation is unacceptable, dangerous to the perpetrators and surrounding communities and a complete waste of public funds, as the damage has to be fixed repeatedly at great cost,” the City of Cape Town said in a statement.

Cable theft impacts electricity infrastructure and MyCiTi services

The targeted infrastructure includes substations, cables, switchgear, control panels and transformers.

Both low- and medium-voltage equipment have been affected.



Cable theft and vandalism has also impacted MyCiTi operations and infrastructure in the area.

The City noted that streetlights along the MyCiTi route from the Culemborg Safe Spaces Shelter to Paarden Eiland remain out of order as a result of the damage.

The municipality says the situation is “completely unsustainable,” with the estimated R8 million in damage excluding labour and other repair-related costs.

City monitoring area amid ongoing eviction battle

All recent and historical incidents have been reported to SAPS for investigation.

City law enforcement is also monitoring the area. Meanwhile, officials are exploring ways to better protect electrical infrastructure.

The land occupation has also become the subject of an ongoing legal battle.

Transnet secured an eviction order, but occupants appealed the ruling to the Supreme Court of Appeal. This has suspended the execution of the order.

The City and Transnet are appealing the ruling, citing risks to public safety, service delivery and electricity supplies to residential and commercial customers.

The City says it will continue exploring anti-theft and vandalism measures across the metro.

World.title: Mayoral chain or not, Moya vows to drink first glass of Bronkhorstspruit’s clean water
World.content:
MIDRAND - ActionSA Tshwane mayoral candidate, Nasiphi Moya, says her promise to ensure clean, drinkable water to Bronkhorstspruit residents remains unchanged even if she no longer wears the mayoral chains.

Moya says the metro is waiting for water results to confirm it meets safety standards before household distribution can begin.

'I made a promise to the people of Bronkhorstspruit that once it's complete, I'll be the first one to drink it. So, for me, I need to also give that assurance that the water is truly clean. So, when the water is clean, they will see me being the first one to drink it,' she said.

She says areas close to the reservoirs could get their water sooner.

'The high-lying areas sometimes take about 12 hours for the water to get there. It's a phased-out approach. But what I'm assured of, we'll have enough quantities that will reach all the households that are supposed to benefit from those'.

Moya was speaking to eNCA at the Results Operation Center (ROC) in Midrand as the capturing of the 2026 Local Government Election results continues.

READ | ANC faces worst-ever election result as support slumps

The most recent results indicate that around 81% of the votes have been counted in the City of Tshwane.

The DA is leading with 32.43%, followed by ActionSA with 22.94%.

The ANC is third with 21.58%. Moya said she was surprised and humbled by the support she received from residents.

'For me, whenever people were doubtful whether the work was happening and whether the work we were doing was resonating with communities, I always knew i would be judged by the residents and I think the outcomes show that the work did resonate.'

Regarding coalitions, Moya says ActionSA's doors are open.

World.title: MK Party says its door remains open to a coalition, but there are conditions
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MK Party) says its doors remain open for coalition talks, but parties who are interested have to do more than simply just to come knocking.

MK Party national spokesperson, Sifiso Mahlangu, said they will not compromise on issues it believes voters want them to fight for.

This as he lists some of their ‘preconditions' ahead of any coalition talks.

“Whilst our door is open for negotiations to talk, wherever those meetings are held, the conditions are that the land question must be on the table, radical economic transformation must be on the table, and the identity and the dignity of the African child must be paramount,” Mahlangu said.

According to Mahlangu, coalition talks have not yet started in a formal setting, with their phones ringing non-stop.

“We have been getting calls the whole night, calls from various parties across South Africa who would like meetings and would like engagement with ourselves.

World.title: eNCA News Bite | ANC coalition horse-trading, Zuma dock ruling and Springboks tour start | 06 November 2026
World.content:
Stay informed, fast, with ⁠News Bite⁠, your daily update on South Africa and the world, presented by Marcelle Gordon.

As the country awaits ⁠final election results⁠, coalition horse-trading has begun in earnest across dozens of hung municipalities, with the battle for Johannesburg front and centre. With about half of the votes captured, the DA was leading the race in the city of gold, putting the ANC under pressure to consider an unlikely coalition with ⁠GNU⁠ partner ActionSA. Analysts note that incoming leaders face intense scrutiny over service delivery and every rand spent.

The ⁠IEC⁠ is expected to declare ⁠final election results⁠ on Sunday. Political parties have wasted no time claiming victories or assessing performance. The DA has declared wins in the Western Cape and ruled out coalitions with the EFF or MK Party in the Eastern Cape.

Meanwhile, the MK Party dominated historic ANC strongholds across KZN, securing outright majorities in Richmond, Impendle, and the Johannes Pumani Phungula local municipalitiesPolitical analysts ⁠Andre Duvenhage ⁠and Thabang Motswaledi describe the current polls as the biggest rejection for the ANC since 1994, pointing to a permanent reconfiguration of South Africa's political landscape.

While ⁠ANC ⁠spokesperson ⁠Mahlengi Bhengu⁠ notes the party remains a leading force in six provinces, mayoral candidates like Jeremiah Thuynsma admit voters have lost trust and the party must own its mistakes.

⁠Low voter turnout⁠, particularly among the youth, emerged as a defining feature of the elections. eNCA journalist Naomi Kobbie spoke with young voters in ⁠Mpumalanga⁠, where post-grad student Liabona Mula explained that despite hundreds of contesting parties, many young South Africans feel systemic corruption and lack of targeted economic planning leave them sidelined.

⁠Former president Jacob Zuma⁠ spoke outside the Durban High Court, where his daughter ⁠Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla ⁠saw her application to have terrorism-related charges withdrawn rejected by Judge Mbuzeni Mathenjwa. She remains in the dock facing charges of inciting public violence during the ⁠July 2021 unrest⁠, with the trial postponed to 17 May next year.

Severe storms and hailstorms battered parts of the Eastern Cape, causing several home collapses in Nomaheya Village and New Look, with disaster officials from the Amathole District Municipality deploying aid.

Globally, U.S. stock markets fell following the midterm elections and a democratic blue wave that triggered portfolio reassessments away from AI-linked stocks over regulatory fears.

Additionally, low-cost carrier flights across Europe faced security disruptions following a series of ⁠bomb threat ⁠hoaxes.

SPORTS

The double World Cup-winning Springboks face Italy in Turin on Saturday to open the Nations Championship, with veteran Damien Willemse stressing the importance of a strong start.

In football, Bafana Bafana coach Hugo Broos announced a 27-man squad featuring 12 Mamelodi Sundowns players for upcoming Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Kenya.

In the EPL, Michael Carrick prepares ⁠Manchester United ⁠to host Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

That is your ⁠News Bite⁠ for 6 November 2026. Keep an eye on enca.com and DStv Channel 403 for the latest updates.

World.title: ANC faces worst-ever election result as support slumps
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The once-dominant African National Congress is headed for its worst-ever election performance with about a third of support after 80 percent of the votes from local government polls had been counted on Friday.

Wednesday's municipal elections were dominated by concerns over failing water and power supplies in one of Africa's wealthiest nations which became a democracy in 1994 when the ANC took power.

With final results expected by Sunday, the election authority dashboard showed the ANC was still the largest party with nearly 32 percent of votes after 80 percent had been counted.

This was its lowest score yet for the ANC after it secured just over 40 percent at the 2024 national polls and 46 percent at the previous municipal elections in 2021.

At the heart of South Africa's anti-apartheid struggle, the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004.

"This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared," political analyst Daniel Silke told AFP. "It's the ANC's worst result in history."

"It will undermine its ability to exert authority across South Africa, not just at a local level, but frankly at a national level as well," he told AFP.

"And opposition parties will be smelling blood when it comes to the next election in 2029."

The result of this week's local ballot is seen as an indication of voter sentiment ahead of the 2029 general election, including whether frustrations with local government failures are changing political loyalties.

About 15.9 million of 29.2 million registered voters cast ballots, the electoral commission said. Turnout was an estimated 54.5 percent, up from 46 percent in the pandemic-hit 2021 local elections.

Coalition bargaining

The pro-business, centre-right Democratic Alliance (DA) was placing second with just over 24 percent of votes, according to the 80 percent count.

This was up from nearly 22 percent in the 2021 local government election.

The party was set to maintain control of the tourism magnet city of Cape Town and was also leading in the battle for Johannesburg, the country's financial capital, where it ran a spirited campaign spearheaded by its former leader Helen Zille.

Former president Jacob Zuma's breakaway opposition uMkhonto weSizwe party (MKP) -- contesting local government elections for the first time -- was third with just over nine percent.

It was leading in the eastern metropolitan municipality of eThekwini, which includes the port city of Durban, the capital of KwaZulu-Natal province that is Zuma's Zulu homeland.

With outright majorities unlikely to be assured in several major cities, the results will usher in complex coalition negotiations as parties start bargaining to assemble the alliances needed to govern.

"All of the cut and thrust that comes with the election is now over, and it is time now to rise above ... and to put together governments that can actually fix these towns and cities," DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis told reporters.

"We have already reached out to many parties over the last 24 hours, and will continue to do so today," he said.

While some of the ANC losses are down to disillusionment after years of corruption and mismanagement, chunks of its support base have also been won over by splinter parties like the MKP in the country's increasingly fragmented political landscape.

"Key among the reasons why the ANC is losing votes is because of the emergence of the parties such as the MKP," said university lecturer and analyst Sanet Solomons.

"The smaller parties have been part of coalitions, but those coalitions have in the past been quite unstable and that is not going to improve service delivery," political science professor Amanda Gouws told AFP.

World.title: IEC survey reveals what was on voters' minds
World.content:
MIDRAND - The belief that a single vote can make a difference remains a motivation for South Africans who voted in the 2026 Local Government Elections.

This is according to the Electoral Commission of South Africa’s (IEC) Election Satisfaction Survey, which found that 59% of voters cast their vote because it would make a difference.

The research, conducted by the Human Science Research Council on behalf of the IEC, sampled 300 voting stations across the country’s nine provinces, with fieldworkers randomly interviewing 50 voters at voting stations through election day.

Other motivations included 39% who said they want to get good quality and reliable government services ranging from issues such as electricity, water and rubbish removal, among others.

There was at least 38% who cited an improved economy and 36% cited the fight against corruption.

READ | DA open to coalition talks - Hill-Lewis

The survey also found that the perceptions of political tolerance during election campaigns remain strongly positive and have improved over time.

In 2026, 86% of voters regarded political parties and candidates as either very tolerant or somewhat tolerant, compared with 81% in 2011, the survey revealed.

Meanwhile, the proportion perceiving political intolerance has declined from 13% in 2011 to 7% in 2026.

The proportion perceiving political intolerance has declined from 13% in 2011 to 7% in 2026.

World.title: DA open to coalition talks - Hill-Lewis
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Democratic Alliance leader Geordin Hill-Lewis says the party is open to coalitions with other political parties.

The DA is calling on political parties to help it rebuild municipalities nationwide.

Hill-Lewis says the party is determined to improve service delivery in failing municipalities.

"We will approach the next few weeks with respect for the mandates those parties have received from their voters," he says.

"We know that these cities desperately need a period of long and sustained progress under the honest and integrity-driven government," he adds.

The party has amassed a leading number of votes in many of the country's metros and municipalities.

However, as seat allocation gets underway, a different picture is emerging that could change the trajectory of many municipalities.

The party is open to talks with 'like-minded' people. It says even an alliance with the Economic Freedom Fighters is a possibility.

"We have already reached out to many parties over the last 24 hours and we will continue," says Hill-Lewis.

World.title: eNCA MarkData | Understanding overhangs in municipal councils
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - As the final votes come in, political parties are turning their attention to their seat allocations in municipal councils.

The final allocation of council seats should broadly reflect each party’s share of the vote. But what happens when a party wins more wards than the number of seats it would normally be entitled to under proportional representation?

This is known as an overhang.

World.title: Family identifies two security officers involved in Abshir Abdi abduction
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

LSK president Charles Kanjama leads members in a protest over the disappearance of lawyer Abshir Abdi. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The family of Nairobi lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi has identified two security officers alleged to have taken part in their kin's abduction, even as his colleagues threatened mass protests to push for his release.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) said the two names have been forwarded to the police to aid in investigations and demanded that the office of the Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, speed up the probe into the abduction.

"One is named Siad and the other is Hussein, and we want them released for investigation, arrest, prosecution, conviction, sentencing and imprisonment," said LSK.

The revelation came during a demonstration led by (LSK outside the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police and other towns yesterday .

Abshir was forcibly taken on November 1 along Muchai Road, his vehicle was pursued and intercepted by armed individuals in two vehicles before he was seized.

While state security agencies have denied holding him in custody, court filings and colleagues suggest his abduction may be connected to his professional work representing clients in high-profile cases involving senior police officers.

Furthermore, the LSK presented additional names of security personnel linked to the incident, demanding immediate legal action against Chief Inspector Vitalis Kibet, Inspector Kennedy Kimani Karanja, Siad Mohammed, Abdurahman of the Anti-Terrorism Police Unit (ATPU), and KDF officer Ali Hussein.

The leadership voiced their frustration over the state's inaction and the alarming pattern of extrajudicial actions targeting officers of the court. Representatives insisted that lawyers must be allowed to execute their duties without fear of intimidation, torture, or abduction.

"We demand that the officers involved be handed over, arrested, prosecuted, and convicted. We will stand in the courts, in the streets, and in the boardrooms until abductions come to an end," they said in a statement.

The LSK has issued a stern ultimatum to the police command, including the president, DIG Gilbert Masengeli, Inspector General Douglas Kanja, and senior commanders. If Abshir is not released safely and the identified suspects are not formally charged in court by Monday, the LSK warned it will initiate private prosecutions itself.

Furthermore, the society threatened to bring activities to a complete shutdown and demand the immediate resignation of Kanja, Masingeli and Minister for Security Kipchumba Murkomen, carrying their demonstrations to Parliament and State House if necessary.

As court proceedings continue under a habeas corpus application at the Milimani High Court, the legal fraternity remains resolute: the protest at Jogoo House is merely the beginning of an unyielding campaign for justice and the rule of law.

In Nakuru, lawyers protested within the Law Courts, calling for his production.

“It is shocking that one of our colleagues was picked and today we do not know where he is. Unless we voice our concern, there will be complete lawlessness in the country,” said LSK member Ekaterina Handa. “Our lives matter and silencing lawyers is silencing justice. we will not relent until we get justice.”

Rift Valley LSK Chair Wangari Mwangi said it was shocking that the alleged abduction was captured on CCTV.

She rubbished the narrative that the missing lawyer was involved in a crime syndicate, maintaining that he should have been arrested and charged in court. [Additional reporting by Daniel Chege]

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.
