In plain English In France, a prefect is the national government’s top local official. He can ban a march when he fears trouble, and organisers are expected to tell his office beforehand.

What the Ban Covers

In Quimper, no demonstration is allowed from 6:00 a.m. Saturday to 6:00 a.m. Sunday Paris time (12:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. ET). The zone runs from the Rue du Palais and the Place de la Tour d’Auvergne to the Place de la Résistance and the Allées de Locmaria.

In Brest, the ban starts at 8:00 a.m. Saturday Paris time (2:00 a.m. ET) and ends at 6:00 a.m. Sunday (12:00 a.m. ET). It covers streets around the Boulevard Gambetta, the Rue Duquesne and the Avenue Franklin Roosevelt.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the Prefect Acted

The prefecture points to violence and damage at protests in the department since 1 October. On 4 November it also banned weapons, flammable products, paint and face coverings in eight communes, including Brest, Quimper and Morlaix.

That order runs until 12:00 p.m. Monday, 9 November, Paris time (6:00 a.m. ET). The prefect stresses that the freedom to protest is fundamental, but says advance notice and dialogue with the state are essential.

What Happened on Thursday

About 16,000 people marched across Finistère on 5 November, the prefecture says. That included 7,000 in Brest, 4,950 in Quimper and 2,400 in Morlaix.

In Quimper, a march by two French union confederations, UNSA and CFDT, kept to the route agreed with police. A second, undeclared march dispersed at Place Saint-Corentin around 3:30 p.m. Paris time (9:30 a.m. ET), and one person who tried to burn a bin was arrested.

In Brest, nearly 500 masked people tried to provoke police at the head of the march. One gendarme from the mobile units, the paramilitary riot force, was injured in the department.

The prefect praised the unions that planned with his office and criticised those who marched without declaring. He said his office had offered talks several times before Thursday.

What Prediction Markets Say Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, priced a French state of emergency by 31 December at about 3% at 2:43 p.m. ET on 6 November, with about US$2.8 million traded. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Americans in Brittany this weekend should avoid the two city centres on Saturday. Paris time is six hours ahead of New York, so the Quimper ban starts at midnight on Friday night US time.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has called unions and employers to talks on pay on Monday, 9 November. Whether Saturday stays calm may shape how far unions push before then; our France travel safety guide covers the wider picture.

What Is Not Known

The prefecture does not say who issued the calls to protest, or how many people may come. It gives no figure for extra police on Saturday.

Its Thursday account also differs slightly: its summary counts two arrests, while its town-by-town details describe three. We will update as the prefecture publishes more.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it legal to protest in Quimper on Saturday?

Not in the banned zone. The prefect banned all demonstrations in a defined central perimeter from 6:00 a.m. Saturday to 6:00 a.m. Sunday Paris time (12:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. ET).

Why were the Brest and Quimper protests banned?

The prefecture says no protest was declared and organisers made no contact. It cites the risk of public disorder.

Sources: Préfecture du Finistère, Prime Minister’s office.

COLOMBIA · POLITICS

Key Facts Who Day Vásquez is the ex-wife of Nicolás Petro, son of former president Gustavo Petro.

What Colombian radio reports say she has been in contact with US authorities about 2022 campaign money.

Status No US agency, Vásquez or Gustavo Petro has confirmed the reports, which use conditional wording.

Prediction markets Polymarket, a US prediction platform, gives a 9% chance that Gustavo Petro is charged in the US by 31 December (6 November, 2:38 p.m. ET).

Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.1 points (November 2026 edition).

Colombian radio stations reported on Thursday 5 and Friday 6 November 2026 that Day Vásquez, a key prosecution witness in Colombia, has been in contact with US authorities about money that may have reached the 2022 presidential campaign of Gustavo Petro. The reports use conditional wording, and no US agency has confirmed them.

For US readers, the story matters because a US case involving a former Colombian president would test ties between Washington and Bogotá, a close security and trade partner. Our guide to Colombia’s key players explains who is who.

What Is Reported

One radio report, citing high-level sources, said Vásquez had contacts with US authorities to give details of 2022 campaign meetings where illicit money was allegedly agreed. A second report, quoting a journalist rather than named sources, said she would be handing US entities the evidence she holds on money and contributions in that campaign.

Who Is Day Vásquez

Vásquez is the former wife of Nicolás Petro, who is the son of Gustavo Petro, Colombia’s president from 2022 to August 2026. She became a public figure in 2023 after saying that her then husband had received cash during his father’s campaign.

Prosecutors gave her a “principio de oportunidad”, a deal that spares a cooperating witness from prosecution for her own role in the case against Nicolás Petro; a judge approved it in 2024 and a higher court kept it in force in September 2026. She has said before that Gustavo Petro did not know about the money.

What She Said in June

On 3 June 2026 Vásquez asked several Colombian bodies, including the House of Representatives’ Commission of Accusations, the panel that investigates presidents, to hear her. She also said then that she would speak to US authorities.

That earlier statement is why the new reports are plausible, but it is not confirmation. She has not publicly said that she has handed anything to a US agency.

What Colombian Prosecutors Have Done

Colombia’s Attorney General’s Office has charged Ricardo Roa, the 2022 campaign manager, with exceeding the campaign’s legal spending limits, which is an allegation he has not accepted. He told the court he is innocent.

Colombia’s National Electoral Council, which oversees campaign finance, has also fined the campaign’s manager and two parties for exceeding spending limits and taking prohibited contributions. No court has found that money of criminal origin entered the 2022 campaign.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a prediction platform where users bet real money, traders gave 9.0% to Gustavo Petro being charged in the United States by 31 December, as of 2:38 p.m. ET on 6 November. About US$12,000 has been traded on this market, so the price is a rough signal only.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you invest in Colombia, this is a political-risk story rather than a market mover today. A US case against a former president would be unusual and could affect relations between the two governments.

Travellers face no direct effect. US companies in Colombia should watch the Colombian court cases and any step by US authorities.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether any US agency has received material, in what form, or whether it would be used in a case. Vásquez, her lawyer and Gustavo Petro had not publicly confirmed or denied the reports by 6 November.

Nothing in the reports shows that Gustavo Petro knew of illicit money, and he has not been charged in Colombia or in the United States.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Is Reported About Day Vásquez and the US?

Colombian radio says she has been in contact with US authorities about 2022 campaign money. The reports are unconfirmed.

Who Is Day Vásquez?

She is the former wife of Nicolás Petro, the son of former president Gustavo Petro. She is a witness for prosecutors in the case against her ex-husband.

Has Gustavo Petro Been Charged?

No. He has not been charged in Colombia or in the United States.

Do Prediction Markets Expect a US Case?

Polymarket, a US prediction platform, gave 9.0% to a US charge against Gustavo Petro by 31 December as of 6 November. That is a bet, not a forecast by officials.

Sources: Colombian radio reports of 5 and 6 November 2026; Attorney General’s Office of Colombia, charges against Ricardo Roa (2026); Polymarket market data, 6 November 2026.

UGANDA · POLITICS

Key Facts Who General Muhoozi Kainerugaba commands Uganda’s army and is the son of President Yoweri Museveni.

What He said on 6 November 2026 he will hand over command “in a few months.”

Timing He also said he will stay “at least for another year” and gave no handover date.

Unknown No successor has been named by the army or the president’s office.

Uganda’s army chief, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, said on Friday 6 November 2026 that his time in command is coming to an end. He said he will hand the office to “a qualified officer” in a few months, and that he will stay “at least for another year.”

Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Africa story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

Muhoozi is the son of President Yoweri Museveni, so any change at the top of the army is read as a signal about who will lead Uganda next. For US readers, Uganda is an East African state where the army chief is the president’s son, so any change at the top matters to diplomats and investors.

What Happened

Muhoozi made the announcement in a post on X, the social media platform, on Friday, writing: “My time as CDF is coming to an end.” CDF stands for Chief of Defence Forces, the officer who commands the Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF), the national army, under the president as commander in chief.

He added: “I have accomplished all the tasks my God gave me.” He said he would “dedicate my life to Christ” after the handover.

He also wrote that his heroes have always been UPDF soldiers and that “we are struggling to improve their accommodation.” We could not find any army or government reply to those lines.

He also told followers that he is “still around” and will remain “at least for another year.” His words leave open whether he means a year as chief or a year in uniform.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Pay Proposal

Muhoozi also proposed that every UPDF private be paid 2 million Ugandan shillings (Ush2,000,000, about US$500) as a basic salary, starting in the next financial year. It is a proposal, not an approved pay scale, and his post announced no funding.

We use a rounded rate of 4,000 shillings per US dollar, because quotes for the shilling differ between data providers. The dollar figure is therefore approximate.

Who Muhoozi Is

President Yoweri Museveni, who has ruled Uganda since 1986, appointed Muhoozi chief of defence forces on 21 March 2024. The chief commands the whole army under the president, so the post is among the most powerful in the country.

In late August 2026 Muhoozi said in posts on X, the social media platform, that he will run for president in 2031. In the posts we found, he did not link his army exit to that bid.

Our guide to Uganda’s key players explains who holds power around the president. It is a useful map if the handover turns into a succession story.

What It Means for You

If you follow Uganda as an investor or a traveller, nothing changes this week. Muhoozi remains chief for now, and no handover date has been announced.

A handover would end the term as chief that began in March 2024, so the name of his successor is the next thing to watch. Governments and companies that work with the UPDF will also want to know whether the next chief changes its priorities.

The pay proposal may matter more to soldiers than the handover date, since a salary for every private would reach the whole force. It would need money from the government budget before it could take effect.

What Is Not Known

It is not known who will replace Muhoozi, or whether President Museveni, who appoints the chief, has agreed the timing. It is not known whether the army or the president’s office will comment.

It is also unclear whether Muhoozi plans to leave the army altogether or only to give up the top post. He has given no date, and his own words (“a few months” and “at least for another year”) point to different timetables.

More: Uganda news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Muhoozi Leaving Uganda’s Army Now?

No. He said he will hand over command in a few months and stay at least for another year, and he gave no date.

Who Is Muhoozi Kainerugaba?

He is a general and the son of President Yoweri Museveni. He has led the army as chief of defence forces since March 2024.

Who Will Replace Him?

No successor has been named. He said only that the next chief will be “a qualified officer.”

Sources: Public posts by General Muhoozi Kainerugaba on X, 6 November 2026 and late August 2026.

World.title: Haiti Finds Burned Vehicle of 4 Salvadorans
World.content:
Port-au-Prince and its bay seen from a hillside in September 2008, a file photo. Photo: U.S. Navy / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)

Key Facts What. Haitian police found the burned remains of an armoured vehicle that four missing Salvadoran technicians used.

Where and when. Santo, in Croix-des-Bouquets outside Port-au-Prince; police announced it on Tuesday, 3 November 2026.

Who. Haitian police, the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) and Salvadoran troops; the men vanished on 18 October.

Numbers. More than 2,000 Salvadoran troops are in Haiti; the UN says only about 200 fall under GSF jurisdiction.

Next. GSF mandate expires 31 March 2027; Haiti votes on 18 July 2027, with a second round on 4 October 2027.

This story is part of our coverage of the haiti crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Police Find the Vehicle

Haitian police said they found the burned remains of an armoured vehicle they believe was used by four missing Salvadoran aviation technicians. Police announced the find on Tuesday, 3 November, in the Santo neighbourhood of Croix-des-Bouquets, outside Port-au-Prince, part of our haiti crisis coverage.

Police were conducting a joint operation with the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), a UN-backed multinational security force, and Salvadoran troops. The four men have still not been found.

The technicians disappeared on 18 October after an attack in the area. El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, has sent troops to Haiti.

The cathedral in Cap-Haïtien, northern Haiti, far from Croix-des-Bouquets (file photo).

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Commands the Salvadoran Troops

Stéphane Dujarric, spokesman for the UN Secretary-General, said this week that only about 200 of the Salvadoran soldiers fall under the GSF's jurisdiction. He added that any security operation must follow international human rights law.

Haiti's Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé said on Tuesday that foreign forces operate under Haitian authority. "The international forces did not come to replace the state. They came to support it, to reinforce our capacity," he said.

Bukele has sent more than 2,000 troops, and on Wednesday, 4 November, he wrote on X, the social network: "Gather your gangs so we can go fight with them." On Tuesday he posted a video he said showed Salvadoran helicopters firing on gangs attacking GSF soldiers.

Salvadoran troops began armed patrols on 30 October. Security analysts question the terms of El Salvador's separate deployment, which the UN says operates outside the GSF framework.

Romain Le Cour, an analyst at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, said the rules of engagement, chain of command, objectives and duration remain opaque.

Civilians Bear the Cost

Doctors Without Borders (MSF), the international medical charity, said 30 people were injured by gunfire and drone explosions in the eight days after 18 October. Its head of mission in Haiti, Davina Hayles, said: "We fear that this armed conflict will claim even more victims."

Vote and Mandate Dates

Haiti has had no elected president since President Jovenel Moïse was assassinated in 2021. The Provisional Electoral Council, the body that organises elections, moved the first round from 13 December to 18 July 2027, with a second round on 4 October 2027.

Fewer than 1 million people are registered to vote. The UN Security Council extended the GSF mandate on 29 September to 31 March 2027, with China, Pakistan and Russia abstaining.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, said about 1,500 GSF troops were in Haiti, with another 4,000 expected in the coming months.

What It Means for US Readers

Washington co-sponsored the September resolution that renewed the GSF mandate. Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, described the GSF as an attempt to do something different after seven earlier missions with limited success.

The force was operating at about 30 percent of its intended size as of late September.

What Is Not Known

The fate of the four technicians is unknown. Bukele said four bodies handed over on 24 October were not his men, and a gang leader's claim that they were killed came without evidence.

Reports differ on whether the vehicle was found on 2 or 3 November. It is unclear whether the Salvadoran force is legally inside or outside the GSF framework, since the UN says only about 200 soldiers are covered.

Reports of the troop numbers vary. Whether the July 2027 election date will hold is not known.

We found no named-institute poll and no live prediction-market odds on Haiti.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Haitian police announce on 3 November?

Police said they found the burned remains of an armoured vehicle they believe four missing Salvadoran technicians used. It was in the Santo neighbourhood of Croix-des-Bouquets, outside Port-au-Prince, and the men have not been found.

Are the Salvadoran troops part of the Gang Suppression Force?

The UN says only about 200 of the Salvadoran soldiers fall under the force’s jurisdiction. Haiti’s prime minister says all foreign forces operate under Haitian authority.

When is Haiti’s next election?

The first round is now set for 18 July 2027, with a second round on 4 October 2027. Whether the date will hold is not known.

Sources: Haitian National Police, UN spokesperson's briefing, UN Security Council, Doctors Without Borders (MSF), Haitian prime minister's office, Provisional Electoral Council, US Mission to the UN.

Key Facts Who. José Maria Neves, Cabo Verde’s president, backed by the PAICV (African Party for the Independence of Cabo Verde), seeks a second term against five rivals.

What. Neves is skipping Friday’s second TV debate over remarks two rivals made at the first debate on 27 October.

When. The first round is Sunday, 15 November; a runoff follows on Sunday, 29 November if nobody wins a majority.

Unknown. We could not confirm whether the debate went ahead, and found no independent poll.

Neves Pulls Out of the Second Debate

José Maria Neves, Cabo Verde’s president, will not take part in the second presidential debate on Friday, 6 November, on Televisão de Cabo Verde (TCV), the public broadcaster. His campaign says it formally notified the station, as part of our Cape Verde presidential election 2026 coverage.

The campaign cites remarks at the first debate, held on 27 October, which it calls "de extrema gravidade", or extremely serious. It says they breached mutual respect and democratic coexistence.

The campaign’s statement said: "A não participação neste segundo debate não representa uma recusa do contraditório ou do escrutínio público." In English, it says skipping the debate is not a refusal of challenge or public scrutiny.

What the Candidates Say

According to the Neves campaign, Casimiro de Pina, an independent who finished third in 2021, made criminal accusations and referred to a possible perpetual punishment of the president. It says Gilson Alves, another candidate, spoke of having Neves shot, using the word "fuzilamento".

Pina has replied that Neves had no reason to miss the debate, and Alves accuses him of cowardice and of abandoning voters. We could not independently verify what was said on 27 October.

Joana Rosa, a former justice minister backed by the Movement for Democracy (MpD), has challenged Neves to a face-to-face debate and criticised his absence. The MpD fell to 33 of 72 seats in the May parliamentary election, down from 38, while the PAICV won 37.

Six Candidates, One Clear Favourite

Six candidates are on the ballot: Neves, Rosa, Pina, Alves, Antero Tavares and Loisito Tavares de Sousa. In the 2021 first round Neves won 51.8% against 42.4% for Carlos Veiga, the runner-up, while abstention was about 52%.

We found no opinion poll from a named institute, so the only public gauge of the race is market pricing.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a platform where users trade real money on outcomes, Neves was priced at 94.0% and Rosa at 3.5% at 2:22 p.m. ET on 6 November, with US$35,336 traded. Prices are bets, not polls, and this is a thin market.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Dates That Matter

Campaigning ends on 13 November, and the first round is Sunday, 15 November. Under Presidential Decree 22/2026, which set the vote, a runoff follows on Sunday, 29 November if no candidate wins a majority of valid votes.

Cabo Verde is on UTC−1 all year, four hours ahead of US Eastern Time until March. The National Elections Commission (CNE), the official electoral body, will publish the official results.

What It Means for US Readers

For readers in the United States, the story is whether a stable island democracy’s campaign turns sour in its final nine days. Market prices are the fastest signal, but they are bets rather than polls, and our live election hub tracks both.

For background, see our guides to what to watch in round one and who holds power in Cabo Verde.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm the start time of the 6 November debate, whether it went ahead or what was said. Readers should check TCV directly.

We have not confirmed polling hours for 15 November. No independent poll has been published that we could find.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is José Maria Neves skipping the debate?

His campaign cites remarks by rivals Casimiro de Pina and Gilson Alves at the first debate on 27 October. It says it is not refusing public scrutiny, while both rivals have criticised his absence.

When is Cabo Verde’s presidential election?

The first round is Sunday, 15 November 2026. A runoff follows on Sunday, 29 November if no candidate wins a majority of valid votes.

Who is favoured to win?

Polymarket gave Neves 94.0% at 2:22 p.m. ET on 6 November, but that is a thin market and a bet, not a poll. We found no independent poll from a named institute.

World.content:

GHANA · ECONOMY

Key Facts What happened Reports say Mahama and Boeing, the US aircraft maker, agreed a roadmap for a national airline.

The steps The plan covers partners, an operating licence, the choice of aircraft and financing.

The goal Mahama hopes the airline will be flying before his term ends in January 2029.

The gaps No airline name, partner, aircraft order or budget has been announced.

Ghana’s President John Dramani Mahama and officials of Boeing, the US aircraft maker, have agreed a roadmap for setting up a new national airline, according to reports on Friday 6 November 2026. The plan lists four steps: finding partners, winning an operating licence, choosing aircraft and arranging the money.

Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Africa story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

For US readers, the story puts an American manufacturer at the centre of a possible new carrier in West Africa. It also shows Ghana courting US industry as it tries to turn its capital, Accra, into a regional air hub.

What Was Agreed

The roadmap covers identifying strategic and technical partners, getting an Air Operator Certificate (the licence needed to carry paying passengers), choosing the fleet and arranging financing. Reports say preliminary assessments of the project were positive.

An Air Operator Certificate, or AOC, is granted by the aviation regulator once it is satisfied that the airline can operate safely. Without it, no new carrier can sell tickets, whatever aircraft it has.

Boeing assured Mahama of its continued support through the setting-up and operating phases of the airline. The company is described as providing technical support for the project.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Ghana Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Accra Wants It

The airline is expected to make fuller use of Ghana’s airport facilities and to support Mahama’s vision of Accra as the leading aviation hub of West Africa. Reports also expect the project to create jobs for pilots, cabin crew, engineers and aviation managers.

Mahama has said he hopes Ghana will have a national airline in operation before his term ends in January 2029. That leaves about 26 months from now.

A Country Without a Flag Carrier

Ghana’s former national carrier, Ghana Airways, ceased operations in 2004, and its successor, Ghana International Airlines, collapsed in 2010. The country has had no national airline since, and governments have talked about reviving one several times.

This time the plan has a list of steps and a US technical supporter. In September, reports said Boeing had estimated roughly 18 months for a carrier to fly if Ghana put the needed structures in place.

Why It Matters for the United States

Boeing is a US company, so its involvement ties a possible new Ghanaian carrier to American aircraft, training and suppliers. The reports say Boeing is giving technical support, and no aircraft order or investment has been announced.

The reports do not say whether Boeing will supply aircraft, since fleet selection is still an open step. Any aircraft purchase would be a large cost for a government that has not announced a budget.

What It Means for You

If you fly between the United States and Ghana, nothing changes now, because no airline has been named and no aircraft are on order. The government’s own target is for the airline to fly before January 2029.

Investors in US aerospace should note that this is a technical-support agreement, not a sales contract. Any aircraft order would show up in Boeing’s published monthly orders and deliveries data.

What Is Not Known

It is not known who the strategic and technical partners will be, how much the airline will cost, or who will pay for it. The airline’s name, ownership split and first routes have not been announced.

The date and place of the meeting were not given in the reports, and neither was the name of any Boeing executive. It is also not known whether Boeing will supply aircraft.

More: Ghana news in English, every day from The Rio Times. See also how Ghana is screening airport arrivals for Ebola.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Did Ghana and Boeing Agree?

They agreed a roadmap for a new national airline, covering partners, an operating licence, fleet choice and financing. It was reported on Friday 6 November 2026.

Will Boeing Own or Fund the Airline?

No such deal has been announced. Boeing is described as giving technical support through the setting-up and operating phases.

When Could Ghana’s New Airline Fly?

Mahama hopes the airline will operate before his term ends in January 2029. No launch date has been set.

What Is an Air Operator Certificate?

It is the licence an aviation regulator gives an airline before it may carry paying passengers. The roadmap lists getting one as a key step.

Sources: Statements reported on 6 November 2026 on the meeting between President Mahama and Boeing, the US aircraft maker; Ghana’s earlier national airline plans, as reported in 2026.

World.title: Nigeria Sets US$11 Million Stablecoin Rule
World.content:
NIGERIA · MARKETS

Key Facts What happened Nigeria’s central bank released new rules for stablecoin issuers on Thursday 5 November 2026.

The floor Issuers of dollar-linked stablecoins need 15 billion naira (about US$11.1 million) in shareholder capital.

The catch Foreign issuers must set up a licensed Nigerian company to serve Nigerian users.

The lower tier Issuers of naira-linked tokens must hold 10 billion naira (about US$7.4 million).

Nigeria’s central bank, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), has told companies that issue digital dollars to hold 15 billion naira, Nigeria’s currency (about US$11.1 million) in shareholder capital, and to do it through a company based in Nigeria. A stablecoin is a crypto token built to stay worth one US dollar, and published summaries of the rules say foreign issuers such as Tether, which issues the USDT token, and Circle, the US company behind USDC, get no exemption.

The CBN, whose governor is Olayemi Cardoso, released the rules on Thursday 5 November 2026, according to published summaries, in a document titled Regulations for the Operations of Non-Security Virtual Assets in Nigeria. For US readers, it is an early test of how a large emerging market will treat the dollar tokens that US-linked fintech and crypto firms sell abroad.

What the Rule Says

The regulation sorts stablecoin issuers into two classes. Class 2 covers tokens tied to a foreign currency such as the US dollar, and its issuer must hold at least 15 billion naira in paid-up capital, meaning money that shareholders have actually put into the company.

The regulation says that capital must be in place on entry and at all times afterwards, or at any higher amount the CBN sets. At about 1,346 naira per US dollar (market rate, 6 November 2026), 15 billion naira is about US$11.1 million.

Class 1 covers tokens tied to the naira, and its issuers must hold 10 billion naira (about US$7.4 million). Other virtual asset service providers, such as wallets and exchanges, face a floor of 1 billion naira (about US$740,000), according to published summaries of the regulation.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Has to Comply

A Class 2 stablecoin can be issued only by a company incorporated in Nigeria that holds a Class 2 licence. The rules give no exemption to offshore issuers, so a foreign group must create a local entity that answers to the CBN.

Tokens may not be offered in Nigeria unless the CBN has approved them, according to a published summary. That keeps the approval decision with the central bank rather than with the issuer.

How the Money Is Protected

The capital is not the same money as the reserves that back each token. The regulation says capital must be separate from, and additional to, issuer reserves, so one pot of money cannot satisfy two rules.

A published summary adds that the capital must also stay separate from customer funds and operating liquidity. An issuer that falls below its floor must tell the CBN immediately and file a plan to restore its capital within 10 business days.

Published summaries say existing operators have 30 days from the start date to register with the CBN and 180 days to complete licence applications. They add that operators who miss the deadline must stop work until they are licensed.

Why It Matters Beyond Nigeria

A published summary says the Class 2 licence is built for cross-border payments, remittances and trade settlement. Those are the uses where dollar tokens compete with banks and money-transfer firms.

US fintech companies that move money between the United States and Nigeria will now need to work out whether they count as issuers or only as service providers. A firm that wants to issue dollar tokens to Nigerians needs a Nigerian company, a licence and about US$11.1 million of locked capital before it starts.

What It Means for You

If you invest in US-listed crypto or payments companies, watch whether they announce Nigerian licence applications. The capital is a one-off lock-up, while the licence and the local office add running costs.

If you send money to family in Nigeria through a stablecoin app, the service may change as providers decide whether to apply. The naira trades near 1,346 per US dollar, so 100,000 naira is worth about US$74.

What Is Not Known

It is not known which foreign issuers will apply, and the published summaries do not say that Tether or Circle has responded. One summary also mentions a separate liquidity requirement for dollar issuers, and its size is unconfirmed.

It is also unclear how the CBN will treat tokens already circulating in Nigeria while licences are pending. The day counts for existing operators run from a start date that the summaries describe in different ways.

More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times. See also how much Nigeria owes foreign lenders.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Is Nigeria’s New Stablecoin Capital Rule?

Issuers of stablecoins tied to a foreign currency must hold 15 billion naira (about US$11.1 million) in paid-up capital. The Central Bank of Nigeria released the rule, reports say, on Thursday 5 November 2026.

Does the Rule Cover Tether and Circle?

The rules give offshore issuers no exemption and require a licensed Nigerian company. Neither company’s plans for Nigeria are known.

How Does the Naira Stablecoin Floor Compare?

Issuers of naira-linked tokens must hold 10 billion naira (about US$7.4 million). Foreign-currency issuers face the higher floor of 15 billion naira.

What Happens if an Issuer Falls Short?

It must tell the central bank at once and file a plan to restore its capital within 10 business days. The capital cannot also be counted as reserves or operating funds.

Sources: Central Bank of Nigeria (central bank), Regulations for the Operations of Non-Security Virtual Assets in Nigeria, 5 November 2026; Central Bank of Nigeria; USD/NGN market data (RT), 6 November 2026.

NIGERIA · MARKETS

Key Facts The country Nigeria is Africa’s most populous nation, led by President Bola Tinubu since May 2023.

What happened Nigeria’s total external debt, public and private together, was US$145.0 billion at the end of 2025, up 6.6% in a year.

Who says The World Bank, the global development lender, published the figure on Thursday 5 November 2026.

The pressure Debt payments took 19.3% of export earnings in 2025, up from 17.6% in 2024.

Prediction markets Polymarket, a betting platform, gives Tinubu 67.5% to win the next presidential election (6 Nov, 1:52 p.m. ET).

Nigeria’s total external debt, meaning everything the government, companies and banks owe to lenders abroad, reached US$145.0 billion at the end of 2025, the World Bank said on Thursday 5 November 2026. The figure is 6.6% above the US$136.0 billion of a year earlier; the government’s own share, debt it borrowed or guaranteed, was US$56.9 billion.

For US investors, the number shows how much of Nigeria’s foreign debt sits outside government books and how costly it is to service. It matters to anyone who holds Nigerian Eurobonds, the dollar bonds that Nigeria sells to international investors.

What the World Bank Reported

The World Bank published the figure in its International Debt Report 2026, which tracks the borrowing of low- and middle-income countries. Its data show Nigeria’s external debt, meaning money owed to lenders outside the country, at US$145.0 billion for 2025.

Debt that the government borrowed or guaranteed was US$56.9 billion, up 13.2% from US$50.2 billion in 2024. Private borrowers without a state guarantee owed US$54.5 billion, down from US$57.5 billion, while short-term debt rose to US$28.1 billion from US$22.2 billion.

Bonds issued by the public sector, including Eurobonds, stood at US$19.4 billion, up from US$18.0 billion. Loans from commercial banks to the government or its agencies more than doubled to US$5.0 billion from US$2.2 billion.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Debt Is Larger but Slightly Lighter

Measured against the size of the economy, Nigeria’s external debt fell to 51.5% of gross national income, the total income of its citizens and firms, from 55.1% in 2024. Measured against export earnings it fell to 211.9% from 221.4%.

The cost of paying it back moved the other way. Debt service, the interest and principal paid each year, rose to 19.3% of export earnings in 2025 from 17.6% in 2024.

The Global Picture

Nigeria’s rise came as developing countries’ external debt jumped 5.5% to a record US$9.4 trillion in 2025, the fastest pace since 2021, according to the World Bank. These countries paid US$1.4 trillion in principal and interest in 2025, up 1.9% and the fifth rise in a row.

The bank said private lenders returned and bond markets reopened, but the cost of borrowing stayed high. Countries that qualify for the bank’s concessional loans, which carry below-market interest, paid an average of 8.2% on new private loans in 2025, the highest rate since 1989.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a platform where people bet real money on events, Bola Tinubu trades at 67.5% to win Nigeria’s next presidential election and Peter Obi, a leading opposition figure, at 26.0%. About US$153,000 has been traded on that market as of 1:52 p.m. ET on 6 November.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you hold Nigerian Eurobonds, the data show a public-sector bond stock of US$19.4 billion that is growing slowly and a heavier annual repayment bill. Higher debt service leaves less export income for imports, which can weigh on the naira, Nigeria’s currency.

If you run a business that sells to Nigeria, note that US$54.5 billion of the total is private debt, so many firms carry their own dollar repayments. Travellers and expatriates are not directly affected, but a weaker currency raises local prices over time.

What Is Not Known

The World Bank figure covers the whole country, public and private, so it is far larger than the roughly US$54.5 billion of government external debt that Nigeria’s Debt Management Office reported for 30 June 2026 (US$51.9 billion at 31 March). The two measure different things and dates and should not be compared.

The 2024 base is also higher than in an earlier World Bank dataset, which showed US$108.8 billion before this update. It is also not known how new foreign loans that President Tinubu has sought from the Senate, Nigeria’s upper house of parliament, will change the picture, since they fall after 2025.

Final figures for 2025 may be revised in later editions of the report.

More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times. See also what new loans could mean for each Nigerian.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Much Foreign Debt Does Nigeria Owe?

The World Bank puts Nigeria’s total external debt, public and private combined, at US$145.0 billion at the end of 2025. That is up 6.6% from US$136.0 billion a year earlier.

Is All of It Government Debt?

No, about US$56.9 billion was borrowed or guaranteed by the public sector. Most of the rest was owed by private borrowers without a state guarantee or was short-term debt.

Is Nigeria’s Debt Burden Getting Lighter?

Debt relative to national income fell to 51.5% from 55.1%, and relative to exports to 211.9% from 221.4%. Yearly debt service rose to 19.3% of export earnings from 17.6%.

What Is the International Debt Report?

It is the World Bank’s yearly report on the external debt of low- and middle-income countries. The 2026 edition was published on Thursday 5 November 2026.
