Marta Pachón, del equipo de comunicación financiera de la compañía y una de las impulsoras de esta estrategia de nuevos lenguajes cercanos de Mapfre, explica la premisa de esta serie divulgativa: “Sofía, de 32 años, acaba de firmar la hipoteca de su primera vivienda y se pregunta cómo volver a ahorrar tras ese enorme desembolso inicial. Carlos, de 47, tiene tres hijos adolescentes y necesita planificar los gastos en que incurrirá al enviar a estudiar fuera a una de sus hijas. Rosa, por su parte, tras un triste suceso, debe decidir qué hacer con una herencia… A partir de estos escenarios comunes se plantean cuestiones que nos incumben a todos: cómo se elige un seguro y qué coberturas debe tener, cómo se decide qué producto de inversión te conviene…”.

La gamificación, como describe Pachón al hecho de implicar al lector o espectador —en los vídeos tendrá que responder a preguntas que irán surgiendo durante el episodio— es una de las claves del éxito de esta propuesta. El mejor simulacro de cómo aprender tomando decisiones.

Ya a comienzos de los años setenta del pasado siglo, la Fundación Mapfre fue la impulsora del Diccionario de Seguros, un lexicón hoy consultable en línea (como el de la RAE) con un propósito claro y todavía vigente: traducir el vocabulario técnico a términos comprensibles para ayudar a los ciudadanos a entender todos esos conceptos abstrusos relacionados con las aseguradoras, la protección del patrimonio, el ahorro o la gestión de riesgos.

Se trata de un aspecto que, insiste Zuleta, lleva en el ADN de la compañía aseguradora más de medio siglo. “La educación financiera y la cultura aseguradora solo es útil si las personas la entienden y pueden aplicarla en su vida cotidiana. Por eso nos esforzamos por utilizar formatos cada vez más cercanos, prácticos y adaptados a los hábitos de aprendizaje actuales”.

Un universo nuevo de posibilidades (y de ruido)

Si bien la Bolsa española nace en 1831, en su primer siglo de vida aquel parqué está reservado casi en exclusiva a grandes fortunas, terratenientes, bancos o corporaciones. El primer gran hito popular de la inversión en España fue el que, a finales de los sesenta, en pleno desarrollismo económico, protagonizaron las Matildes, sobrenombre que recibieron por causa de la celebérrima campaña publicitaria del actor José Luis López Vázquez las acciones de Telefónica.

La era de internet y las redes sociales ha traído consigo otro cambio de profundo calado: se ha democratizado el acceso a las múltiples formas y vehículos de inversión, pero también se ha expandido la difusión de mensajes que, en opinión de Zuleta, son “simplistas o poco rigurosos o contrastados”. El discernimiento, la capacidad de pensamiento crítico, es más importante que nunca. “Nuestro papel nunca va a ser decir a las personas qué hacer con su dinero, sino dotarles del conocimiento y las herramientas para decidir con criterio y confianza”.

La brújula primordial debe ser siempre el objetivo que uno se marca: ¿para qué necesita ahorrar? “No es lo mismo”, cuenta Pachón, “intentar juntar dinero para celebrar una boda en el plazo de un año que ahorrar con la vista puesta en tu jubilación, dentro de 20 o 30 años”. Y, por lo tanto, no se puede asumir el mismo riesgo cuando se trata de un dinero que sí o sí vas a necesitar en pocos meses que cuando puedes mantener la inversión ahí, trabajando durante décadas (los horizontes temporales más largos permiten estrategias menos susceptibles a las oscilaciones de mercado).

Ahorrar no depende de grandes sumas: reservar una cantidad pequeña de forma constante puede marcar una gran diferencia con el tiempo Mónica Zuleta, directora Corporativa de Sostenibilidad de Mapfre

En ese camino, el acompañamiento de un profesional puede suponer el salto entre fracasar y cumplir el objetivo. Mapfre cuenta con una unidad específica, Mapfre Gestión Patrimonial, dedicada a la planificación financiera y al ejercicio de ese asesoramiento personalizado, un servicio que, como los tiempos, también se adapta hoy a cualquier tipo de cliente. Su propuesta parte del análisis de la situación para ayudarle a definir qué metas son plausibles y en qué plazos para, una vez definido eso, construir una estrategia. No se trata solo de recomendar un producto financiero u otro, sino de poner en orden las finanzas para establecer la mejor ruta posible en cada etapa de la vida. Como le ocurre a los protagonistas de Vecinos a todo riesgo.

Porque el ahorro es, sobre todo, un hábito que se aprende con dedicación y constancia, tal como aseguran desde Mapfre. Incluso cantidades pequeñas, si se reservan de manera sistemática, pueden tener un efecto significativo. Cambiarnos en algo la vida. Es un saber útil, imprescindible en una sociedad como la de hoy, y qué mejor que aprenderlo de la mano de quien lo enseña con llaneza, sin esconderse detrás de palabros incomprensibles.

World.title: Una red que garantiza buena salud
World.content:
La conectividad ya es una parte esencial de la atención sanitaria. Vodafone Empresas ayuda a organizaciones como ASISA a mantener operativos sus servicios, incluso cuando las circunstancias ponen a prueba toda la infraestructura

Una consulta médica ya no depende solo de la conversación entre paciente y profesional. Detrás de cada diagnóstico hay historias clínicas digitales, pruebas almacenadas en la nube y sistemas que conectan hospitales y especialistas en tiempo real. La sanidad se ha digitalizado a gran velocidad, apoyándose en una infraestructura tan esencial como invisible: las redes de comunicaciones.

Su importancia se hace evidente cuando algo falla. Una interrupción no significa solo quedarse sin internet. Puede impedir el acceso a pruebas diagnósticas, dificultar la coordinación entre equipos médicos, obligar a cancelar operaciones o desviar ambulancias. La actividad continúa, pero la operativa se vuelve más compleja.

Evitar que la conectividad se convierta en un punto vulnerable es una de las prioridades del sector. Vodafone Empresas combina redes fijas y móviles, gestión de infraestructuras, herramientas para garantizar la disponibilidad de aplicaciones críticas y soluciones de ciberseguridad. La experiencia de ASISA, uno de los grandes grupos aseguradores y sanitarios de España, muestra la importancia de contar con una infraestructura capaz de mantener la actividad diaria.

La infraestructura invisible de las redes

La transformación digital de la sanidad no consiste solo en incorporar nuevos equipos o desarrollar aplicaciones más avanzadas. También requiere redes capaces de mover grandes volúmenes de información de forma segura, ágil y sin interrupciones.

Para dar respuesta a estas necesidades, Vodafone Empresas combina conectividad fija y móvil, soluciones IoT, redes privadas, capacidades de edge computing y servicios en la nube. Un ecosistema tecnológico diseñado para entornos complejos, donde conviven múltiples sedes, miles de dispositivos conectados y una exigencia constante de disponibilidad.

José Antonio Martínez, Director de Cuentas Estratégicas de Vodafone Empresas, apunta tres tecnologías que están acelerando esta transformación. La primera es el 5G, que, precisa, “ha ampliado las capacidades de conexión, el ancho de banda y la disponibilidad de las comunicaciones”, facilitando el acceso en tiempo real a imágenes médicas de gran tamaño, como las resonancias magnéticas, que antes se entregaban en soportes físicos.

El 5G ha ampliado las capacidades de conexión, el ancho de banda y la disponibilidad de las comunicaciones José Antonio Martínez, Director de Cuentas Estratégicas de Vodafone Empresas

A ello se suman la inteligencia artificial (IA), que empieza a impulsar la modernización de procesos y servicios en las organizaciones sanitarias, y la nube, “que permite centralizar sistemas, almacenar imágenes médicas y garantizar que los profesionales autorizados puedan acceder a la información de forma rápida y segura desde distintos centros”.

Arquitectura de una sanidad digital

Con más de 3,5 millones de asegurados y una red de hospitales, clínicas, centros médicos y oficinas repartidos por toda España, ASISA depende de unas comunicaciones que deben funcionar de forma ininterrumpida. La gestión de citas, el acceso a las historias clínicas, la coordinación entre centros o la atención al asegurado descansan sobre una misma infraestructura digital.

Para modernizarla, Vodafone ha desplegado una red corporativa inteligente SD-WAN, ha renovado las redes locales de comunicación y ha reforzado la infraestructura WiFi de la compañía. El objetivo es dotar a la organización de una arquitectura más robusta, capaz de responder a las exigencias de una actividad asistencial cada vez más digitalizada.

“Buscábamos entrar en el siglo XXI como merecía nuestra actividad y aprovechar todas las posibilidades que ofrecían los avances tecnológicos”, aclara José Pereira, director de Medios de ASISA. La rapidez de las comunicaciones, añade, es determinante para la toma de decisiones: “Si las señales no llegan o no lo hacen con agilidad, las decisiones no se toman a tiempo, se toman mal o ni siquiera se dispone de la información necesaria para tomarlas”.

José Antonio Martínez, Director de Cuentas Estratégicas de Vodafone Empresas. Cedida por Vodafone

Las consecuencias pueden traducirse en retrasos en consultas y pruebas, dificultades para acceder a información clínica crítica, problemas de coordinación entre equipos y mayores riesgos para la seguridad de los datos. Pero una conectividad adecuada no solo reduce estos riesgos. También amplía las posibilidades de atención. “Cuanto mejor sea esa conexión y mayor la información que podamos intercambiar, más posibilidades se abren. En última instancia, hablamos de la salud y la vida de las personas”.

El día que la conectividad se puso a prueba

El apagón eléctrico de 2025 evidenció hasta qué punto las infraestructuras esenciales están interconectadas. “Existe una estrecha relación entre el sistema eléctrico, las telecomunicaciones y el sistema asistencial”, puntualiza Martínez. Por aquel entonces, ASISA ya contaba con la infraestructura de Vodafone. “Mantener la conectividad fue un alivio y nos permitió seguir operando en un momento especialmente complejo”, recuerda Pereira.

La incidencia puso a prueba la resiliencia de las redes. Vodafone logró mantener operativa su red móvil durante más tiempo gracias a una combinación de planificación previa, capacidad de respaldo y protocolos de emergencia. Según explica Martínez, la compañía tenía más autonomía en sus estaciones base y priorizó los servicios esenciales para prolongar la conectividad. Entre ellos se encontraban clientes estratégicos y organizaciones de misión crítica, como ASISA.

La experiencia también reforzó una idea compartida por ambas compañías: en situaciones de crisis, la tecnología es tan importante como la coordinación. “Existe una relación de colaboración”, afirma Pereira. Martínez coincide: “La confianza nos permite compartir los retos y la innovación nos ayuda a encontrar nuevas formas de afrontarlos”.

Innovar sin bajar la guardia

La IA abre nuevas posibilidades para la sanidad, desde el apoyo al análisis clínico hasta la personalización de la atención al paciente. Sin embargo, su adopción también plantea importantes desafíos. Entre ellos, la protección de los datos, la fiabilidad de las respuestas y el coste asociado a un uso intensivo de esta tecnología.

Mantener la conectividad [en el apagón eléctrico de 2025] fue un alivio y nos permitió seguir operando en un momento especialmente complejo José Pereira, Director de Medios de ASISA

También resulta clave definir en qué ámbitos puede aportar más valor. Como recuerda Pereira, “la IA puede ampliar la información disponible para el médico, pero las decisiones clínicas deben seguir apoyándose en su criterio profesional y en las circunstancias personales, sociales y médicas de cada paciente”.

Martínez coincide en que el coste puede convertirse en uno de los principales frenos a su implantación. Por ello, Vodafone apuesta por lo que denomina IA soberana: modelos que se ejecutan en la propia infraestructura de las organizaciones, reduciendo la dependencia de servicios externos y permitiendo una gestión más previsible de los recursos.

La otra gran preocupación es la ciberseguridad. A medida que la IA amplía sus capacidades, también lo hacen las herramientas de las que disponen los ciberdelincuentes para intentar acceder a sistemas sanitarios, robar información sensible o secuestrar datos. “No tenemos otra alternativa: los ataques pueden producirse en cuestión de segundos y alcanzar un volumen que dificulta la respuesta humana por sí sola”, señala Martínez. En este escenario, tanto los operadores tecnológicos como las propias organizaciones sanitarias tendrán que reforzar sus capacidades de prevención, detección y respuesta para proteger una infraestructura cada vez más crítica.

World.title: El mar impone su poder en la economía: estos son los puntos calientes capaces de someter al comercio mundial
World.content:
El bloqueo de Ormuz y los problemas en Bab-el-Mandeb y Panamá muestran la vulnerabilidad del planeta ante estos pasos estratégicos, con capacidad para disparar la inflación y en los que se juega el pulso por la hegemonía global

Más del 80% del comercio mundial de mercancías se transporta por mar, un enorme porcentaje que en tiempos de paz permite que los intercambios comerciales fluyan en calma pero que en tiempos convulsos muestra con crudeza el poder de los océanos sobre la economía y la capacidad de compra de los ciudadanos. El bloqueo del estrecho de Ormuz, una lengua de agua de poco más de 30 kilómetros de ancho por la que hasta febrero circulaba el 20% del petróleo que se consume en el mundo, es un ejemplo traumático y sin precedentes de cómo la interrupción del tráfico marítimo por un paso estratégico puede desencadenar un gigantesco efecto bola de nieve. Menos suministro de energía al mundo, súbito encarecimiento de los combustibles, coste disparado del transporte marítimo y más inflación. Imposible que la economía funcione de espaldas al mar.

La onda expansiva del bloqueo de Ormuz es planetaria y ha afectado también de lleno a la economía de Estados Unidos, donde Donald Trump probablemente ni imaginó que el conflicto desatado junto a Israel contra Irán fuera a durar tanto ni que fuese a encarecer hasta niveles récord el precio de la gasolina y el diésel para los estadounidenses. El desplome del tráfico marítimo por Ormuz ha impactado en las exportaciones de petróleo desde el golfo Pérsico y encarecido también su transporte por todo el globo: el aumento de los fletes es responsable de más de 30 dólares del precio del crudo, diez veces más que antes del conflicto.

Ormuz, con su gigantesca influencia sobre el suministro mundial de energía, es el ejemplo palmario de la importancia estratégica de los estrechos marítimos en el comercio y la economía global. Pero el mundo está plagado de otros tantos estrechos vitales para que fluyan las mercancías y en los que se juega el diseño del tablero geopolítico presente y futuro. Son los denominados chokepoints o puntos de estrangulamiento, puntos clave por los que pasa una parte muy importante del comercio mundial y extremadamente sensibles. Quien los controla, dispone de una palanca para mover el mundo.

No es necesario ni siquiera que se bloqueen, como sucede en Ormuz. Basta con que las condiciones meteorológicas o de seguridad se deterioren para que el efecto reverbere a nivel global. Es lo que ya está pasando con el estrecho de Bab-el-Mandeb, que separa el cuerno de África con la Península Arábiga y es la puerta de entrada desde el sur al mar Rojo para luego atravesar el canal de Suez y llegar a Europa. Los ataques de los rebeles hutíes de Yemen contra Arabia Saudí están poniendo en jaque la navegación por la zona, que no ha vuelto a ser la misma desde que en 2023 y 2024 esta milicia ya amenazara el tráfico por este estrecho en protesta por la ofensiva Israelí sobre Gaza.

Por motivos meteorológicos y no bélicos, el canal de Panamá es otro de los puntos calientes. El fenómeno de El Niño está causando una escasez de lluvia que ha obligado a reducir el tráfico y rebajar el calado de los buques en ese paso que une el océano Atlántico con el Pacífico, ya que el agua es necesaria para el funcionamiento del sistema de esclusas. Y sobre el estrecho de Malaca, situado entre Malasia, Singapur e Indonesia y una de las principales rutas del mundo al ser el principal corredor entre Asia y Europa por el océano Índico, también ha sobrevolado brevemente el riesgo de bloqueo. En abril el ministro de Finanzas de Indonesia llegó a sugerir un peaje, aunque rectificó enseguida. “Ormuz es el gran cuello energético; Malaca es el gran cuello comercial y energético de Asia”, apunta Alicia García Herrero, economista jefe de Natixis para Asia-Pacífico.

Ormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb, Suez, Panamá y Malaca son los grandes puntos críticos para el comercio marítimo. Cualquier sobresalto en estos pasos tiene efecto inmediato en la economía global. Pero hay más estrechos de vital importancia estratégica, como Gibraltar, Bósforo y Dardanelos en Turquía, Taiwán, Lombok y Sonda en Indonesia y el canal de la Mancha. Pasos cruciales que cada día vigila la poderosa industria marítima: los armadores propietarios de los buques, las navieras que gestionan el transporte de mercancías y las aseguradoras que cubren el riesgo de buques y mercancías y tramitan también las pólizas de guerra en caso de conflicto, ahora disparadas desde el estallido de la guerra en Irán. Las primas de seguro por riesgo de guerra en Ormuz han llegado a situarse entre el 3% y el 10% del valor del buque, frente al 0,25% previo a la guerra.

La Universidad de Oxford calculó en un estudio el año pasado que el valor estimado del comercio interrumpido en los cuellos de botella marítimos asciende a 192.000 millones de dólares al año, a causa de los retrasos en la entrega de mercancía, los cambios de ruta y las primas de las aseguradoras. “El mundo ha cambiado, pero las consecuencias en cuanto a las distancias de desvío y los costes son las mismas”, defiende por correo electrónico uno de sus autores, el profesor Jim Hall. En junio, en lo más álgido del bloqueo de Ormuz, Allianz estimó en más 125.000 millones de dólares el valor de la carga atrapada en los más de 1.000 buques anclados en la zona. La Organización Mundial del Comercio señala en su informe más reciente, del mes de octubre, que “el impulso alcista del comercio podría haberse estancado tras el estallido del conflicto en Oriente Próximo”. Así, el volumen de tráfico de contenedores a nivel mundial había alcanzado máximos en febrero de este año, pero en julio de 2026 ya había descendido un 2,5%, incluyendo una caída del 4,0% en el volumen de tráfico de los puertos chinos, según detalla la OMC.

Ormuz, dimensión energética y financiera

No shipping, no shopping (sin barcos no hay compras) es un conocido eslogan de la industria naviera que con Ormuz ha cobrado más fuerza que nunca. Nunca antes se había cerrado a cal y canto este paso marítimo y “no existe ningún antecedente histórico en el que el tráfico en un importante cuello de botella mundial se haya reducido a cero en cuestión de días”, según el Banco Internacional de Pagos (BIS). La institución señala que Ormuz es el estrecho con mayor dimensión económica del mundo no solo por su impacto en el suministro energético sino por sus implicaciones financieras. Por Ormuz pasaba antes de la guerra cerca de una quinta parte del petróleo y del gas natural licuado mundiales, pero también el 13% de todos los productos químicos, incluidos los fertilizantes y los plásticos.

Antes de la guerra cruzaban este enclave más de 130 buques diarios y ahora rondan los 20 al día, lo que ha disparado el precio de estas materias primas y sembrado la semilla de un repunte de la inflación generalizado al que por ahora, y mientras no se normalice el tráfico marítimo por la zona, no se ve techo. Ormuz ha forzado de hecho a los bancos centrales a elevar los tipos de interés —dos veces el BCE y una, la primera en tres años, la Fed— y es causante en buena parte del actual aumento de rentabilidades de los bonos, que encarece el coste de financiación. Para el BIS, este Estrecho tiene una “importancia crucial” para la estabilidad financiera mundial y es el más relevante del mundo en cuanto a su impacto en las condiciones crediticias. “El papel único de Ormuz como punto de estrangulamiento para los flujos energéticos mundiales lo convierte en una variable clave a la hora de evaluar las vulnerabilidades financieras”, advierte el BIS, por si no quedara clara su importancia estratégica.

Militares estadounidenses contemplan el tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz. Scpo Amanda Dunford/Dod (Zuma Press / Europa Press / CONTACTO)

Los fletes y la cadena inflacionista

Mover una tonelada de petróleo desde el golfo Pérsico a China cuesta unos 237 dólares, frente a los 25 que costaba en febrero, antes de la guerra. Por barril, el flete ha pasado de unos 3,5 dólares a superar los 30, lo que supone más de una cuarta parte del precio del brent, frente a un porcentaje mínimo de entre el 2% y el 3% antes de la guerra. El coste del transporte se está convirtiendo de hecho en el gran obstáculo que impide que se relaje el precio del combustible, incluso a pesar de que los países del Golfo están comenzando a exportar petróleo con más intensidad. La crisis de suministro está mutando en crisis de transporte marítimo. Y sigue muy vivo el riesgo de que la tensión bélica se reanude en el golfo Pérsico, un temor que ha impulsado en los últimos días el brent a máximos de abril, sobre los 116 dólares.

“Aunque haya suministro, escasea la flota y las rutas son ahora más largas. Lo que ha ocurrido con la guerra es que la oferta de barcos ha caído por varias vías a la vez. Aunque la flota mundial es la misma (se tarda años en construir un barco), muchos petroleros se han quedado atrapados dentro del Golfo. Además, los viajes se han alargado: los cargamentos que antes iban del Golfo a Asia se han sustituido por crudo de orígenes más lejanos, lo que supone más días en el mar y menos barcos disponibles”, explica Jorge Molinero, analista de la plataforma de materias primas Sparta. A esto hay que sumar que las pólizas de guerra de los petroleros se han disparado, un coste que los armadores trasladan al precio final del flete.

Más ejemplos: la ruta de un petrolero de EE UU a Europa ha alcanzado en octubre unos 188 dólares por tonelada, máximo histórico, casi cuatro veces más que en febrero. “Los petroleros se han desplazado y los viajes son más largos, así que falta flota en todas partes”, añade Molinero. Con las nuevas tensiones en Bab-el-Mandeb, el buque que evita el mar Rojo para transportar crudo a Europa y opta por rodear África por el cabo de Buena Esperanza añade hasta dos semanas más de navegación.

Los petroleros se han convertido en el bien más valioso del transporte marítimo, en especial para quien no posee flota propia y debe alquilar uno. Según la consultora especializada en comercio marítimo Clarksons Research, los ingresos medios ponderados de los petroleros habían superado los 200.000 dólares al día a finales de septiembre. Y en el caso de los superpetroleros VLCC, con capacidad de carga de dos toneladas, han alcanzado los 600.000 dólares diarios, unas 17 veces su media de los últimos 10 años. Pero el impacto de la interrupción de la navegación por Ormuz va mucho más allá del petróleo y se contagia a toda la cadena de transporte. “El aumento de los precios del crudo y de los productos refinados está haciendo subir el coste del combustible marítimo, el combustible para aviones y el transporte de mercancías por carretera, lo que a su vez encarece los costes de transporte a nivel mundial”, confirma Izabela Listowska, la analista responsable de Transporte de S&P Global Ratings.

Las navieras de contenedores también han aplicado recargos de emergencia para compensar el aumento de los costes de combustible y de explotación, los gastos de cambio de ruta y el incremento de las primas de seguro. “Por ejemplo, para un contenedor que transporta 10.000 pares de zapatos para adultos, un recargo de emergencia de 3.000 dólares por contenedor equivaldría a un coste adicional de transporte marítimo de 0,30 dólares por par”, añade Listowska por correo electrónico. La analista explica que las tarifas en la ruta de China a la costa oeste de EE UU han subido hasta los 7.500 dólares por contenedor —tomando una medida estándar de 40 pies—, frente a los 1.850 dólares de finales de febrero.

China, del “collar de perlas” al Ártico

La interrupción del tráfico por Ormuz ha tenido por tanto impacto no solo en los precios de la energía sino en el conjunto de la logística del transporte marítimo, pero si hay un estrecho cuyo bloqueo sería un verdadero mazazo para el comercio global es el de Malaca. “Por él circula alrededor de un tercio del comercio marítimo mundial y, en volumen reciente, más petróleo que por Ormuz (unos 23 millones de barriles diarios frente a unos 21). Para China, Japón y Corea es crítico: cerca del 80% del petróleo importado por China pasa por ahí”, explica Alicia García Herrero.

Hay alternativas al paso por Malaca, como los estrechos de Lombok y Sonda en Indonesia, pero son más caras y lentas y en previsión de un posible bloqueo de ese enclave estratégico, China ha desarrollado un entramado de oleoductos que traen el crudo desde Rusia, Asia Central y Myanmar y de puertos de influencia por el Índico. Es el denominado “collar de perlas”, bases comerciales chinas pero que no esconden su potencial de base militar llegado el caso, como el puerto de Gwadar en Pakistán; Hambantota, en Sri Lanka; Kyaukpyu, en Myanmar o Chittagong, en Bangladesh. “China es una potencia y está rodeada de gobiernos que pueden llegar a ser una amenaza, como Japón o Taiwán”, explica Emilio Rodríguez-Díaz, director del Departamento de Ciencias y Técnicas de la Navegación y Construcciones Navales de la Universidad de Cádiz y especialista en seguridad marítima.

La protección del comercio y la geopolítica se funden en la estrategia marítima de China, que ha estrenado una nueva ruta comercial regular entre Asia y Europa a través del Ártico, utilizando la Ruta Marítima del Norte bajo control ruso. Aunque es muy estacional y mueve volúmenes de carga reducidos, para Pekín es la ruta de la seda del hielo, ya que permite navegar de China a Europa en unos 20 días —la mitad de una travesía por Suez— y evita además Ormuz, Malaca y el mar Rojo. Como explica García Herrero, “no sustituye a Suez ni a Malaca a gran escala, pero sí añade una carta en el pulso con Washington”.

La disputa por la hegemonía mundial también se juega por tanto en el mar. Lo explica el afán de Trump por controlar Ormuz o Groenlandia. “Estados Unidos ha sido durante décadas el gran defensor de la libertad de navegación y ahora busca asegurarse el control de puntos concretos: escolta a los petroleros de sus socios del golfo en Ormuz mientras bloquea las exportaciones iraníes, llegó a plantear en julio cobrar por esa protección y ha firmado con Dinamarca y Groenlandia un acuerdo que le permite ampliar su presencia militar en la isla”, corrobora Judith Arnal, investigadora principal del Real Instituto Elcano.

Un antes y un después

Con Donald Trump buscando el control de rutas marítimas clave y con Irán planeando el cobro de peajes por Ormuz, ¿qué cabe esperar para la seguridad del transporte marítimo? En Ormuz está el nudo gordiano a partir del que desenredar la escalada de precios de la energía y los fletes pero “para que el tráfico marítimo por el estrecho de Ormuz vuelva a la normalidad, tendrían que cesar los bloqueos y los ataques a los buques y garantizarse un paso seguro”, avisa Niels Rasmussen, analista jefe de transporte marítimo de BIMCO (Baltic and International Maritime Council), la principal asociación internacional de armadores y navieras. De momento, añade Rasmussen, la mayoría de armadores cree que los riesgos de cruzar Ormuz son demasiado elevados.

La vuelta a la normalidad solo será posible con un acuerdo fiable y duradero entre Irán y EE UU y puede que ni siquiera así. “Las aseguradoras y los armadores exigen pruebas de una estabilidad sostenida antes de considerar como normal una zona que anteriormente se encontraba en conflicto. Tras el memorando de entendimiento firmado en junio entre EE UU e Irán, observamos que volvió al mercado una mayor capacidad de seguro, pero las primas se mantuvieron muy por encima de los niveles previos a la guerra”, puntualiza Listowska.

Bajar el inmenso y traumático suflé que ha causado en el transporte marítimo la guerra en Irán no será fácil cuando, en el momento que sea, termine el conflicto. La reapertura de un estrecho puede ser más o menos rápida si hay acuerdo político pero no tanto la recuperación de los niveles de seguridad previos al conflicto y el respeto a las reglas de navegación. “Irán ha cobrado a algunos buques por cruzar Ormuz y tramita una ley para formalizarlo. Y Estados Unidos llegó a anunciar un peaje del 20% sobre la carga”, recuerda Arnal. La cicatriz que la guerra en Irán vaya a dejar en el comercio marítimo es una incógnita, aunque el impacto ahora sea máximo. “Me resisto a aceptar la idea de que el derecho internacional que rige los mares haya desaparecido de alguna manera simplemente porque se estén produciendo graves disturbios regionales en determinadas partes del mundo”, explica Antonios Tzanakopoulos, catedrático de Derecho Internacional Público en la Facultad de Derecho de la Universidad de Oxford, que apunta además que los riesgos para la navegación fluctúan considerablemente con el tiempo. “Hace más de una década, en el golfo de Adén esos riesgos eran significativos debido a la piratería, y hoy en día lo son menos”, añade Tzanakopoulos. Solo el tiempo dirá si el cierre insólito de Ormuz dejará un transporte marítimo más caro de forma irremediable.

World.title: Cabinet sets out AI plan, seeks partners beyond US and China
World.content:
The cabinet is establishing a vision of how to integrate AI into Dutch society so as to take advantage of its benefits, control reliance on foreign powers and strengthen national security.

Digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts released 28-page vision letter to parliament on Friday, acknowledging that AI will “largely determine our future”.

“We want a Netherlands where AI makes everyone better and helps us move forward. Where a nurse has more time for patients, entrepreneurs can grow, and technology helps us with the major challenges of our time,” she said.

“That requires choices. Where do we want to lead the way and where do we draw the line? We don’t have to be able to do everything ourselves, but we do want to decide for ourselves which direction we take.”

The vision names Canada, Japan, Singapore and South Korea as “middle powers” the Netherlands wants to work with, alongside other EU member states.

It also says the Netherlands will keep working on “stable and predictable relations” with the US and China. The letter notes that the Netherlands has joined Pax Silica, a US-led partnership on chips, computing power and AI infrastructure.

The only funding figure in the vision is €120 million for Dutch participation in an EU-wide AI project, which was already set aside in September. The letter says more “targeted and structural investment” is needed in infrastructure, talent and research, but gives no amounts.

“This is a toothless tiger,” Volt leader Laurens Dassen told broadcaster NOS. “AI should be a top priority. It isn’t if there is no budget.”

Plans for computing power and datacentres, which use large amounts of electricity and water, will follow in the first quarter of 2027.

The cabinet is also exploring whether to set up a Dutch AI safety institute modelled on the UK’s AI Security Institute. An advisory report is due in December.

Aerdts and the education minister plan to agree a “media pact” with public and private media organisations, which will also cover how AI systems use journalistic content. No details on that have been given yet.

World.title: Activists occupy site of Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam
World.content:
Police are clearing a building site in Westpoort after pro-Palestinian activists occupied it this morning in protest to the city’s plans to build a massive data centre there, which will be leased to Microsoft.

Microsoft has acknowledged selling cloud and computing software to the Israeli military. The action was originally organised by the climate and justice group Geef Tegengas and joined by Extinction Rebellion and other groups. Other groups turned up and some stormed the site, and hung up Palestinian flags.

There was a confrontation between the police and activists this morning, according to broadcaster NOS, although the demonstration was allowed to continue after police surrounded them.

Some activists climbed onto cranes and the roof of the construction.

The €1 billion, 78MW campus is being built by Pure DC and is let in full to Microsoft. Critics say it gets round the 2022 national ban on hyperscale data centres because on paper it is three smaller data centres. According to NRC, it will use as much electricity in a year as the whole of Amsterdam.

Microsoft told NOS that it is aware of the demonstration. “We understand that this project stirs up strong emotions and respect people’s right to express their opinions peacefully. However, we do not condone actions that violate the law or endanger people’s safety.”

World.title: Cancelled Jewish exhibition back on table after mayor steps in
World.content:
Amersfoort Mayor Lucas Bolsius has said he wants a cancelled Jewish exhibition at the Amsersfoort Museum to go ahead, and the museum has now agreed to look at how it can be staged. The museum announced earlier this week that it was cancelling the exhibition due to the situation in the Middle East and rising global tensions.

The exhibition, “300 Years Amersfoort Shul”, has been years in the making, and its last-minute cancellation has caused outrage in the Jewish community.

“Apparently, many struggle to distinguish between Jewish identity and Israel. The reflex to cancel performances in situations like this is becoming increasingly common across the cultural sector,” Alexander van Dijkhuizen, chairman of the Jewish Community of Amersfoort, is reported as saying in US Jewish newspaper The Algemeiner.

“It is essential not only to reflect on the past, but also to acknowledge the difficult circumstances facing the Jewish community today.”

Hard to manage

When museum director Paul Baltus cancelled the exhibition, he said possible reactions to it were hard to manage.

“As a small and vulnerable organisation, I do not want to expose my staff to that kind of pressure,” he told the AD. “While security guards can be hired and cameras installed, the reality is that our volunteers would still have to deal with a range of possible reactions.”

But the mayor said he wasn’t informed about that decision, and he met with the museum and Amersfoort’s Jewish community on Thursday to discuss how the exhibition can go ahead.

“I am enormously saddened,” the mayor told the city council on Wednesday. “Jewish history and present-day life belong to our city. That must get the attention it deserves.” He said it was painful that the community was being made to feel it is not permitted to exist.

After Thursday’s meeting, the city said in a statement that the city, the museum and the Jewish community would look together at how 300 years of Jewish life in Amersfoort could be shown in an exhibition. “It was a good and intensive conversation,” Bolsius said. “We jointly concluded that we consider it important that there is an exhibition telling the story of 300 years of Jewish culture in Amersfoort.”

The Amersfoort Synagogue dates back to 1727 and is the oldest functioning Ashkenazi synagogue in Western Europe. The Jewish community has planned a wide-ranging programme of concerts and performances to mark the synagogue’s 300th anniversary.

Earlier this week, a Jewish student association lecture at Maastricht University was cancelled less than an hour before it was due to start, with the university saying it couldn’t guarantee participants’ safety.

World.title: Skaters get three hours on natural ice as first frost arrives
World.content:
The first frost has appeared after temperatures dropped below freezing overnight in parts of the Netherlands, in Brabant, Limburg and parts of Zeeland, according to the national weather service KNMI.

It also allowed the season’s first natural ice skating in Gelderland for a couple of hours in early morning.

The lowest temperature was recorded in Woensdrecht in Brabant, at minus 1.2°. Ell in Limburg reached minus 1.1° and Westdorpe in Zeeland minus 0.4°.

It does not yet count as an official frost day though. For that, the temperature at the KNMI’s base in De Bilt, near Utrecht, has to fall below zero. Overnight it stayed at 0.8° there.

In Winterswijk, in Gelderland, the local skating club opened the country’s first natural ice rink of the season, even though there was only ground frost there. The club uses special techniques to make ice quickly.

“When you tell people that, they say ‘it can’t be done’. But it can,” chairman Auke Spijkstra told broadcaster NOS. “It’s wonderful to see all those enthusiastic people.” About 20 skaters took to the ice. The sun soon melted it, and the rink closed again at around 10am.

World.title: Verwey-Jonker Institute facing bankruptcy amid AI rise
World.content:
The Verwey-Jonker Institute, an independent research institute in Utrecht, appears to be on the brink of bankruptcy, citing budget cuts and the rise of AI as the culprits. The Institute has applied to court for a suspension of payments.

Moving to a less expensive location and downsizing its board hasn’t been enough to save the beleaguered Institute. Broadcaster NOS also reported there’s been unrest within the agency’s leadership.

The Verwey-Jonker Institute, founded in 1993, addresses societal issues, providing research to governments, municipalities and others with “social value and impact”, according to its website. They work on issues such as poverty, youth, education, discrimination and domestic violence, among others.

The Institute says technological developments mean many of their clients are now using AI instead of engaging researchers.

While they say they want to continue their work, it will now be up to an administrator to see just how they can do that.

World.title: Graffiti group posts video of attack on Amsterdam metro
World.content:
A group of some 20 masked and hooded graffiti writers stopped a metro in Amsterdam Nieuw-West and sprayed the entire train with paint within minutes, leaving passengers inside stranded.

The action took place at the Henk Sneevlietweg stop last Saturday on Halloween. A video uploaded Tuesday on YouTube by the anonymous graffiti writers’ group Locos Worldwide, titled “Amsterdam Nightmare”, shows the sprayers entering the station and speed-spraying the train in orange, purple and black before running away cheering.

They also threw a bicycle onto the tracks and spray painted the driver’s window, leaving the train unable to move.

Shaken and shocked

“Our driver is quite shocked by the incident,” a spokesman for Amsterdam transport company GVB said. “We can also imagine that this was a frightening situation for travellers.”

The GVB, which called the incident a “serious form of vandalism”, has filed a police report. It’s still not known who is responsible for the action, but the GVB says it plans to seek compensation from the “perpetrators” when they are identified.

They tagged the train with apparent acronyms ‘NSPSKU’ and ‘LCSNTC’. NSPS has been tagged on transit vehicles in the past.

Police say they are taking the incident “seriously” and have appealed to the public to come forward with any video images they may have.

The GVB says that while graffiti does happen, the scale of the Halloween night action is extraordinary. Not only was the driver severely shaken, but the ordeal was a “potentially terrifying situation for passengers as well”.

And, according to the GVB, it put them at risk. “There was not only a subway smeared, but also a bicycle thrown on the track. That entails major security risks,” a spokesman said.

Five years ago, Locos Worldwide uploaded another video showing a masked group spray painting an in-service Amsterdam metro. The group also posts similar actions that have taken place across Europe, including in Paris, Madrid and Copenhagen.

World.title: Five of seven Dutch reptile species in decline, CBS says
World.content:
Five of the seven reptile species found in the Netherlands have declined over the past 12 years, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS and research foundation RAVON.

Only the wall lizard has grown in number since 2014, while the slow worm has stayed stable. On average, reptile populations have fallen since 2014 and are now roughly back at their 1994 level.

The viviparous, the common lizard, has fared worst, with numbers down almost 75% since 1994. The smooth snake has fallen by more than 60% since 1997, and the adder and grass snake are also in decline.

CBS said climate change may be hitting species that prefer cooler, wetter conditions, such as the common lizard and the adder. Overgrown habitats and fewer insects to eat are also likely factors.

Wall lizard numbers, by contrast, have risen more than five-fold since 1995, helped by the warmer climate.

World.title: 2,000-year-old Vandal artefacts anonymously handed to Polish museum
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A collection of artefacts associated with the Vandals and dating back almost 2,000 years has been handed anonymously to a museum in eastern Poland. The collection includes a sword, spear and javelin heads, shield components and spurs. Museum staff do not know who originally discovered the burial or exactly where it was located, leaving the circumstances of the find largely a mystery. The Father Stanisław Staszic Museum in Hrubieszów announced in a Facebook post that the objects had been passed to them anonymously through an intermediary. The items are in poor condition and will undergo urgent conservation, with the iron components of the weapons particularly vulnerable after centuries in the ground. They were also exposed to high temperatures during a burial practice in which the deceased was burned along with their personal belongings. The museum says that the nature of the objects indicates that their owner held a high social position. The most notable object is a sword preserved in three pieces, reflecting the Vandal practice of deliberately breaking or bending weapons and other grave artefacts as part of funeral rituals. The collection also contains two spearheads, both broken. Other items include a shield boss with a spike, a shield grip, a fragment of a knife, a belt buckle and two spurs. Fragments of a bone comb and a bronze fibula, used to fasten a cloak, were also recovered. The circumstances surrounding the discovery and recovery of the objects remain unknown, but the museum says that, according to the information it has received, the burial site was discovered in an agricultural field several years ago in the municipality of Werbkowice. “We intend to verify the exact location through archaeological excavations, most likely next summer,” they added. “Based on the information we have gathered, there are strong indications that there may be more similar burials in the area that have been disturbed by agricultural work.” The opportunity to recover the objects and transfer them to an appropriate institution arose only recently. The museum said that a local metal detectorist played a key role in arranging the transfer, acting as an intermediary in securing the artefacts. The recovery of the artefacts follows another recent archaeological discovery in the same region. In August, the museum announced that a metal boss from a warrior’s shield dating to the second century was found at a scrap metal yard near Hrubieszów. The Vandals were an ancient Germanic people believed to have reached the territories of present-day Poland around the 3rd or 2nd century BC. They lived in the region for several centuries and are generally associated by researchers with the Przeworsk culture, which flourished across parts of present-day Poland during the Iron Age and Roman period. Around the turn of the 4th and 5th centuries AD, amid the expansion of the Huns, they left Central Europe and moved westwards into the declining Roman Empire. As the Vandals left Central Europe, the Slavic population gradually moved into the region over the following centuries. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish deputy PM proposes “constitutional reset” to resolve crisis around top court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The leader of one of the parties in Poland’s ruling coalition has put forward plans for a “constitutional reset” that he hopes can resolve the crisis around the country’s top court. The proposal, presented on Thursday by deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, head of the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), would remove all current judges on the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) and allow new judges to be chosen only with the approval of 60% of members of parliament and the president. To take effect, the measure would require amending Poland’s constitution, something that has happened only twice since the document was adopted in 1997 and which also requires a three-fifths majority in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament. Deeskalacja sytuacji wokół Trybunału Konstytucyjnego jest konieczna aby przywrócić obywatelom niezależny sąd konstytucyjny. Apelują o to przedstawiciele organizacji społecznych, Rada Przedsiębiorców, Naczelna Rada Adwokacka, Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka i Episkopat Polski.… pic.twitter.com/3RCsKRlSiM — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 5, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz’s announcement comes amid the fallout from events last Friday, when eight new judges elected to the TK this year by the government’s majority in parliament seized control of the court. They announced that its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, had been suspended for failing to fulfil his duties, including by refusing to allow most of those judges to take up their seats on the court. Święczkowski denounced the takeover as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the tribunal’s remaining six judges, who, like him, were appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, which brought the TK under its political influence when it ruled from 2015 to 2023. As well as pitting judges aligned with the national-conservative PiS, which is now the main opposition party, and the current more liberal government against one another, the dispute also centres around the legitimacy of certain judges. The government points to the fact that PiS unlawfully appointed three judges to the TK in 2015. As a result, both Polish and European courts have found the tribunal in its current form to be illegitimate. Meanwhile, Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of the eight judges appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority this year, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 The standoff has led some NGOs and experts to call for a “constitutional reset”, whereby the TK would be reformed to make the process of selecting judges more consensual and less politicised. Indeed, the current government even proposed legislation in 2024 that would have required new TK judges to be approved by a three-fifths parliamentary majority. The plans would also have removed unlawfully appointed judges from the PiS era and annulled rulings they were involved in. That prompted the president at the time, Andrzej Duda, who was also aligned with PiS, to send the bills to the TK, which was still packed with PiS-era judges, for assessment. The tribunal rejected them as unconstitutional the following year. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Now, Kosiniak-Kamysz has proposed new legislation intended to resolve the issue. His solution would create a mechanism under which parliament, at the request of the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS), could declare the TK “permanently incapable of performing its duties”. Such a status could only be declared with the support of a three-fifths majority of both houses of parliament – the Sejm and the Senate – combined. It would have to come at the request of the KRS because, says Kosiniak-Kamysz, the terms of judges cannot be shortened without the participation of other judges. The process of appointing new TK judges would involve the speaker of the Sejm proposing candidates after obtaining the opinions of the heads of the Supreme Court and the Supreme Administrative Court – which are separate from the TK – as well as professional bodies representing legal professions. The candidates proposed by the speaker would also have to receive the prior consent of the president. For a new TK judge to be approved, they would have to receive the support of three fifths of members of the Sejm and Senate combined. 💬 336 głosów posłów i senatorów. To wykracza poza większość jakąkolwiek koalicyjną dzisiaj sformułowaną – @KosiniakKamysz w Warszawie pic.twitter.com/iLUuM5TSxQ — 🍀 PSL (@nowePSL) November 5, 2026 Whereas TK judges currently all serve nine-year terms, under Kosiniak-Kamysz’s proposal, five of the judges would serve three-year terms, five of them six-year terms, and the final five would serve for nine years. Unlike now, the new judges would not have to swear their oath before the president, but before parliament. Kosiniak-Kamysz emphasised, however, that the measure was intended as a “one-time” emergency tool. “Later, we will return to the method of selecting judges described today in the constitution, or a better one, if there is a majority for it.” The current method of choosing new TK judges requires only the support of a majority in the Sejm. However, judges must then swear an oath “before the president”, an issue that has become a bone of contention this year. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz’s plans would require changes to Poland’s constitution, which specifies the manner in which TK judges are chosen. A constitutional amendment requires the support of a three-fifths majority in the Sejm and a simple majority in the Senate. It does not need presidential approval. PSL itself has only 28 members of the 460-seat Sejm and four senators. Kosiniak-Kamysz acknowledged that “it won’t be an easy road” to win the necessary support for his idea. He appealed not only to his fellow ruling parties, but also to opposition groups that have expressed their backing for a constitutional reset, such as the centre-right Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) and far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). On Thursday evening, one of Confederation’s leaders, Sławomir Mentzen, shared a photo of himself meeting Kosiniak-Kamysz, with the caption: “It’s going in the right direction”. However, some voices within the ruling coalition expressed scepticism towards the idea. Borys Budka, a former leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) – which is the largest governing party – said it was “hard to imagine changing the constitution alongside someone like PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński”. Tomasz Trela of The Left (Lewica) likewise said that, “if anyone thinks The Left will change the constitution arm in arm with PiS, they’re mistaken”, reports Polsat News. World.title: Chinese fashion platform Shein to invest €500 million in Polish logistics hub

We cannot do what we do without your support. Chinese fast fashion platform Shein has announced a €500 million (2.2 billion zloty) investment to expand its logistics centre in Poland, a move it says will create around 2,000 new jobs by the end of this year. The announcement comes amid growing controversy over the impact of Chinese e-commerce platforms on European businesses and follows a recent decision by the European Union to introduce a special fee on low-value parcels sent from outside the EU and European Free Trade Area. SHEIN investește 500 mil. euro în Polonia. Extinde hub-ul logistic europeanhttps://t.co/WNbib4dFta pic.twitter.com/KiI1AB4wFM — Cristi Dorombach (@piticu21) November 4, 2026 The investment will expand Shein’s existing logistics facility in Magnice, near the city of Wrocław in southwestern Poland, which has been operating since 2022. The expansion will bring total employment at the site to around 10,000 by creating 2,000 jobs in logistics, supply chain management, technology and warehouse operations, according to local news service Wroclaw.pl. The facility will also host 6,500 autonomous robots for sorting items. Shein says that the move will help it cut delivery times in Europe, allowing some orders to arrive within 48 hours. “This investment in Poland clearly demonstrates our commitment and belief in the potential of the European market,” said Leonard Lin, the firm’s global head of public affairs. “Poland has become one of the pillars of our operations in Europe,” he added. “This latest investment is a testament to our confidence in the country’s potential, the competencies of its workforce, and its business environment.” The expansion comes as Shein faces a tougher trading environment in Europe. Its sales in the region fell by 13.9% year-on-year to $3.77 billion in the second quarter, while net profit dropped by 67%. The decline comes as the EU steps up efforts to curb the influx of low-cost imports from Chinese platforms such as Shein, Temu and AliExpress, which European retailers say pose unfair competition. In July, the bloc introduced a €3 fee on parcels worth less than €150. From 1 November, a further €2 handling fee was added to all imported parcels, regardless of their value, to cover customs processing costs. China overtook Germany to become Poland’s biggest source of imports for the first time in July, ending a period of around 35 years in which Germany had consistently held top spot https://t.co/U6rQwfEJ7I — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 Shein has also faced accusations of labour-law violations at its facilities in China, including concerns that it may use cotton produced through forced labour. The company disputes many of the allegations, saying that it prohibits forced and child labour and regularly inspects working conditions at its suppliers. China is an increasingly important trading partner in Poland. In July, it overtook Germany to become Poland’s largest source of imports for the first time, driven by rising purchases of cars, computer hardware and consumer goods. Poland has detained and charged six people – five Poles and one Russian – suspected of running an operation to illegally supply Russia with military components. Investigators say that over 2 million zloty (€450,000) worth of equipment was smuggled into the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The arrests, which took place on 21 October and 2 November, were announced on Thursday morning by Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) and National Prosecutor’s Office. 🚨 ROSYJSKI WYWIAD. PRZEMYT CZĘŚCI DO PRODUKCJI UZBROJENIA. 6 ZATRZYMANYCH.@ABW_GOV_PL rozbiła grupę podejrzaną o działalność na rzecz rosyjskich służb specjalnych. 🔴6⃣ osób zatrzymanych, 🔴2⃣1⃣przeszukanych lokalizacji, 🔴 4⃣osoby z zarzutami szpiegostwa – wszystkie trafiły… pic.twitter.com/L90n3rf5rY — ABW (@ABW_GOV_PL) November 5, 2026 Prosecutors report that all six suspects have been charged with participating in an organised criminal group that sought to export weapon components from Poland to Russia in violation of a ban on such trade. Four of the suspects have also been charged under Poland’s espionage law, accused of acting on behalf of Russian intelligence in return for financial benefits. Those four individuals have been placed in pretrial detention. The other two were released with preventative measures put in place. The ABW says that the criminal group “illegally supplied Russia with significant quantities of military components, including those used in the production of ammunition and weapons systems”. “This type of activity may lead to the strengthening of the Russian arms industry and the military capabilities of the Russian Federation, and thus pose a serious threat to Poland’s security and interests,” wrote the agency. Prosecutors say that the group operated at least between June 2023 and December 2025 in Poland, Lithuania and Russia. Members were responsible for procuring goods and transporting them to Kaliningrad, which borders Poland and Lithuania. “Vehicles equipped with hidden compartments were used to transport the goods,” wrote the prosecutor’s office. “The suspects repeatedly crossed the Polish-Russian border, and some of the transports were intercepted by Polish border guards.” Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, revealed that the six suspects include five Polish citizens, aged 25 to 52, and one Russian woman, aged 37. Onet, a leading news website, reports, based on unnamed sources, that the Russian citizen acted as a liaison between the group and the foreign intelligence agency behind the operation. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 6 osób podejrzanych o udział w zorganizowanej grupie przestępczej działającej przeciwko Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. Wśród zatrzymanych jest pięciu Polaków w wieku od 25 do 52 lat i 37-letnia Rosjanka. 🛑 Sąd – pod zarzutem szpiegostwa -… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 5, 2026 Poland has seen a huge rise in espionage cases in recent years. The ABW launched 48 investigations related to espionage last year, more than twice as many as in 2024. In those two years taken together, there were more espionage investigations than over the previous three decades combined. Last month, a Polish man was jailed for five and a half years for spying on behalf of Russia. The tasks assigned to him included reconnaissance of an airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky while he travelled through Poland. In July, a Russian married couple with refugee status in Poland were convicted of working as spies on behalf of Moscow. In October, a member of Poland’s military reserve, who holds both Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, was detained on suspicion of espionage. World.title: Polish far-right leader Braun to face second trial
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun will again stand trial, after prosecutors filed an indictment against him for a series of anti-Ukrainian, anti-Jewish, anti-LGBT and anti-EU acts committed during his presidential election campaign last year. Braun is already separately on trial for a number of other alleged crimes, including an attack on a Jewish religious ceremony in parliament. He is also facing further charges for a range of other alleged offences. Grzegorz Braun stanie przed sądem. Prokuratura Okręgowa w Warszawie skierowała dziś akt oskarżenia za zuchwałą kradzież flag Ukrainy w Białej Podlaskiej i Unii Europejskiej w Katowicach, zniszczenie wystawy LGBT w Sejmie oraz zniesławienie organizatorów akcji Żonkile i Muzeum… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 4, 2026 On Wednesday, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw announced that it had indicted Braun for four alleged crimes. It was able to do so after the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, stripped him of immunity earlier this year. One of the charges, for criminal defamation, stems from Braun’s claim, during a televised presidential debate in April last year, that the yellow paper daffodils distributed each year in Warsaw to mark the anniversary of the 1943 Jewish Ghetto Uprising against German Nazi rule are “symbols of shame”. Prosecutors say that Braun’s words were “extremely xenophobic, manipulative and aggressive”, and that they defamed the organisers of the daffodil campaign, in particular the POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews in Warsaw. During the same debate, Braun also warned about the “Judaisation” of Poland, saying that “Jews have far too much say in Polish affairs”. That prompted protests by some of his opponents, one of whom filed a notification to prosecutors. Two other charges relate to thefts of flags. In one incident, Braun and his supporters removed a Ukrainian flag hanging outside city hall in the town of Biała Podlaska during a campaign event. In another, he removed a European Union flag from the industry ministry in the city of Katowice and set it on fire. Braun regularly rails against what he calls the “Ukrainisation” of Poland, warning of the supposed dangers of having so many Ukrainian refugees and migrants in the country. He is also a vocal critic of the EU. On those and other issues, Braun’s rhetoric often echoes Russian propaganda. The final charge, of destruction of property, relates to an incident in June 2025, when Braun vandalised an exhibition about the LGBT+ community in the Polish parliament. He regularly condemns what he calls the “perversions” of LGBT+ people, and has called for homosexuality to be criminalised. The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes. The decision marks the sixth time it has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial https://t.co/O9FN1YbchE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 The charges Braun faces carry prison sentences of up to five years in the case of destruction of property, and up to one year in the case of criminal defamation and theft. Additionally, the deputy leader of Braun’s Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party, Roman Fritz, was indicted for assisting in the theft of the EU flag, while four other men (who have not waived their right to anonymity under Polish law) were indicted for their alleged roles in stealing both the EU and Ukrainian flags. All four incidents for which Braun has been indicted took place when he was campaigning for the May 2025 presidential elections, in which he finished a surprise fourth, with 6.3% of the vote. Since then, KKP has continued to perform strongly in polls, with its support currently standing at around 9%. If it obtained that kind of result at next year’s parliamentary elections, it would be likely to play a major role in deciding what kind of government could be formed. Our essential guide to Poland's parliamentary elections, which will take place one year from now. How does voting work? What do polls suggest the outcome will be? Which issues may animate the campaign? And what role will President Nawrocki play? https://t.co/fmdoFpBaxz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2026 Much of Braun’s political brand has been built around provocative statements and actions. The politician is already on trial for his attack on a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony taking place in parliament, at which he put out the candles with a fire extinguisher. In their statement on Wednesday, the Warsaw prosecutor’s office noted that the latest hearings in that trial had been cancelled after Braun presented a medical certificate justifying his absence. However, the prosecutors pointed out that, last Friday, the day that the hearings had been due to begin, Braun attended a protest by opposition supporters outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw, which that evening had been taken over by government-backed judges. Braun was pictured “jostling with police riot police, addressing the crowd and giving interviews”, showing “no signs of health problems that would prevent him from attending the hearing”, wrote the prosecutors. They have therefore asked the court to investigate the doctor who issued the medical certificate. Polish political leaders have reacted to the results of Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which the Democrats won control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans. The outcome was welcomed by Poland’s ruling coalition, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk declaring that “democracy won”. The response was more muted from the right-wing opposition and the office of conservative President Karol Nawrocki, who is a Trump ally. 🚨 🇺🇸 Tusk gives Trump some great advice. But will the US president listen? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged the US president to seek compromises after the Republicans' defeat and not to rely on vetoes as his main way of governing. Trump had earlier threatened to become… pic.twitter.com/s3E6G5zIQT — NEXTA (@nexta_tv) November 4, 2026 Tusk addressed the election results on Wednesday afternoon local time at a press conference alongside his Czech counterpart, Andrej Babiš. “Today, democracy won in America,” said a smiling Tusk. “I love democracy; it is a beautiful thing.” “As President Donald Trump himself said just after the election, the Democrats did a good job, and I really could not agree more with him this time,” added Tusk. “I hope that the result will stabilise the situation also in our region.” Although the United States remains Poland’s most important security partner, Tusk’s government – a broad, pro-EU coalition that ranges from left to centre right – has at times had uneasy relations with the Trump administration. It has been critical of Trump’s conciliatory approach towards Russia, his often tough stance on Ukraine, as well as his pursuit of US control over Greenland. Meanwhile, the head of the parliamentary caucus of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, Zbigniew Konwiński, told broadcaster Polsat News that “personally, I was happy with the Democrats’ victory”. “We know how Donald Trump behaves, how volatile he is in his political declarations, how he can sometimes put Ukraine in a more difficult position than Russia, so I would rather look for the positives in what happened,” said Konwiński. “If we look at recent years, the more Democrats, the stronger the Democrats, the better for Poland,” he added. .@Konwinski_PO: Cieszę się z wygranej Demokratów w USA, bo to lepszy scenariusz dla Polski. @marcinfijolek pic.twitter.com/gJ3TnlMn0l — Graffiti_PN (@Graffiti_PN) November 4, 2026 The speaker of Poland’s parliament, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is also the leader of one of KO’s junior coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), has clashed with the US ambassador to Poland twice this year over Czarzasty’s criticism of Trump. Today, Czarzasty shared and commented on a social media post by Trump, published in the wake of the Democrats’ victory, in which the US president showed an image of his signature red cap with the word “VETO” on it. “Where have I heard this before?” wrote Czarzasty, referring to the fact that Nawrocki has vetoed a record number of bills passed by parliament, where Tusk’s coalition has a majority. Czarzasty then went on to list a series of characteristics that he suggested both Trump and Nawrocki share, including “arrogance”, “lack of respect for women”, a “suspicious past”, “transactional exploitation of their position”, and “admiration for politicians with fascist tendencies”. Skąd ja to znam? Arogancja. Buta. Nieuzasadniona pewność siebie. Brak szacunku dla kobiet ( a to popchnę jakąś dwojga nazwisk, a to zakpię prymitywnie). Dziwna przeszłość. Instrumentalne traktowanie dziennikarzy. Pieniądze za spotkania. Transakcyjne wykorzystywanie funkcji.… pic.twitter.com/ryT2BMOZb2 — Włodzimierz Czarzasty 📚📖 (@wlodekczarzasty) November 4, 2026 Nawrocki has closely aligned himself with Trump. During last year’s Polish presidential election campaign, Trump invited Nawrocki for a private meeting at the White House. His then-homeland security secretary, Kristi Noem, visited Poland to endorse Nawrocki. Nawrocki himself has not thus far commented on Tuesday’s midterm election results. However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the president’s International Policy Bureau, did address the issue in a social media post. “As predicted, in the US midterm elections voters decided on change,” wrote Przydacz. “Poland will continue its good cooperation with the US, because it is our ally, and collaboration is in our mutual interest.” Przydacz also added that the results were “a reminder for Tusk” that “no government lasts forever”. In Poland, too, “the moment will come when voters will decide on change – and it might be quite soon”, added Przydacz, in a nod to next year’s Polish parliamentary elections. Zgodnie z przewidywaniami w wyborach połówkowych w USA wyborcy zdecydowali o zmianie. Wcześniej wygrywali Republikanie, dziś Demokraci. Polska będzie kontynuować dobrą współpracę z USA, bo jest to nasz sojusznik, a kooperacja jest w naszym wspólnym interesie. O tym, kto sprawuje… — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) November 4, 2026 Tusk’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, meanwhile, used the US election results to revive his long-running feud with Elon Musk, who is no longer part of the Trump administration but donated enormous amounts of money to support the Republicans ahead of the midterms. Last year, Musk and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticised Sikorski after he suggested that Musk had threatened Ukraine. In a post on his social media platform, X, Musk told Sikorski to “be quiet, small man”. On Wednesday, Tusk shared a screenshot of a tweet he had published last year, after Musk left the Trump administration, in which Sikorski wrote: “See, big man, politics is harder than you thought.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: International Commission of Jurists criticises takeover of Polish constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) has criticised the takeover of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) by a group of government-backed judges. It says that the move “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary”. However, the ICJ, a Swiss-based NGO led by judges, lawyers and academics from around the world, also chastised Poland’s opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, for his role in the crisis surrounding the TK, in particular his refusal to swear in judges elected by parliament. 🚨#Poland’s constitutional crisis must be resolved through the rule of law. The ICJ urges all authorities to respect judicial independence, follow lawful procedures, and comply with European court rulings. 🔗More information: https://t.co/NWmca9mpUx — ICJ (@ICJ_org) November 3, 2026 On Friday, eight judges who were elected to the TK this year by the government’s parliamentary majority effectively took over the tribunal. They announced that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been suspended for failing to properly fulfil their duties. Meanwhile, large numbers of riot police were deployed outside the court, holding back protesters, including opposition politicians, and preventing Święczkowski and Sochański from entering the grounds. Święczkowski denounced the takeover of the court as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the tribunal’s remaining six judges, who, like him, were appointed under the rule of the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which brought the TK under its political influence. Nawrocki has likewise denounced the actions of the government-backed judges. In the early hours of Saturday, he dramatically forced his way into the court, where he clashed physically and verbally with the judges who had taken over the TK. During a visit to the Constitutional Tribunal last night, President Nawrocki clashed physically and verbally with judges involved in an attempt to take control of the court. The president is today seeking talks with political leaders to discuss the crisis https://t.co/7HmBnuIaDG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 31, 2026 In a statement on Tuesday, the ICJ expressed regret that the latest developments have “deepened the crisis over the tribunal”. It called on Polish “state institutions to seek solutions…that comply fully with the rule of law, including the principle of the independence of the judiciary”. The ICJ’s secretary-general, Santiago Canton, noted that Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of the eight TK judges elected by parliament this year. That “violates international standards and is contrary to the interim measures indicated by the European Court of Human Rights”, said Canton. In May, the ECHR issued an interim order for all judges elected by parliament to be allowed to serve on the court. However, that has been ignored by Nawrocki and Święczkowski, who argued that the ECHR does not have the authority to make such a decision. The ICJ also noted that the roots of the crisis at the TK date back a decade, to the time when the PiS government took actions – including unlawfully appointing judges to the tribunal – that rendered the court illegitimate. “At the same time,” continued Canton, “the suspension of the president and vice-president of the tribunal without a fair and appropriate procedure established by law, carried out with the involvement of the police, contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary.” In its statement, the ICJ added that “criminal and disciplinary proceedings must respect all the guarantees of a fair trial and must never be used as a means to change [a court’s] composition”. Later on Tuesday, after the ICJ had issued its statement, the eight government-backed judges held their first general assembly, at which they moved forward with disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski and Sochański. The justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, has also submitted six requests to the TK to lift Święczkowski’s immunity from prosecution so that he can face charges for a range of alleged crimes relating to both his time as chief justice and his previous role as a senior prosecutor under the PiS government. Skierowałem do Trybunału Konstytucyjnego kolejny, szósty już wniosek o uchylenie immunitetu Bogdanowi Święczkowskiemu, dołączając go do pięciu wniosków przekazanych w piątek. Dzisiejsza sprawa dotyczy zakupu systemu szpiegowskiego Hermes w czasie, gdy pełnił funkcję Prokuratora… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 3, 2026 The takeover of the TK has also stirred controversy among Polish legal experts. The issue has even caused an unprecedented split at the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights (HFPC), a well-respected NGO. On Saturday, the HFPC’s management board issued a statement, signed by its president, Maciej Nowicki, saying that it “sees no clear legal basis” for the actions taken on Friday by the government-backed judges to suspend Święczkowski and take control of the tribunal. It warned that the situation “set a dangerous precedent” and “does not contribute to fixing the tribunal”. However, HFPC also made it clear that the crisis at the court dates back a decade and reiterated its view that Nawrocki “has no right to block or invalidate the election [of judges] by parliament”. That statement prompted six of the eight members of HFPC’s council – a separate body from the management board – to resign. Those to depart included a former chief justice of the TK, Andrzej Rzepliński, and a former deputy human rights commissioner, Hanna Machińska. Machińska announced their resignation in a social media post. She said that the reason for her decision had been the management board’s statement, “with which I disagree”. Speaking later to broadcaster TVN, Machińska said that “we believe that the legal basis [for the TK takeover] was clearly defined”. Poland’s government, including Prime Minister Donald Tusk, has also argued that the takeover of the tribunal was necessary to ensure that legally appointed judges can take up their seats and that the court’s legitimacy can be restored. However, on Tuesday evening, Tusk shifted to a more conciliatory tone, offering to hold a one-on-one meeting with Nawrocki to discuss the crisis around the Constitutional Tribunal and “try to find solutions that will protect Poland from any political upheaval”.
