World.title: PM Modi's Sule message to Sharad Pawar; 'internal tussle' in NCP: Is Maharashtra politics heading for another churn?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Is a storm brewing in Maharashtraâs Pawar clan? The family that saw a vertical split in 2023, seems to be at a crossroads again.

"As a member of the Pawar family and their relative, I want to alert Parth Pawar, Jay Pawar and Sunetra

kaki

. They need to understand the political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them": Nephew Rohit Rajendra Pawarâs warning for his â

kaki

â Sunetra Pawar, who is the wife of late

, and her two children.

Sunetra, who is the deputy chief minister in the ruling BJP-led Mahayuti at present, is on the other side of the family divide. She and her sons control the

(NCP), which was originally formed by

in 1999 but was wrested from him by Ajit Pawar in 2023.

So, letâs look at some of the recent developments to analyse if

Rohit Pawar

âs warning has a genuine basis.

Senior NCP leaders met Union home minister

Amit Shah

recently. Some reports suggested that the NCP leaders complained to Amit Shah about the unilateral functioning of party MP Parth Pawar and a lack of proper coordination.



The NCP spokesperson denied this claim and slammed irresponsible media reporting.

6 senior NCP leaders meet Amit Shah to demand finance ministry portfolio in Maharashtra.

NCP chief Sunetra Pawar convened an urgent meeting of the core committee at her official residence, Devgiri. This was the second meeting of the core committee in a week. The first meeting happened after the senior leaders had met Amit Shah.

At the core committee meeting, the party legislators and ministers expressed serious concerns over internal frictions and claimed the party is weakening in the absence of unity.





When Sharad Pawar was hospitalised, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called him in the hospital and requested the veteran politician to prioritise his health and rest. PM Modiâs message to the senior Pawar, "Supriya and we will handle the country. You take care of your health and rest. Let your blessings remain with us," sparked political buzz. And perhaps carried a political undertone about possible churn, amid speculation about Sunetra Pawar and her sons' political future.

PM Modi met Sharad Pawar during the Monsoon session.

Adding fuel to the fire, Union minister and Republican Party of India (Athawale) president Ramdas Athawale claimed that Sule could be considered for a position in the Union cabinet during its next expansion if she joined the ruling NDA.

These four developments, significant in their own ways, collectively point to the flux within the NCP factions after the party was split in 2023.

Ajit Pawar, while he was alive, had managed a firm grip on his faction winning 41 assembly seats in the 2024 assembly elections.

There were even talks of the two factions uniting again. However, his unfortunate death in a helicopter crash in January 2026, suddenly made the NCP vulnerable and the merger talks were put to rest.

Ajitâs wife Sunetra Pawar, who took over the reins of the NCP and also became a minister in the Mahayuti government, tried to fill the vacuum in the party.

Her sons - Parth and Jay Pawar - became an integral part of decision-making.

Senior NCP leaders who had worked with Ajit Pawar over the years were sidelined. This led to heartburn and talks of discontent within the party. It is in this context that the meeting of senior NCP leaders with Amit Shah and the subsequent meeting of the partyâs core committee held by Sunetra Pawar have set tongues wagging.

Rohit Pawar in his warning message had pointed to the âpolitical strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them.â So, is something happening behind the scenes? Is the BJP working to merge the NCP factions to water down the influence of Sunetra and her sons?

Well, there is no definitive answer to these questions.

For the record, the NCP has denied all speculations of any power tussle within the party.

NCP spokesperson Umesh Patil termed the reports suggesting senior party functionaries met Shah, a BJP leader, in New Delhi three days ago without informing Sunetra Pawar as "completely incorrect".

Patil maintained she herself had requested the Union minister to give time to a delegation of senior party leaders. He said Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth had met Shah twice last month when discussions were held on matters related to the party, a BJP ally and constituent of the Mahayuti government in the state.

Sunetra Pawar had then requested Shah to meet senior NCP leaders who had been involved in discussions with BJP leaders when the party joined the NDA, said Patil.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah met Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar in Pune in August.

An appointment with Shah for the delegation was subsequently given, said the spokesperson, adding the NCP's core committee and legislative wing meetings were also scheduled several days in advance.

The official spokesperson also defended the involvement of Parth Pawar in party affairs, saying the Pawar family had dedicated itself to the organisation following the death of former NCP president Ajit Pawar in an air crash in January this year.

"After Ajit Dada's death, Sunetra Pawar (and her sons) Parth and Jay have dedicated themselves to the party," Umesh Patil said.

Now, coming to the second aspect of the developments. It is not for the first time that the Prime Minister has expressed his special bond with Sharad Pawar, despite the two leaders being on opposite sides of the political divide.

In July this year, Sharad Pawar and

Supriya Sule

met the Prime Minister at his office even as opposition MPs protested outside.

The Prime Minister was then seen receiving Pawar at the door of his room. During the meeting Sharad Pawar submitted a memorandum to the Prime Minister listing the issues faced by the farmers in the country and issues related to irrigation.

In February 2025, PM Modi made a gesture of respect by helping 84-year-old Sharad Pawar with his chair on stage and offering him a glass of water.

In August 2023, Sharad Pawar shared the stage with PM Modi in Pune when the Prime Minister was conferred with the Lokmanya Tilak Award.

The move created unease among some members of the opposition INDIA alliance. Uddhav Thackerayâs Shiv Sena (UBT) questioned the optics of the two leaders appearing together, especially when Sharad Pawar was a key leader of the oppositionâs INDIA bloc.

Is BJP courting Sharad Pawar?

Well, the saffron party is obviously not âworkingâ or ânot workingâ to facilitate a '

Hum Saath Saath Hain

' reconciliation moment for the Pawar clan. The real prize of the BJP would be co-opting the political infrastructure of the veteran, who was also known as '

Janata Raja

' (people's king). With decades of work, the influence of Pawar Saheb extends beyond assembly seats to an entrenched network of sugar cooperatives, district banks, local bodies and influential political families across western Maharashtra.

Though the seats and power is not transferable as it is, a working understanding with Sharad Pawar could give the BJP access to this ecosystem without having to build its own grassroots machinery from scratch.

If Sharad Pawar does decide to merge and if Athawaleâs claim turns out to be true, Sule may get an opportunity to be in âpowerâ again.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

There may also be a larger opposition calculation at play. Sharad Pawar was instrumental in stitching together the Maha Vikas Aghadi and managing the competing ambitions of the Congress and Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena.

Any rapprochement with the BJP, even without a formal merger, could weaken this arrangement, complicate seat-sharing and disrupt opposition coordination in Maharashtra. The BJP could gain not just an ally but also greater room to manoeuvre against a much fragmented opposition.

This will also help the BJP in Maharashtra to keep the Eknath Shinde Shiv Sena in check. The recent loss of the ruling Mahayuti in the MLC elections turned into an ugly war of words between the two allies - with the BJP accusing the Shinde Sena of not working for the coalition.

A united NCP on its side may perhaps provide the BJP manoeuvring room against the Shinde Sena in Maharashtra.

World.title: Living near a highway toll plaza? New FASTag rule offers annual pass of up to Rs 3,000, but there's a catch
World.content:
Living within 20 km of a National Highway toll plaza could now mean lower toll expenses for motorists. From November 1, 2026, eligible owners of non-commercial vehicles can obtain a Concessional Local Pass for an annual fee of Rs 1,500 at toll plazas outside municipal or local town limits, and Rs 3,000 at those within these limits, according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

But simply living nearby does not guarantee eligibility. The scheme requires motorists to have a valid and functional

, restricts the pass to a specific toll plaza and excludes highways and expressways operating under a closed user-fee collection system. It also rules out issuance where a service road or alternative road is available to commuters.

The concession comes as India continues to expand its highway network and transition towards

. While FASTag has reduced dependence on cash payments and cut waiting times at toll plazas, operational challenges persist, prompting the government to introduce further changes to the system.



The need for FASTag: India's highway boom and the push for seamless travel

India's National Highway network has expanded significantly over the past decade, making efficient toll collection increasingly important. The network grew from 91,287 km in financial year 2013-14 to 1,46,572 km in March 2026, according to an infrastructure factsheet released by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in August 2026.

India's highway network rapidly grew over the years; so did FASTag

As highways and expressways multiply, ensuring uninterrupted traffic movement has become critical.





Long queues at toll plazas can undermine the very benefits that faster road infrastructure is meant to deliver, particularly during peak travel periods.

Before electronic toll collection became widespread, motorists had to stop at toll booths and pay manually. This often meant long delays, higher fuel consumption from idling vehicles and increased pollution. Cash handling also made toll collection more dependent on physical transactions and records.

The government introduced electronic toll collection to address these bottlenecks.

FASTag uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology. A tag affixed to a vehicle's windscreen communicates with electronic readers at toll plazas, enabling the applicable fee to be deducted from the linked account without requiring motorists to pay cash at the booth. The ministry documented the launch of electronic toll collection on the Delhi-Mumbai corridor on October 31, 2014, describing FASTag as a passive RFID tag.

The system was subsequently rolled out across National Highways. From midnight on February 15-16, 2021, all lanes at National Highway fee plazas were designated as FASTag lanes, according to the ministry's year-end review.

Adoption has grown substantially since then. In its October 27, 2026 announcement on the new local pass, the ministry said more than 13 crore FASTags had been issued across the country. A separate Rajya Sabha reply dated July 22, 2026, stated that approximately 98% of National Highway user-fee collection was being carried out through FASTag.

The transition has created a digital trail of toll transactions, reduced dependence on cash collection and improved transparency and accounting in the process.

The challenges: What FASTag solved, and what it couldn't

FASTag addressed several problems associated with conventional toll collection, particularly queues and delays caused by cash transactions. Automatic deductions helped reduce the time vehicles spent at toll booths.

Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said in June 2023 that waiting time at toll plazas had fallen from 734 seconds in 2014 to 47 seconds in 2023 following the introduction of electronic toll collection.

However, digitising payments has not eliminated operational problems. Motorists continue to encounter issues involving FASTag activation, insufficient account balance, damaged or improperly affixed tags and failed transactions.

In January 2026, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) announced changes to the Know Your Vehicle (KYV) process for car-category FASTags, acknowledging that post-activation verification requirements had caused inconvenience and delays.

The authority also cited complaints involving loosely affixed tags, incorrect issuance and misuse.

Disputes over incorrect deductions have also necessitated dedicated grievance-redressal mechanisms. A July 2026 parliamentary reply listed the National Highway helpline 1033, issuer-bank helplines, the Rajmargyatra app and a dedicated email address as channels through which motorists can lodge complaints.

Another persistent concern involves residents living close to National Highway toll plazas. Even as FASTag has made toll collection quicker, people who regularly cross a nearby plaza on short journeys continue to face recurring toll expenses.

The existing monthly local-pass arrangement was designed to address this problem. In August 2026, NHAI announced that online subscriptions for monthly local passes had been extended to 121 toll plazas through the Rajmargyatra app.

The new annual concession builds on this facility, offering eligible residents another option.

What changes: New FASTag rules, cheaper local passes and the catch

The government has introduced the Concessional Local Pass for eligible owners of non-commercial vehicles residing within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The provision was notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the National Highways Act, 1956.

Eligibility for the annual local pass.

According to the ministry's October 27 announcement, the scheme came into effect on November 1, 2026, with two annual fee structures depending on the location of the toll plaza.

Motorists using fee plazas outside municipal or local town limits will have to pay Rs 1,500 annually. For plazas located within these limits, the annual fee has been fixed at Rs 3,000.

To qualify, applicants must own an eligible non-commercial vehicle, reside within the specified 20-km radius and possess a valid and functional FASTag.

Commercial vehicles are excluded.

Eligible motorists can choose between the existing monthly local pass and the new concessional annual pass. However, the annual pass is valid only at the specific toll plaza for which it is issued. It cannot be used at other plazas along the same highway or elsewhere on the National Highway network.

Why living within 20 km may not be enough

The new rules contain additional exclusions that could deny eligibility even to residents who meet the distance requirement.

The first applies to National Highways and expressways where toll collection operates under a closed user-fee collection system. The ministry has clarified that the concessional local pass will not be available on these stretches.

The second exclusion concerns toll plazas where a service road or alternative road is available for commuters. According to the ministry's announcement, the annual local pass will not be issued in such cases.

In other words, residential proximity alone is not enough. The toll collection system in operation and the availability of alternative roads will also determine eligibility. However, the PIB announcement does not spell out how authorities will assess the availability of alternative roads or resolve disputes involving residential distances and municipal boundaries.

The pass is also restricted to the designated toll plaza and cannot be used at other locations.

The government has retained the power to revise the annual rates, with any revisions taking effect from April 1 each year.

When can motorists obtain the pass, and how is it different from the FASTag Annual Pass?

The ministry has said that the new annual local pass will be available at eligible toll plazas from November 1, 2026. Motorists will also be able to obtain it through the Rajmargyatra app from December 1, 2026.

The new concession should not be confused with the separate FASTag Annual Pass introduced in August 2025.

The latter is available to non-commercial cars, jeeps and vans and follows a different fee structure and coverage arrangement.

For financial year 2026-27, the FASTag Annual Pass costs Rs 3,075 and remains valid for one year or 200 fee-plaza crossings, whichever comes first. It covers approximately 1,150 National Highway and National Expressway fee plazas, according to NHAI's rate-revision announcement.

The distinction is important. While the FASTag Annual Pass offers wider geographical coverage, subject to a limit on crossings, the new Concessional Local Pass is meant specifically for residents living within 20 km of an eligible toll plaza and can be used only at that location.

The actual savings under the new scheme will depend on the existing monthly-pass rate at the particular toll plaza and how frequently a motorist uses it. The two annual-pass arrangements therefore serve different purposes and should be assessed separately.

The future: From FASTag to satellite-based toll collection

Even as FASTag remains the backbone of electronic toll collection on National Highways, the government is exploring technologies that could eventually allow motorists to be charged according to the distance they travel.

One such technology is the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-based toll collection system. It uses satellite-based positioning to determine a vehicle's location and track its movement along designated highways. The applicable user fee can then be calculated according to the distance travelled, rather than relying solely on vehicles passing through conventional toll plazas.

This is fundamentally different from FASTag, which primarily relies on RFID communication between a vehicle-mounted tag and electronic readers at tolling points.

GNSS-based tolling could eventually enable distance-based charging and reduce the need for physical toll barriers.

However, satellite-based toll collection has not replaced FASTag in India. In a July 2026 reply to the Rajya Sabha, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways said expert committees had recommended further deliberations on GPS-based barrier-free tolling, citing concerns over security, privacy, data breaches and operational control.

The response did not specify a nationwide implementation timeline.

Meanwhile, the government is advancing Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection, which allows vehicles to pass through tolling points without stopping at conventional barriers. Unlike GNSS-based tolling, MLFF can continue to use existing FASTag technology.

The system combines Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras, artificial intelligence-based analytics and FASTag-enabled RFID technology to identify vehicles and collect the applicable toll.

The two technologies represent different approaches to seamless toll collection. MLFF aims to eliminate the need to stop at toll barriers while retaining electronic identification and payment mechanisms such as FASTag. GNSS-based tolling, on the other hand, could eventually make distance travelled the basis for calculating toll charges.

For now, FASTag remains central to India's electronic toll collection network, even as the government experiments with barrier-free systems and explores satellite-based alternatives. The new concessional local pass adds another option for residents living near toll plazas, but its restrictions mean that not everyone within the 20-km radius will necessarily benefit.

World.title: '1,800 fake AI books, inflated prices': Periyar library pits CM Vijay against DMK
World.content:
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday accused the previous

government of corruption in the purchase of books for Coimbatore's Periyar Knowledge World, days after allegations emerged that nearly 1,800 fake AI-generated books had been bought at inflated prices.

Vijay credited writer and professor

with exposing the alleged irregularities and said he deserved to be commended.

The controversy has also drawn in the Congress, with state party president Manickam Tagore demanding a comprehensive probe into the purchases. The demand puts the DMK, the Congress's former ally, under pressure to answer allegations of wrongdoing during its tenure.

The DMK, meanwhile, has accused the Vijay government of trying to take credit for a project built under its rule and covering up the name of its 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme at the newly inaugurated centre.



What are the allegations against DMK

The controversy centres on the purchase of books for Periyar Knowledge World, also known as Periyar Arivulagam, a library and science centre in Coimbatore.

Writer Perumal Murugan reportedly flagged alleged irregularities in the procurement process. Citing his allegations, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore claimed that nearly 1,800 fake, AI-generated books from Agalvilakku Pathippagam were purchased at inflated prices.





He also alleged that the books carried fabricated author and publisher details.

In a letter to Vijay, Tagore sought a comprehensive investigation into the alleged multi-crore corruption. He demanded that the disputed books be removed, those responsible identified and arrested, and similar purchases at other state-run libraries examined.

The Congress leader's intervention is politically significant because the allegations concern the previous DMK government, with which the Congress was previously allied.

His demand puts the spotlight on the DMK's record in office even as the party faces attacks from the ruling TVK.

Vijay calls DMK 'fountainhead of corruption'

Vijay seized on the allegations to launch a sharp attack on the DMK, accusing it of turning the institution into what he described as a centre of corruption.

Hitting out at the opposition party, the chief minister called it the "fountainhead of corruption" and alleged that its claims of building the institution after careful scrutiny had been undermined by the book procurement controversy.

"The DMK has engaged in corruption in a slightly different way, turning Coimbatore Periyar Knowledge World itself into a world of corruption," the ruling TVK founder alleged in a statement.

He further claimed that the DMK had a history of corruption, including in the awarding of tenders, and said the party would not be forgiven by future generations of Tamil Nadu.

"That the DMK is a party which built a very huge world of corruption for themselves is getting exposed one after the other," he alleged.

Vijay's remarks came on the day he inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam, which houses a library, a digital library and a planetarium.

Stalin defends the project

The DMK has sought to highlight the institution as a major project completed under its 'Dravidian Model' government.

Party president and former chief minister

visited the centre on Wednesday along with Dravidar Kazhagam president K Veeramani. He expressed satisfaction over its completion and urged students and young people to visit the facility to understand the principles and ideals of the Dravidian movement and Periyar.

Stalin said nearly 99.75% of the work had been completed and suggested that the project could have been abandoned had it been left unfinished.

"Fortunately, the Periyar Knowledge Centre has reached the stage of near completion. Had the project been left halfway, the current govt would have dropped the project and had brought it to a closure. Thankfully, it has escaped that fate," he remarked.

He also expressed hope that other library projects would be completed and opened to the public, saying such institutions could encourage reading and help younger generations understand Tamil Nadu's social reform movements.

Udhayanidhi targets CM Vijay

The DMK's criticism of the Vijay government has also focused on an alleged attempt to remove the previous regime's imprint from the institution.

Leader of Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly

Udhayanidhi Stalin

welcomed the inauguration of the centre but alleged that the name of the DMK government's 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme had been covered up at the premises.

In a post on X, Udhayanidhi said the facility had been built at a cost of Rs 290 crore under the previous government's 'Dravidian Model' and accused the TVK of taking credit for projects initiated by the DMK.

"Those who habitually 'stick their own labels' (take credit) on the schemes of our government have, this time, gone as far as covering up the name 'Naan Mudhalvan' (I am the First/Leader) at the Periyar Knowledge World. In this regimeâled by a 'cheap' chief minister obsessed with sticking his own labelsâwhat is the reason for not only undermining the 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme but also refusing to even accept its name?" he said.

Questioning the alleged move, Udhayanidhi asked whether the word 'Mudhalvan' reminded the ruling party only of the DMK's leadership, or whether it did not want students to become leaders and top achievers.

"Instead of running a 'circus'âby covering up names given by our government, cancelling schemes, and then performing U-turns by 'cancelling the cancellations'âthis 'dummy' chief minister should focus on governing in the interest of the people."

The row has thus developed into a wider political contest over alleged corruption in the previous regime, the ownership of a high-profile public project and the legacy each party wants to claim from it. While the Congress is seeking an investigation into the alleged book purchases, Vijay has used the allegations to target the DMK, which is accusing his government of erasing its contribution to the institution.

World.title: 'Inviting death': Jharkhand tribal leader dies by suicide after emotional Facebook Live post
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Tribal leader Nisha Kumari Bhagat was found dead at her residence in Ranchi on Friday, hours after allegedly going live on Facebook and speaking about threats she faced for raising her voice against the Jharkhand government and alleged land brokers.

Police suspect suicide, though the exact circumstances surrounding her death are yet to be established, according to the news agency PTI.

In the nearly 11-minute video, which was available on her Facebook profile, Bhagat is seen crying and alleging that speaking out against the "Hemant Soren government and its land brokers meant inviting death".

The video ends abruptly, with the camera apparently getting blocked by a green object.



Ranchi City Superintendent of Police Paras Rana told PTI that Bhagat's body was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a room at her house. Her body has been sent to the Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) for a post-mortem examination.

"Prima facie, it appears that she died by suicide after going live on social media. The exact reason behind the incident is yet to be ascertained," another police official said, adding that a detailed investigation has been launched.





Leader of the opposition Babulal Marandi expressed grief over Bhagat's death and alleged that she had been harassed for standing up for tribal rights.

Describing her as a young tribal leader who fought for her community, Marandi claimed that Bhagat had held chief minister Hemant Soren, the officer-in-charge of Pithoria police station and Ajay Tirkey responsible for her death in her video.

"She held chief minister Hemant Soren, the Pithoria police station in-charge, and Ajay Tirkey responsible for this," he claimed in a social media post.

Marandi said it was "shameful and unfortunate" that a young woman who raised her voice for tribal rights was allegedly harassed to such an extent that she took her own life.

"Chief minister Hemant Soren should immediately resign from his post," he added.

The BJP leader also demanded the immediate arrest of those named by Bhagat and called for an impartial investigation into the incident.

World.title: Pakistan says willing to issue visa to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann for visit
World.content:
Pakistan on Friday (November 6, 2026) said it would consider issuing a visa to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann if the Indian politician wished to visit the country.

Pakistan Foreign Office Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing in response to a question about the possible visit of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader.

The Pakistani government would “consider issuing him a visa if he wished to visit the country”, Mr. Khan said, clarifying that whether the Indian government permits Mr. Mann to travel to Pakistan was an entirely separate matter.

On October 23, Mr. Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27.

However, he questioned whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan. “Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he had said.

Mr. Mann had also expressed his desire that all legislators of the Punjab Legislative Assembly visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if the Kartarpur Corridor reopened.

The corridor, which connects Dera Baba Nanak in India's Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims travelling to the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.

It allows Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without requiring a visa for Pakistan, subject to the applicable arrangements.

The corridor has remained closed to pilgrim movement from the Indian side since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack.

Pakistan said it remained ready to facilitate pilgrims once the restrictions were lifted.

The foreign office spokesperson said Pakistan welcomes pilgrims of all faiths and remains committed to facilitating visits to religious sites.

He said the country issued more than 9,000 visas to Indian religious pilgrims in 2025, including Sikh and Hindu pilgrims, and issued over 4,000 additional visas to Sikh pilgrims during the first half of this year.

“Pakistan looks forward to welcoming a large number of Sikh pilgrims at Nankana Sahib later this month to mark the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji,” Mr. Khan said.

The spokesperson said Pakistan established the Kartarpur Corridor as a special initiative to facilitate Sikh pilgrims, enabling more than 5,000 pilgrims to visit the shrine daily and return on the same day.

Mr. Khan said the 1974 Protocol on Visits to Religious Shrines between Pakistan and India provided a framework for facilitating religious pilgrimages between the two countries.

He also said Pakistan was taking steps to preserve and protect Buddhist heritage sites, including those in Taxila and Takht-i-Bahi, and had established a special task force for the purpose.

World.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
World.content:
Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people.

The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects. The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement.

He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually. Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns.

Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights. He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others.

The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess.

The additional revenue, he said, would be used to strengthen education and healthcare, improve road infrastructure, generate employment and ensure timely payment of financial benefits to government employees.

Congratulating the State’s nearly 75 lakh residents, Mr. Sukhu said protecting its resources and making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant remained a top priority for his government.

World.title: A missing persons complaint that unravelled Bengaluru’s seven murders
World.content:
It was not until the mother of Nalini, one of the seven allegedly killed by cab driver-turned-YouTuber Indushekhar, lodged a missing person complaint that the police found the first clue to the murders. While the murders allegedly took place between October 16 and October 31, the last two bodies were disposed of on November 1 or 2.

Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered. Sunita and Indushekhar had been married for 20 years, and an officer said they had been having regular arguments throughout their marriage. Sunita worked as a typist for an advocate, while Indushekhar was a cab driver. Their respective jobs were often a point of contention between them.

“Indushekhar claimed that he was verbally abused and harassed by his wife and her family, while her brothers also encouraged her to fight with him,” a senior officer said.

Prima facie, the police have found that Indushekhar had been planning the murders for over a year. The growing friction and pent-up anger allegedly came to a head following a recent meeting.

“The accused claimed that Roopavathi had visited his house on October 14, when she and Sunita reportedly verbally abused him. This became a trigger point, and he wanted to eliminate them,” the officer said.

According to the police, Sunita and Roopavathi were murdered first. Subsequently, the accused invited Sunita’s younger brother Shivakumar and his wife Divya to his house on the pretext of hosting a dinner party. The couple were then killed along with their seven-year-old son Puneeth. On October 30, the accused allegedly invited Shankar, another brother of Sunita, and his wife Nalini, and allegedly murdered them.

Missing persons complaint

On November 3, Tungamma, Nalini’s mother, approached the police, stating that her daughter’s phone was switched off and that their house in Srirampura was also locked. Tungamma subsequently went to Indushekar’s house to check on him but found that his house was locked as well.

Sensing that something was amiss, she contacted Divya’s mother Kalavathi, who also said that her daughter and son-in-law were missing. Tungamma then lodged a missing person complaint with the Srirampura police.

Karthik, a shopkeeper near Indushekhar’s house, said a police team visited the house on November 3 and made inquiries about Indushekhar among the neighbourhood residents. “They also came the next day and questioned people because Indushekhar’s house was locked,” he said.

A senior officer told The Hindu that the police grew suspicious and began tracking Indushekhar. Several technical inputs indicated that he was on the move. “Finally, when he was in the city, we tracked him and intercepted his car,” he said.

Allegations

High drama unfolded near the Rajajinagar police station on Friday as Nalini’s family accused the police of delaying action on their complaint. “We approached the police on November 1 itself, but they did not register our complaint. Only after two days did they take it up,” a family member alleged.

Bengaluru City Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh refuted the allegations and said that action would be taken against the officers if any lapses were found.

Murder weapon

While the accused has claimed that he murdered the victims using a grinder stone, the police are yet to ascertain the exact modus operandi. “Only when the bodies are found can we verify the cause of death. We have seized the suspected weapon,” the officer said.

Seemant Kumar Singh, Bengaluru Police Commissioner, said, “As this is a serious case, we will gather all the evidence and present it before a fast-track court. We have deputed senior officers to closely monitor the investigation and ensure that all necessary evidence is collected.”

World.title: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff after GOP’s midterm defeat
World.content:
President Donald Trump said Friday (November 6, 2026) that Stephen Miller was replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, mere days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.

On his social media site, Mr. Trump praised Ms. Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation. Ms. Wiles also released a social media statement on Friday (November 6, 2026).

"Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honour of a lifetime. I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together, from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” Wiles said in a social media post shortly after Trump’s announcement. She added that her commitment to “the President and the mission” will not change.

Mr. Miller, long a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a key architect of the administration’s hard-line immigration policies.

Ms. Wiles, the steely political operator and longtime adviser to Mr. Trump, was the first woman to ever serve in that post.

Ms. Wiles' departure comes almost immediately after the GOP's midterm thrashing on Tuesday (November 3, 2026). She will be replaced by Stephen Miller, a longtime trusted aide to Mr. Trump.

The departure also came months after Ms. Wiles indicated she no longer showed evidence of breast cancer after she underwent months of treatment for the disease, a diagnosis she went public with in March 2026.

Ms. Wiles is the longest-serving White House chief of staff for Mr. Trump, who cycled through four of them during his first four-year term.

Mr. Miller is one of Mr. Trump’s closest and longest-serving advisers, having jumped on board during his long-shot 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter. He currently serves as White House deputy chief of staff, and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, Mr. Miller is most closely aligned with Mr. Trump’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration.

Mr. Miller is a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

World.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
World.content:
The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest.

“Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed.

According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation.

The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants.

It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC).

Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. Noting that so far only around 40 gram sabhas had become functional to commence the process of inviting claims, the government gave a last opportunity of 30 days to the State government to complete the formation of the remaining gram sabhas. The process of adjudication of the claims would be concluded within a period of five months from the date of constitution of the gram sabhas.

The court further constituted a ‘special committee’ chaired by former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai to supervise the expeditious disposal of claims and scrutinise the orders passed by the competent authorities under the 2006 Act.

The Supreme Court directed the CEC to furnish an opinion regarding the government’s view that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. This is significant for the biosphere. Presently, 3,637.83.2 hectares of the 5,072.64.3 hectares of forest land is under silk cotton cultivation.

Giving a prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton, the court said “what emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop”.

“The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce. If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change… The fact that large swathes of forest are being destroyed under the garb of cultivation of silk cotton,” the court observed.

Separately, the court directed the CEC to examine the National Highway Authority of India’s proposal relating to NH-744, including the proposed Puliara–Edamon tunnel section, which requires permission for diversion of a limited extent of reserved forest land in the biosphere.

World.title: Did all the murders happen in the small house on the terrace?
World.content:
Indushekhar lived with his wife Sunita and daughter in a small house, barely 500 sq. ft, on the terrace of a two-storey building, nestled among several commercial establishments, 50 metres from the famous Bhashyam Circle, Rajajinagar.

The building has commercial establishments on the ground floor, including a watch repair shop, a tea stall and a small condiments shop. The entire first floor was occupied by a small political party. Indushekar’s house is on the second floor, which also serves as the terrace.

Household appliances were crammed into the space, with several other household items scattered around. A board on the wall read, “Police Voice”.

Reaching the second floor itself through a very narrow staircase itself is a task. This has raised questions as to whether all seven murders were committed here in the house. However, the accused claimed that the murders took place inside his house. The location has raised several questions, as the building has very little space to move around.

However, the police investigation indicates a high probability that the murders took place there. “He may have cleaned the entire scene, but residues were found at the crime scene,” the officer said.

How did he transport the bodies down to the road into his car is a question that has left the police puzzled. He couldn’t have done it alone and that is where police suspect the role of the minor daughter. Given the lane mostly has commercial establishments, the police suspect that he could have shifted the bodies only during night time.

World.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
World.content:
From bamboo bus shelters that offer shade and cooling to commuters, to the reclamation of waste dumps and the plugging of water supply leaks, Telangana is drawing up a broad plan to make its cities more resilient to climate change. The measures, backed by new urban policies and a project pipeline worth about ₹20,000 crore, are part of the State’s long-term Telangana Rising 2047 vision.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), said Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi said. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

Heatwaves and erratic rainfall are becoming increasingly evident across Telangana, though their impact varies by region. The government says this calls for location-specific interventions based on climate data. The challenge is significant: the State’s cities account for net emissions of about 66.56 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, with buildings, transport, wastewater, waste management and urban expansion among the major contributors.

Some interventions are already under way. Bamboo misting bus shelters in Khammam use a low-carbon building material while providing relief to commuters. Bio-mining of legacy waste dumps is aimed at reducing methane emissions and reclaiming land. The government is also working to reduce non-revenue water through leak detection, pipeline renewal and digital monitoring, besides expanding underground sewerage networks and reusing treated wastewater.

The bio-mining programme has helped avoid an estimated 5.6 lakh tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions and reclaimed about 418 acres for productive urban use, Ms. Sreedevi said.

To coordinate these efforts, a State Climate Centre for Cities has been established at the office of the Commissioner and Director of Municipal Administration. It will coordinate city-level climate action plans, maintain a climate data repository and provide technical support to municipalities.

Dedicated Climate Change Cells, city-specific action plans and nine Climate Action Officers are also planned for municipal corporations outside Hyderabad: Greater Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Ramagundam, Nalgonda, Mancherial, Mahabubnagar and Kothagudem.

The Telangana Urban Climate Atlas, a climate intelligence platform, has been set up to help municipalities identify vulnerable zones, prioritise investments and track climate indicators. Capacity-building programmes have been conducted for representatives of 113 ULBs to strengthen preparedness and project planning.

A key intervention is the Cool Roof Policy, effective from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2028. It targets 300 sq km of cool roofs, including 200 sq km in the Hyderabad metropolitan region and 100 sq km in other urban local bodies. Cool roofs reflect about 80% of incoming sunlight, against 20% for conventional roofs. They can lower indoor temperatures by 2.1°C to 4.3°C and reduce air-conditioning costs by up to 20%. Full implementation is expected to save nearly 600 million units of electricity annually and generate a one-time carbon offset of about 30 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

The policy covers government and commercial buildings and residential properties on plots of 600 square yards and above. Compliance has been integrated into the ‘Build Now’ building approval system and linked to occupancy certification. The government has also set a three-year target for retrofitting all non-residential buildings.

Urban heat mitigation proposals for Ramagundam and Adilabad are being prepared under UCF financing. Both cities are among the 29 ULBs covered by the World Bank-supported Telangana Urban Transformation and Jobs Programme, which includes urban greening, shaded public spaces and cool-roof measures.

Wastewater treatment remains a major challenge. Telangana’s urban areas generate nearly 2,750 million litres of sewage a day, while 59 operational sewage treatment plants have a combined capacity of about 1,950 MLD. Hyderabad accounts for most of the installed capacity, leaving smaller and medium-sized towns with a substantial treatment gap.

The State aims to treat 80% of sewage and reuse 20% of treated water by 2030. The targets rise to 90% treatment and 50% reuse by 2035, and 100% for both by 2047. Industries with high pollution loads and bulk water users consuming more than 5,000 litres a day will be required to shift to treated wastewater in phases by 2035.

Other measures include drinking-water kiosks planned with the Panchayati Raj department, shaded structures at major traffic junctions and cooling centres at bus stations, markets, public buildings and places of worship. Community drinking-water and buttermilk distribution points are also being promoted during summer.

Long-term plans include avenue plantations, cool pavements, shaded seating and integrated stormwater systems in road projects. Municipalities have been asked to promote rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge through pits, trenches, permeable pavements and connected drains. Future road designs will prioritise unobstructed footpaths, cycle tracks on wider roads, barrier-free access, better bus stops, street lighting and underground utility corridors to avoid repeated road cutting.

World.title: Karnataka CM ridicules BJP leaders for trying to take credit for PM’s visit
World.content:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take credit for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bengaluru on November 13 to inaugurate the metro Pink Line, even though he was arriving on the official invitation of the State government.

Without taking the name of BJP MP Tejasvi Surya, the Chief Minister alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take publicity by claiming that they were responsible for the Prime Minsiter’s proposed visit.

Speaking to media persons in Kanakapura, he wondered why the BJP leaders were tying to take publicity for this event though they had nothing to do with it.

“We are developing metro network by borrowing money. I will present some of these issues before the Prime Minister on November 13,” he said.

World.title: Petrol price down by Rs6.59 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 in fifth straight reduction
World.content:
The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378.

The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Trump promotes Stephen Miller to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
World.content:
US President Donald Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller on Friday, elevating the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies to run the White House after Republicans lost control of Congress in this week’s midterm elections.

The shake-up puts a longtime Trump loyalist and firebrand policy adviser in charge of steering Trump’s agenda as the president prepares to confront a Democratic-led House of Representatives and Senate, and an expected wave of congressional investigations.

White House officials told Reuters that Miller’s selection suggests Trump will take an aggressive approach to domestic policy and politics.

Miller is a veteran of Trump’s first term in office in 2017-2021. Since Trump’s return to the White House in 2025, Miller has officially been deputy chief of staff under Wiles, but he wielded outsize influence across much of Trump’s domestic agenda and has had the ear of the president.

He is perhaps best known for driving Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests a day. In pursuit of that target, federal immigration agents expanded their list of targets to include migrants who had been living in the US for decades.

In a social media post, Trump called Miller “one of my most trusted advisers,” and he praised Wiles for doing “an outstanding job”.

Trump said the change would take effect on Monday.

Wiles, who submitted her resignation on Thursday night, will move to Trump’s political operation, according to a White House official.

Wiles, 69, who announced recently that she had been given the all-clear from breast cancer, said in a statement on X that Friday would be her last day in her job.

“Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime,” she wrote.

“I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.”

Trump had been displeased with his political and communications operations in the run-up to Tuesday’s election as his public approval ratings fell near record lows.

This week, he said the White House needed to be “more aggressive” as Democrats retake congressional power, according to a person briefed on the matter.

Wiles’ allies in the White House began sharing concerns with others on Wednesday about her potential replacement, the person said.

“He’s rewarding those most loyal to him. He’s not changing course,” said another White House official.

World.title: Banks, utilities among services put on alert against AI-enabled cyberthreats
World.content:
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (NCERT) has warned of an increased use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated bots to carry out credential-based and coordinated cyberattacks, noting that critical infrastructure and financial services are at particular risk.

NCERT, in an advisory dated Nov 5, said an increase in “AI, automated bots, botnets and agentic tools to automate reconnaissance, identify vulnerabilities, conduct credential-based attacks and launch coordinated cyberattacks” has been observed recently.

“These capabilities may help threat actors and sophisticated cybercriminal groups to broaden the scale, speed and sophistication of their operations,” it added.

“This advisory is relevant to all sectors/organizations. However, two sectors require particular attention,” it stressed, referring to financial services, along with operational technology (OT) and critical infrastructure.

It warned banks that they could face attacks targeting core banking systems, digital banking platforms, payment systems and customer-facing applications, with potential scenarios including the disruption of online services, automated credential attacks, and manipulation of displayed account balances.

In terms of critical infrastructure, NCERT warned: “Third-party service providers, connected IoT (internet of things) devices, vulnerabilities in industrial control systems and insecure remote access may expose oil and gas facilities, water utilities, power generation and distribution networks, manufacturing, transportation and other essential services.

“A compromise could disrupt physical processes and critical services,” it added.

NCERT cited recent incidents in Europe, where supermarket refrigerators and freezers were targeted in cyberattacks, as examples of the “physical and commercial consequences of attacks against connected operational systems”.

“However, AI involvement in said incidents has not been confirmed yet,” it added.

Threat indicators

The advisory listed anomalies which may indicate a potential cyberattack targeting financial institutions, such as frequent automated login attempts, repeated authentication failures, and unusual application programming interface (API) requests.

Abnormal transaction patterns, differences between core banking records and the displayed account balance, and unauthorised payment access were other indicators.

For critical infrastructure, NCERT said changes to refinery, pipeline, grid, power generation or distribution parameters could indicate an attack, as could unexpected changes to pressure, temperature, cooling or heating control settings.

Unexpected remote access sessions or changes to IoT/OT device configurations could also point towards a cyberattack.

Recommendations

NCERT recommended that financial institutions check their core banking security, APIs, third-party integrations, payment gateways and digital banking applications.

It further urged them to use multi-factor authentication and protection against automated login attempts, while enforcing integrity checks between consumer-facing applications and core banking records.

The team also suggested monitoring bot-driven attempts, potential service disruption and abnormal API activity.

For utility providers, NCERT’s advice was to limit direct internet exposure and remote access and check the security of IoT assets and industrial control systems.

“Enforce OT/IT network segmentation and continuously monitor access to operational systems,” it recommended. “Keep applying security updates and maintain backup operating procedures for essential processes.”

NCERT also urged all organisations to check their preparedness against bot-driven AI cyberattacks, maintain incident logs and enhance arrangements for incident response, business continuity and security monitoring.

World.title: CDF Munir, Sudan's interior minister discuss avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation: ISPR
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Sudan’s Interior Minister Lieutenant General (Police) Babiker Samra Mustafa Ali on Friday discussed avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation between their countries.

Lt Gen Ali called on CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi during his visit to Pakistan, according to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and global security dynamics and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation were discussed,” the statement said.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening relations between the two countries, particularly in the fields of security, counterterrorism and institutional cooperation.”

The visiting dignitary “appreciated Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace and stability and acknowledged the longstanding fraternal ties between Pakistan and Sudan”, according to ISPR.

CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s desire to “further deepen bilateral engagement with Sudan and underscored the importance of close cooperation in addressing shared security challenges”.

Earlier in the day, Ali called on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

DPM Dar “reaffirmed Pakistan’s steadfast support for Sudan’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity”, the Foreign Office said.

He underscored the importance Pakistan attached to its relations with Sudan and its commitment to further strengthening the brotherly ties between the two countries.

Meanwhile, the Sudanese minister expressed his “appreciation for Pakistan’s support and continued solidarity with Sudan”.

“He highlighted the strength of brotherly relations between the two nations and underscored Sudan’s desire to further deepen cooperation across areas of mutual interest.”

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also attended the meeting.

Meeting with PM Shehbaz

On Thursday, a delegation led by Lt Gen Ali had met PM Shehbaz Sharif at the PM House.

The premier affirmed that Pakistan attaches “great importance to its longstanding and fraternal relations” with Khartoum, the PM’s Office (PMO) said.

“We want Sudan to emerge from its current crisis as a peaceful, stable, and prosperous country,” he was quoted as saying, expressing Pakistan’s desire to strengthen trade and investment ties with the North African country.

“There are vast opportunities for bilateral cooperation in sectors such as agriculture, defence, education, and others,” the prime minister added.

The Sudanese minister expressed gratitude to the premier for the humanitarian and medical assistance provided by the Pakistani government and people during difficult times, according to PMO.

He also commended Pakistan’s support on international forums regarding efforts to restore peace and security in Sudan.

Sudan remains the ​world’s largest displacement crisis more than three years after war broke out in 2023, when the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces clashed over issues including how to ​integrate their forces in a planned transition to civilian rule.

Around 8.6 million ​people remain displaced within the country, while more than 4.6m have fled across borders. ‌More ⁠than 5.2m people have also returned to their areas of origin, often finding homes, infrastructure and basic services destroyed.

World.title: Bilawal urges federal govt to engage all political forces instead of ‘fighting everyone’
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the PML-N-led federal government to engage all political and social stakeholders rather than “fighting everyone”.

Responding to a query at a ceremony in Larkana, the PPP chairman highlighted that people around the world were bearing the economic burden of the US-Israeli war on Iran.

“This is a backbreaking burden. We have not seen this phenomenon in the past,” the former foreign minister said, adding that even if the war ended tomorrow, its economic consequences were unlikely to end soon.

Bilawal contended that regardless of whether a country was directly involved in the war or not, supporting its people had become the biggest test for many governments.

“I advise the federal government that this is the time to engage with the political, social and provincial stakeholders rather than fighting everyone,” he remarked.

The PPP chairman further stressed that the coalition government’s focus should be on the economic difficulties faced by the people, not on their “differences with each other”.

“If the federal government and the relevant stakeholders focus on the problems faced by the people, only then we can emerge successful in this test, no matter how long it goes on for,” he said, referring to the economic consequences of the Middle East conflict.

However, Bilawal cautioned that if “we continue to fight among ourselves” and keep fighting with PTI and Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman — alongside the fight against terrorists, India, Afghanistan and others — then they might end up remaining engaged in that.

“Our priority should be the problems faced by the people,” he stressed.

Bilawal’s remarks follow exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between Fazl and federal ministers, after the JUI-F chief accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He has accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Meanwhile, the PTI-led opposition and the Centre have been at odds over various issues, particularly the counterterrorism policy.

On Oct 16, without naming anyone, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship”.

The next day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry rebuked Fazl directly, who later clarified his criticism was aimed at policies, not state institutions.

The row played out in the Parliament as well, where Fazl questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at a meeting of the Makkah pact countries and Iran in Tehran.

In his response the next day, the interior minister explained his participation and went on to assail the JUI-F for “continuously crossing the line” and accused it of “extracting wealth from the state”.

Bilawal defends imposition of governor’s rule in KP

In his remarks, the PPP chairman rejected the accusations that counterterrorism was a pretence to dismiss the elected PTI government in KP by imposing the emergency and governor’s rule.

“This claim is not based on facts,” he asserted.

“The PPP maintains that the democratically elected governments are always in a better position to deal with all matters, including terrorism,” Bilawal said.

However, he noted, the recent surge in terrorist activities and the number of fatalities had never been witnessed since around 2007-2008.

“After the change of the government in Afghanistan, the terrorists’ threats to Pakistan have increased. This is a ground reality,” the ex-foreign minister said.

Bilawal contended that during PTI’s rule in KP, individuals imprisoned on charges of terrorism had been released.

He further said Sohail Afridi — the chief minister who has been rendered non-functional due to governor’s rule — had failed to combat terrorism and protect the people of his province, thereby leaving no constitutional or legal reasons for the president to reject the summary for emergency.

Thanking the federal government for engaging with the PTI on his party’s recommendation, the PPP chairman recalled the breakdown of the talks between the opposition and the government, attributing their failure to the KP CM.

“Even the opposition leaders who were negotiating with us know that they cannot blame anyone, including the prime minister, for this move,” Bilawal said.

“Even today, I invite the PTI to negotiate and request the government to engage with them. Do not close the door for talks,” he urged, stating that if a consensus is reached on countering terrorism, he would be the first person calling to end the governor’s rule.

The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were later endorsed by the Parliament amid protests by the opposition.

Electoral reforms ‘fundamental issue’

On electoral reforms, the PPP chairman termed it a “fundamental issue” and called the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER) a primary platform to address the concerns.

Addressing political parties that have alleged rigging in various elections, including PTI, Bilawal maintained that the reforms committee could be the starting point to resolve such grievances.

Noting that opposition leaders in both the National Assembly and Senate had been empowered by PTI founder Imran Khan to make decisions regarding dialogue, Bilawal reiterated his call for them to exercise their authority by “unconditionally” naming their representatives for the PCER.

“If the opposition has some other perspective, the PPP is ready to engage with them or with the government, too,” he said, emphasising that all the political parties should become part of this committee for strengthening democracy in Pakistan.

“After all the efforts, if PTI does not take part in this committee, then the people of Pakistan should not pay heed to their cries against electoral rigging,” he remarked.

While reaffirming his party’s call for empowering the Parliament, the PPP chairman stressed that the opposition bore an equal responsibility in achieving this, and said it had an equal role in weakening the Parliament along with the government.

“If the opposition boycotts committee proceedings, then how can it criticise that the Parliament is frail?”

Bilawal added, “We have to begin from somewhere; that’s why I invite the opposition to participate in the electoral reforms committee.”

World.title: Activists breach Microsoft data centre construction site as protests spread in Europe
World.content:
Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday at the start of two days of rallies that are part of a growing global backlash over the rapid build-out of computing power needed for AI.

Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the “Stop Dirty Data Centres” coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction.

In Amsterdam on Friday, more than 100 activists gathered at the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre, marching arm in arm before breaking into the site, climbing cranes, hanging balloons and dancing while police stood by. Some carried placards with messages reading: “Screw your data centre”.

“These data centres are destroying our world. It’s becoming uninhabitable because of all the resources they consume. That’s why we’re here today,” protester Sam van der Beek said.

Site owner Pure Data Centres, which plans to invest more than $1 billion and is backed by Brookfield-owned Oaktree, said it was committed to engagement with local stakeholders.

“We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have,” it said.

Other planned actions include a march in Dublin, a protest outside the parliament building in Warsaw, and a demonstration against a different Microsoft data centre in Denmark.

Microsoft said it understood that people had strong feelings about the project and respected their right to express them peacefully but did not condone any unlawful actions.

Concern over AI drives stock market rout

Pushback is growing from Spain to India and the United States, where technology stocks fell sharply on Thursday over concern that Democratic control of Congress could mean tougher regulation curtails the AI boom.

Campaigners say data centres pressure electricity and water supplies, compete with housing and other businesses for scarce resources and threaten climate goals. They also point to job losses and potential risks to personal and national security from private and big tech concentrating power.

Technology companies argue that data centres are essential to meeting global demand for artificial intelligence and cloud computing and provide critical infrastructure for businesses, governments and consumers.

Stop Dirty Data Centres says it is not anti-progress or calling for existing data centres to be closed but that major construction should be halted until governments establish clearer rules.

Europe is divided between its ambition to catch up with the US and Asia on AI to boost productivity and to maintain what are generally more stringent controls and public protections.

Speaking to Reuters on Thursday, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Europe needed more data centres to power AI development, though she added it needed to be done with care.

“AI, of course, is a super important technology and we need to have our own capacity,” Virkkunen said, pointing to investments being made in chip-making capacity, AI startups and a plan to build out gigafactories around the region.

However, she added, “It’s very important for citizens that they can trust that their energy bills are not skyrocketing and there are no electricity blackouts because of data centres, or they are not destroying the environment with these projects.”

A Google project in Finland faces a criminal probe over land clearances, Italy and Portugal are tightening environmental regulation for data centres, and Microsoft pulled out of a UK data centre project that was hit by infrastructure delays.

The Netherlands has about 200 data centres either planned, under construction or in operation.

World.title: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday said that the secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, is expected to assume his responsibilities in Riyadh soon.

Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on Aug 7, empowers the three members to consider an armed attack on one member an attack on all.

Speaking at the FO’s weekly press briefing on Friday, Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan further said that the three members would jointly decide on convening a meeting of their alliance.

The Makkah Defence Alliance has garnered particular attention as Saudi Arabia faces attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a deadly strike that closed Riyadh’s international airport for two weeks last month.

Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said in mid-October.

However, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) director general also clarified that all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance were “absolutely clear […] that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”.

The DG ISPR added: “Pakistan is giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is at play, has already been actualised and we will take all necessary steps for the security and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Haramain Sharifain (The Two Holy Mosques).”

Islamabad has two defence pacts with Riyadh aimed at collective deterrence — the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye.

On Thursday, the Turkish parliament approved a bill ratifying the Makkah pact, paving the way for the trilateral security pact to come into force.

On its part, FO said late last month that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already completed the ratification processes, noting that each country followed its own constitutional and legal procedures to approve and ratify international agreements.

Pakistan, others actively making efforts for peace in Middle East

In his briefing, Khan also touched upon the crisis in the Gulf, saying that Pakistan would continue its efforts to facilitate dialogue in the conflict involving Iran and the United States.

He said Islamabad had brought the two parties under one roof despite them having remained out of contact for decades and supported a peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy.

Khan cited the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the warring parties on June 18 as “a testament to Pakistan’s commitment to […] promoting peace and stability in our region”. He added that Pakistan, Qatar and other countries were actively contributing to mediation efforts.

The FO official emphasised that peace in the region must be established through “political dialogue and diplomacy” rather than war.

While acknowledging that the process of negotiations could be time-consuming, Khan asserted, “I believe that peace will eventually prevail and that countries will be able to resolve these matters peacefully.”

Elaborating further, the FO spokesperson said Israel was playing the role of a “spoiler” in the ongoing US-Iran war.

Criticising Israel’s expansionist policies, he said peace in the region was not in Israel’s interest and that its expansionist ambitions were among the major causes of the current regional crisis.

These ambitions were not limited to Iran, he said, adding that Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and other countries in the region were also affected by Israel’s expansionist designs.
